title: Paying for the lifts
line: The lower bound, where most of the code lives
summary: Theorem C: the lattice can’t be too small. This is where Galois representations, Selmer groups and L-values come in.
story: Every lift has a price. Theorem C (`Determinant/Twist/LongForms`) is the lower half of the main inequality: covolume and twice the index together are at least about the main amount. Proving it is where most of the code lives.

`Determinant` chooses a twist for each prime, computes norms of theta lifts and of whole chains, and uses an exchange identity of Siegel–Weil type. `OneLift` studies a single lift: its volume and height, Hecke L-values as squared norms and their valuations, and “false lifts”.

`Congruences` controls the denominators. It uses Galois representations, anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups, the local loss, and the lifting of crystalline classes (p-adic Hodge theory). `Appendix` supplies discrete series with a large gap. This is the “everything” behind the remark that “the Riemann Hypothesis is proved by using everything”.

modules.title: The ratio of twisted to untwisted Hecke L-values, main pairs and regular families of twists
modules.note:
Consider a pair `(ν, z)`, a tame character `ϑ` with set of places `Q` and a sign `s = ±1` (by
default `1`). For these, `New.Data.CriticalPair.ratio` is the quotient
`|L(z, (ν ϑ^s)⁻¹)| / |L(z, ν⁻¹)|`, as a complex number. The remaining definitions record what the
congruence arguments need to know about a family of twists `θ ι`. The family has one twist for each
prime `ℓ` and isomorphism `ι : ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_ℓ` (`New.PrimePadicIso`).

## Main definitions

* `New.Data.goodLift`: the lift `New.Data.singleLift` restricted to good forms, whose range is the
  space of lifts.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.IsRamified`, `New.Data.CriticalPair.IsMainPair`: ramified pairs and main
  pairs.
* `New.Data.denominatorBudget`: the bound for the sums over primes of the logarithmic denominator
  bounds.
* `New.Data.IsNegligible`: numbers `e ℓ` with `∑ e ℓ log ℓ ≤ x ^ C` over every finite set of
  primes.
* `New.Data.HasSmallRatios`: families of twists `θ ι` with modulus prime to `ℓ` whose powers have
  ratios of L-values of small height.
* `New.Data.IsRegularFamily`: regular families, that is, families with small ratios for whose powers
  the projections to the lifts have small denominators.

Notions from other files:
* `New.AutChar.L`: The partial Hecke L-function of the character x ↦ ν(x/x̄) of E.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair`: An integer 1 ≤ z ≤ `D.t` and a character ν of U(1)(𝔸) of weight −c, with
  z ≤ c(v) ≤ 4 `D.b` at every infinite place v and tame part ψ supported on the chosen places.
* `New.Data.Twist`, `New.Data.MFoldTwist`: A tame character whose tame part ψ_w (for an m-fold
  twist: each ψ_wⁿ, 1 ≤ n ≤ m) is non-trivial at every place w of its finite set Q.
* `New.HeightLe`: A bound for the height of a family of complex numbers indexed by the ι.

modules.title: Theorem C: integral forms are long
modules.note:
The main result `New.Data.integral_forms_long` bounds from below the covolume plus twice the index
of a family of target forms that spans almost all of the target. The target forms are a twisted
lattice, and the bound follows from `New.TwistedLattice.covolume_add_index_nonneg` with four inputs:
auxiliary forms that complete a family to a basis, a family of twists `ξ_ι`, the injectivity of the
lifts `Θ_ξ`, and the height of `Z(1) / Z(ξ_ι)`.

In comments, `d` is the dimension `D.targetDim` of the target `D.targetForms`, the space of good
forms on `Y₀ = D.spaceY 0`. The letters `x, x₁, b, a, m, k, t, f` are the numbers `D.x`, `D.x₁`, …
of the data `D`; inequalities between them come from `New.Data.le_of_hasLogBound`.

Notions from other files:
* `D.targetLattice`: the target forms as a twisted lattice, with the lifts `Θ_ξ = D.Θ ξ` indexed by
  the `m`-fold twists `ξ`; the modulus `Q(ξ)` has norm `ξ.normQ`.
* `D.chainDeterminant ξ` is `Z(ξ) = det (Θ_ξ* Θ_ξ)`, and `D.liftDeterminant ξ j` is `Z_j(ξ ^ j)`,
  the same determinant for the `j`-th single lift.
* `HeightLe c y`: the family `y` of complex numbers, one for each pair `ι` of a prime `l` and an
  isomorphism `ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_l` (`PrimePadicIso`), has height at most `c`.
* `D.HasSmallRatios θ`: the `m`-fold twists `ξ_ι = θ ι` have `Nm Q(ξ_ι)` prime to the prime of `ι`
  and inverse ratios of Hecke values of height at most `x₁`.
role: Theorem C, the lower bound: covolume and twice the index together are at least about the main amount.

modules.title: The theta kernel of a descent pair with values in the weight representation
modules.note:
For a descent pair `O : New.DescentPair` with spaces `W` and `V`, the theta kernels of the data
`v_{P_ξ} ⊗ Ψ_bl ⊗ vac = O.fockDatum ξ` depend linearly on the vector `ξ` of the representation of
weight `(O.columnCount, O.detExp)`. Here `v_{P_ξ}` is the Fock vector of the polynomial
`P_ξ = O.fockPoly ξ`, and `Ψ_bl ⊗ vac = O.blockDatum` is the finite datum: a block datum at the
places of the level and the vacuum at the other finite places. So there is one kernel `θ_W(g, h)`
with values in this representation such that the kernel of `O.fockDatum ξ` is `⟨ξ̄, θ_W(g, h)⟩`. The
pairing `⟨ζ, η⟩` is `New.gramForm ζ η`, conjugate linear in `ζ`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.DescentPair.vectorKernel`, `New.DescentPair.gramForm_vectorKernel`: the kernel `θ_W(g, h)`
  and its defining property.
* `New.DescentPair.vectorKernelForm`: the function `θ_W(g, ·)` as an algebraic form on `V`.
* `New.DescentPair.normalizedDescent_eq_inner_vectorKernelForm`: the normalized descent
  `New.DescentPair.normalizedDescent` of a form `Ξ` on `V` has the value `⟨θ_W(g, ·), Ξ⟩` at `g`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.DescentPair`: the data of a space `W` of signs `O.signs`, an embedding of its index set in
  that of `V = I_n`, weights and a character, from which `(O.columnCount, O.detExp)` and the level
  are built.
* `New.WeylIndex n κ`: the index set of the coordinates of the representation of weight `κ`, on
  which `New.weylGramOver` is the Gram matrix of `New.gramForm`.
* `New.G E s`, `New.Gf E n`: the adelic unitary group of signs `s` and the finite part of that of
  the standard definite space `New.stdSpace E n = I_n`.
* `New.stdClassSum K f`: the sum of `f` over the double cosets of the rational points and `K`, each
  weighted by the inverse of the order of its automorphism group.

modules.title: The lift Θ_W, its adjoint and its norm
modules.note:
For a descent pair (`New.DescentPair`, a descent datum) with spaces W and V, the lift Θ_W is the
theta lift from forms on W to algebraic forms on V. The descent `New.DescentPair.normalizedDescent`
maps forms on V to functions on the adelic group of W; it is defined as a class sum and shown here
to be the adjoint of Θ_W. Both commute with the finite group of the chosen places. The finite datum
of the lift is the block datum modulo `π_M Q` times the vacuum, and the block datum is sharp for the
level `J_M`. For the pair `New.Data.descentPair D ϑ j`, which is `(W_j, V_j)` with a tame character
ξ = `ϑ`, the lift Θ_{j,ξ} = `New.Data.singleLift` goes from the forms of level `J_M` on W_j to the
definite space V_j.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.DescentPair.thetaLift`: the lift Θ_W from forms on W to forms on V. It is the lift
  `New.formLift` by the datum `New.DescentPair.fockDatum` of the highest vector, read as an
  algebraic form.
* `New.Data.singleLift`: the lift Θ_{j,ξ} on `New.Data.principalForms` on W_j. It is Θ_W for the
  pair `New.Data.descentPair` when 1 ≤ j ≤ m and 0 otherwise.
* `New.DescentPair.inner_thetaLift`: `New.DescentPair.normalizedDescent` is adjoint to
  `New.DescentPair.thetaLift`, for the Petersson product on `W` and the class sum product on `V`.
* `New.Data.coe_adjoint_singleLift`, `New.Data.normalizedDescent_eq_zero_iff`: the adjoint of
  Θ_{j,ξ} is the descent θ, so θ kills exactly the forms orthogonal to the lifts.
* `New.Data.singleLift_injective`, `New.Data.exists_hasSum_rallisTerm_inner_singleLift`: Θ_{j,ξ} is
  injective, and its Gram form is a constant `A` times the factor `New.DescentPair.gramFactor` of
  the pair times the sum of the terms `New.Data.rallisTerm`.
* `New.Data.exists_hasSum_inner_singleLift`: the same Gram form as a constant `c` times
  `New.DescentPair.twistFactor` times the sum of the terms `cosetTerm`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.descentPair`: the pair of W_j, of rank r, and the definite space V_j, of rank r + t,
  with the character χ_j ξ = `New.Data.liftChar` of weight −κ_j and the places
  `New.Data.levelPlaces`.
* `New.Data.principalForms`: the forms of parameter λ^Y (twice it is `New.Data.paramW`) and level
  `J_M`, which is principal at the chosen places and maximal elsewhere.
modules.literature:
For every tame twist, the theta lift from U(W_j) to a definite unitary group of much larger rank is
injective, and its Gram form is a non-zero twist-free constant times an explicit count at the level
and the twist's conductor times a sum of Hecke operators. The Rallis inner product in the convergent
range, with small-support data giving injectivity at a level, is known in the literature. Related
work: J.-S. Li, Non-vanishing theorems for the cohomology of certain arithmetic quotients, 1992;
Cossutta–Marshall, Theta lifting and cohomology growth in p-adic towers, arXiv 1106.2765, 2011;
Rallis, Injectivity properties of liftings associated to Weil representations, 1984; Rallis,
L-functions and the oscillator representation, 1987.

modules.title: Theta coefficients vanish off negative forms
modules.note:
This file finds a unit vector, supported on the negative signs, that kills the columns of a
frame. The rotations of its line lie in the maximal compact subgroup of `U (signMatrix s)`. It
shows that a polynomial whose Fock vector is fixed by the compact stabiliser of the frame is zero.
It proves that right translation by an element of a compact subgroup preserves the left Haar
measure. Here `New.Exchange.negCount s` is the number of signs `-1`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Exchange.centreCoeff_eq_zero_of_not_representedBy`: a Fourier coefficient of the theta
  integral `New.Exchange.thetaIntegral` vanishes, under conditions on weights, signs and
  integrability, at an invertible form that fails to be negative definite at some real place. After
  unfolding, the coefficient is an integral modulo the stabiliser of a frame, and the mean of the
  integrand over a compact subgroup is an invariant functional on Fock space, which is zero.
* `New.Exchange.apply_eq_zero_of_forall_fixed_eq_zero`: let a compact group act by bounded operators
  `ρ g` on a Banach space, and let `W` be a stable subspace of finite dimension in which only `0` is
  fixed. Then an invariant bounded functional `l` vanishes at every vector of `W` with continuous
  orbit: the mean of the orbit is a fixed vector of `W`.

Notions from other files:
* `thetaIntegral S T α β f`: the integral over `[U(T)]` of the theta kernel of the datum `f`.
* `PairFock E s t`, `realPairWeil`: the Fock space of the pair and its real Weil representation.

modules.title: Matched functions, sections over GL cosets and same-section pairs of matrix functions
modules.note:
This file studies functions on matrices over a finite product F of non-archimedean local fields with
integers O (`New.SemilocalField`). For k in GL_n(F) and n = b ⊔ a, write y_k = `New.firstCols e k`
for the block of columns b of k and x_k = `New.invLastRows e k` for the block of rows a of k⁻¹. A
matrix is primitive (`New.IsPrimitiveMatrix O`) if it is integral with an integral left inverse.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Rows.areMatched_block`: the block determinant functions `New.Rows.blockRowDatum` and
  `New.Rows.blockColDatum` are matched functions.
* `New.localSection χ y`: a linear functional that is the sum of χ(det g) Ψ(y g) over
  representatives g of GL_b(F)/GL_b(O) (`New.IsCommonCosetRep`,
  `New.exists_linearMap_eq_sum_and_isCommonCosetRep`) when that sum is finite;
  `New.exists_isPrimitiveMatrix_localSection_eq` computes it for Ψ with primitive support.
* `New.sameSectionPairs`: the pairs (Φ, Ψ) of Schwartz–Bruhat functions, Φ(x) zero unless xᵀ has a
  left inverse and Ψ(y) zero unless y has one, such that the section of y ↦ Φ(yᵀ) at x_kᵀ is χ(det
  k) times that of Ψ at y_k; GL_n(F) acts on them (`New.sameSectionPairs.translate_mem`).
* `New.sameSectionPairs.exists_linear_factor`: a linear map of Φ that is invariant under Φ ↦ χ(det
  g) Φ(g ·) depends, on same-section pairs, only on Ψ.
* `New.AreMatched.mem_sameSectionPairs`: for tame `χ` (`New.TameLocalChar`) and locally constant
  `Ψ`, matched functions over O form a same-section pair (`New.sameSectionPairs`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.AreMatched`: Φ vanishes off the matrices x_k = `New.invLastRows` (last rows of k⁻¹), Ψ off
  the y_k = `New.firstCols` (first columns of k), k in GL_n(O), and Φ(x_k) = χ(det k) Ψ(y_k).
* `New.TameLocalChar`: A finite ring R, a surjection π: O → R with kernel ϖO, and a primitive
  character η (`New.Exchange.IsPrimitiveMulChar`) with η∘π equal to χ⁻¹ on units, 0 on non-units.
* `New.SemilocalField`: Conditions met by a finite product of non-archimedean local fields: a
  locally compact ring with Haar measure, compact open subring O of volume one, a topologically
  nilpotent ϖ in O that is invertible in F, and `New.IsValuationPair O`.
modules.literature:
See `New.Determinant.Exchange.ExplicitMatching` and `New.Determinant.Exchange.TheoremForPartners`
for related work. See `Lib.Adelic.Hecke.ClassSums` for sources.

modules.title: The difference in the exchange identity as an equivariant lift
modules.note:
This file is a step towards the identity between theta integrals over `U(V)` and `U(V')`, where
`rk W = rk V + rk V'`. The identity is taken for matched functions `Φ`, `Ψ` at the ramified places
of the tame character `𝔠`. This file defines the small side `New.Exchange.thetaSmall`. It proves
how `thetaLarge` and `thetaSmall` change under translation at the ramified places, and that both
are invariant under the integral points of `U(W)` that are trivial there. From this it shows that
the difference of the two sides is an equivariant lift.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Exchange.thetaSmall`: the theta integral for `V'` of the datum `Ψ`.
* `New.Exchange.exists_isEquivariantLift_eq_thetaLarge_sub_smul`: the difference
  `thetaLarge Φ - c • thetaSmall Ψ` is a linear map of `Ψ` alone, on a `GL_n`-stable space, and is
  equivariant (`New.Exchange.IsEquivariantLift`).

Notions from other files:
* `thetaIntegral S T α β f`: the integral over `[U(T)]` of the theta kernel of the datum `f`.
* `thetaLarge W V 𝔠 v Φ`: the theta integral over `[U(V)]` of the datum `v ⊗ Φ`.
* `localChar P ξ k`: the character `t ↦ ξ t * |t| ^ (k / 2)` of the completions at `P`.
* `sameSectionPairs χ σ`: pairs `(Φ, Ψ)` of Schwartz–Bruhat functions on `a × n` and `n × b`
  matrices, `σ : b ⊕ a ≃ n`, whose values of `localSection χ` at the blocks of `k` differ by
  `χ (det k)`.

modules.title: Criteria for a function with a matched function to lie in a stable space; vanishing of lifts
modules.note:
Let χ be tame (`New.TameLocalChar`), and let P be a GL_n(F)-stable space of Schwartz–Bruhat
functions on n × b matrices. Let Ψ be a locally constant function that has a matched function
(`New.AreMatched`). The file gives two criteria for Ψ ∈ P in terms of the standard data
`New.stdColDatum χ s`, the function y ↦ χ⁻¹(det s y) for integral y with det s y a unit of O, and 0
otherwise.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Exchange.match_mem_of_stdColDatum`: if P contains a standard datum multiplied by an ℕ-valued
  function that is non-zero at a suitable point, then Ψ ∈ P; the proof averages over GL_n(O).
* `New.Exchange.IntegralFrame.match_mem_of_isPrimitiveMatrix_vanishing`: if a space M contains the
  shears of a standard datum and P contains what certain functionals kill in M, then Ψ ∈ P; a Gauss
  sum of the shears lies in P, and `New.Exchange.match_mem_of_stdColDatum` applies to it.
* `New.Exchange.IsEquivariantLift.shearInvariant_stdColDatum`: the partial means
  (`New.Space.Splitting.partialMean`) of the coefficients of the image of the standard datum of the
  frame are invariant under the local shears along one more isotropic line.
* `New.Exchange.IsSelfDualTestPair`, `New.Space.Splitting.VanishesAtSelfDual`: the pairs of an index
  and a Levi component at which vanishing at self-dual lattices is tested, and that vanishing.
* `New.Exchange.IsEquivariantLift.apply_eq_zero_of_areMatched`: `𝒟` vanishes on every locally
  constant datum with a matched function, once the image of the standard datum of the frame vanishes
  at self-dual lattices.

Notions from other files:
* `New.SemilocalField`: Conditions met by a finite product of non-archimedean local fields: a
  locally compact ring with Haar measure, compact open subring O of volume one, a topologically
  nilpotent invertible ϖ in O, and `New.IsValuationPair O`.
* `New.schwartzBruhat`: The space of locally constant, compactly supported complex functions that
  vanish outside a given set.
* `New.HasIntegralConductor`: The additive character ψ is continuous and has conductor O: ψ is
  trivial on tO exactly when t lies in O.
* `New.Exchange.IntegralFrame.stdDatum`: For a function G, the function equal to G(x·(K I)) at
  integral x and 0 elsewhere, with K and I two of the column blocks K, I, L of the frame.
* `New.Space.Splitting.partialMean`: the mean of a Fourier coefficient over the shifts of one more
  isotropic vector; `New.Space.Splitting.ShearInvariant` is its invariance under local shears.

modules.title: The image of the cone integral
modules.note:
Let `W' = W ⊕ H` and `V' = V ⊕ H`, with adapted splittings and isotropic lines `A` and `B` in the
hyperbolic planes, and let the rank of `W` be even. For `0 < z`, every Schwartz vector `v` for
`(W, V)` has a Schwartz vector `v'` for `(W', V')` such that the cone integral of `v'` and `v` have
the same theta integrals on standard data (`exists_thetaLarge_cone_eq`). Up to a positive factor
that is analytic in `z`, one `v'` serves for all `z > 0` (`exists_thetaLarge_cone_eq_mul`). The
slices of this `v'` along `A` (its values in the mixed model attached to `A`, as a function of a
vector of `V'` at the infinite places) are `β x • k x v^B`, where `v` is the zero term of `v^B`
along `Hom(W, B)`, `β` is a bump function near the vector `x_B` that spans `B`, and the smooth
family `k x` carries `x_B` to `x` for isotropic `x` in the support of `β`.

In the code `A` and `X` are the splittings of `W'` and `V'` that define the two lines, the adelic
vector `x_B` that spans `B` is `X.kAdelic`, and `lineVector X w` is its component at the infinite
place `w`. The word real refers to the components at the infinite places of `E`.

* `PairFock E s t` is the Fock space of the pair with signs `s` and `t`; a vector is Schwartz
  (`IsSchwartzVector`) if all its weighted norms are finite.
* `realPairWeil γ γ'` is the Weil representation of the real points `GInf` of the two unitary groups
  on this space, with `(x, y)` twisted by `det y ^ γ * det x ^ (-γ')`.
* A splitting is adapted (`IsBaseAdapted`) if its adelic frames are orthonormal at the infinite
  places and integral at the finite places.
* `cone A X μ z v'` is the integral of `coneIntegrand A X μ true z v'` over the pairs `(κ, a)` of a
  point of the maximal compact subgroup `maxCompact E t'` of `U(V')` and a family of non-zero
  complex numbers indexed by the infinite places.
* `thetaLarge W V 𝔠 v Φ` is the theta integral over `[U(V)]` of the datum with real part `v` and
  component `Φ` at the ramified places of `𝔠`, as a function on `U(W)`.
* A `SplitTameChar E μ` is a tamely ramified character of weight `μ`, all `μ w > 0`, of the norm-one
  adeles, with a non-empty set of ramified places that contains no conjugate of one of its places;
  so the ramified places are split over the totally real subfield.

modules.title: Parabolic theta terms, equal ranks, and the exchange identity for the large triple
modules.note:
The theta kernel of the dual pair (U(X), U(V)) is unfolded along a splitting of X over W₁ with an
isotropic frame. It becomes a sum of terms `New.Space.Splitting.thetaTerm` indexed by rational
matrices. Take a standard datum v ⊗ Φ, with v real and Φ an explicit function at the finite places
A. Its terms are computed at points n(c, z) m(q, g) of the parabolic subgroup. They are expressed
through the theta functional `New.Exchange.thetaOnRealData` of the smaller pair (W₁, V). For
V = V' ⊕ W₁ this functional factors as a product. Let `𝔠` be a tamely ramified character,
`V = V' ⊕ W₁`, and `X` equal to `W₁` plus a hyperbolic space. Then the identity between the theta
integrals `New.Exchange.thetaLarge` and `New.Exchange.thetaSmall` for standard data follows from an
identity of periods over `[U W₁]`, under conditions on the rank of `W₁`, the signs and the data,
when `W₁` splits off a hyperbolic plane.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Exchange.thetaTerm_eq_and_centreCoeff_eq_zero`: the terms are integrable
  (`hasIntegrableTerms_localDatum_of_eq_stdDatum`), each is an explicit factor times a value of
  `New.Exchange.thetaOnRealData` (`thetaTerm_localDatum_of_eq_stdDatum`), and the Fourier
  coefficient of the theta integral at `j • T` (`j` the purely imaginary element of the Weil data)
  vanishes if some signs represent the Gram matrices of all points with non-zero real slice but do
  not represent the matrix T (`centreCoeff_thetaIntegral_localDatum_eq_zero`).
* `New.Exchange.thetaOnRealData_boxProd_eq_mul`: on a product of real data, the functional of the
  datum built from a vector for (W₁, V') and a vector for (W₁, W₁) is the one for (W₁, V') times the
  theta kernel `New.pairTheta` of the pair (W₁, W₁).
* `New.Exchange.thetaLarge_eq_apply_one_of_even_rank`: if `W₁` has even rank and splits off a
  hyperbolic plane, the theta integral of `(W₁, W₁)` on the datum `χ⁻¹ ∘ det` is constant.
* `New.Exchange.RowColExchangeIdentity`: the two theta integrals are proportional on the standard
  data `New.stdRowDatum` and `New.stdColDatum`, with a condition on the size of the factor.
* `New.Exchange.IsPeriodIdentity`: the identity of periods over `[U W₁]` between real slices.
* `New.Exchange.exists_thetaLarge_eq_smul_of_isPeriodIdentity`,
  `New.Exchange.rowColExchangeIdentity_of_periods`: the identity for `V = V' ⊕ W₁`, where `X` is
  `W₁` plus a hyperbolic space, follows from an identity of periods over `[U W₁]`, for one character
  and for all characters, when `W₁` splits off a hyperbolic plane.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space.integrated`: the bounded bilinear map (v, f) ↦ v ⊗ f = ∫ v(y) ϱ(y)f dy, for v in the
  Fock space, f in 𝒮(V), y over real vectors in Fock coordinates.
* `New.Exchange.IntegralFrame.stdDatum`: for a frame with blocks K, I, L and a function G, the
  function y ↦ G(y (K|I)) on integral y, and 0 elsewhere.

modules.title: Smooth local Witt theorem and the exchange identity for `V' ⊕ W₁` and `V'`
modules.note:
Construction of the data at the real places for the identity `New.Exchange.RowColExchangeIdentity`
between the theta integrals of the pairs `(X, V' ⊕ W₁)` and `(X, V')`, where `X` splits over `W₁`.

* `New.Exchange.exists_isSchwartzVector_realSlice_eq`: a Schwartz Fock vector whose slices are a
  bump function times `realWeil 1 v`, scaled so that its slice at 0 for the opposite splitting is
  `v`.
* `New.Exchange.exists_contDiff_witt`: a local form of Witt's theorem for spans: frames near a
  nondegenerate frame `x` lie in the span of a unitary image of `x` that depends smoothly on them.
* `New.Exchange.exists_rowColExchangeIdentity_sum`: two vectors for which
  `New.Exchange.RowColExchangeIdentity` holds for these two pairs, one of them with a prescribed
  slice at 0.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space.Splitting`: a decomposition V = (lE^p ⊕ kE^p) ⊥ iV₀ with dual isotropic frames l, k and
  an isometric embedding i of V₀; `New.Space.Splitting.symm` exchanges k and l. It is adapted
  (`New.Exchange.IsBaseAdapted`) if the frames are orthonormal at the infinite places and integral
  at the finite ones.
* `New.PairFock E s t`: the Fock space of matrices whose `(i, j)` coordinate has the sign
  `t i * s j`, repeated at every infinite place. These signs are `New.homSigns s t`, and repeating
  them at every place is `New.realSigns`.
* `New.realPairWeil γ γ'`: the Weil representation on this Fock space, restricted to a pair of
  unitary groups at the infinite places, twisted by the powers of the determinants with exponents
  `γ` on the second and `-γ'` on the first.
* `New.Exchange.IsSchwartzVector`: all moments of the Fock vector are finite.
* `New.Exchange.realSlice`: the slice of a vector in the mixed Schrödinger–Fock model of an adapted
  splitting.
* `New.Exchange.RowColExchangeIdentity`: two theta integrals are proportional on admissible data,
  with a formula for the absolute value of the factor.
modules.literature:
See `New.Determinant.Exchange.TheoremForPartners` for related work. See
`Lib.Adelic.Witt.IwasawaDecomposition` for sources.

modules.title: Change of point and sign, and descent of the exchange identity by removing hyperbolic planes
modules.note:
This file records how forms and theta integrals behave under passage to opposite signs and under
change of point. It also descends the exchange identity `New.Exchange.RowColExchangeIdentity`
between theta integrals from a pair of large spaces to the pair with hyperbolic planes removed. For
any number of planes there is a space with an adapted splitting over a given space `W`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Exchange.isForm_neg_iff_and_integral_neg`: passing to the opposite signs (`G.neg`, the
  identity on matrices) preserves forms of a given type and integrals over the quotient, if it
  matches the rational points of the two spaces.
* `New.Exchange.exists_thetaLarge_thetaSmall_eq_circle_mul`: triples of spaces with the same signs
  have the same integrals `thetaLarge` and `thetaSmall`, up to one translation and numbers of
  modulus one.
* `New.Exchange.RowColExchangeIdentity.cone`: the identity descends along one plane of adapted
  splittings, to the cone integral of the real vector, if `rk W` is even and `rk V ≥ rk W / 2`;
  `New.Exchange.RowColExchangeIdentity.dualCone` is the case `rk V < rk W / 2`, on the other side of
  Poisson's formula.
* `New.Exchange.exists_rowColExchangeIdentity_removing_planes`: the identity descends along the
  planes of an adapted splitting, if `rk W` is even and `V'` has as many more negative signs than
  `V` as planes.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Exchange.RowColExchangeIdentity W V U μ σ x y ℓ`: the real vectors `x`, `y` are Schwartz
  vectors (all their weighted norms are finite), and for every tame character `𝔠` of weight `μ` the
  theta integrals `thetaLarge` over `[U(V)]` and `thetaSmall` over `[U(U)]` are proportional on
  standard data, with a factor `c` such that `D |c| ^ 2` is
  `lValueProdInt 𝔠 (rk V - rk W / 2) * ℓ 𝔠` for a constant `D` that does not depend on `𝔠`. The
  bijection `σ : b ⊕ r ≃ n` of the index sets of `U`, `V`, `W` orders the rows of the standard data.
* `New.Space.Splitting`: a decomposition V = (lE^p ⊕ kE^p) ⊥ iV₀ over E: isotropic frames l, k with
  l*Jk = 1, an isometry i from V₀ orthogonal to both, and rk V = rk V₀ + 2p.
* `New.Exchange.realSlice A U x`: the slice at `x` of a real vector for `(W', U)` in the mixed model
  of the splitting `A` of `W'` over `W`, a real vector for `(W, U)`; at `x = 0` it is the zero term.
* `New.stdColDatum χ z`: the standard datum `y ↦ χ⁻¹(det (z y))`, supported on the integral `y` for
  which this determinant is a unit.

modules.title: Vanishing of theta integrals descends along hyperbolic planes
modules.note:
If the theta integral of `(W ⊕ H, V ⊕ H)` vanishes on all Schwartz vectors and standard data, so
does that of `(W, V)`, provided `W` has even rank and `rk V - rk W / 2 ≥ -k` for a natural number
`k ≤ min μ`. The constant term along the new isotropic line is a value of Tate's integral, and for
the vectors of `exists_thetaLarge_cone_eq_mul` this integral is, by analytic continuation, the theta
integral of `(W, V)` times factors that do not vanish at the value in question.

Notions from other files:
* `thetaLarge W V 𝔠 v Φ`: the theta integral over `[U(V)]` of `v ⊗ Φ`, a function on `G E s`;
* `stdRowDatum σ χ y`: the finite datum `x ↦ χ⁻¹ (det (y; x))`, supported where the square matrix
  `(y; x)`, with rows ordered by `σ`, is invertible and integral;
* `SplitTameChar E μ`: a tame character of weight `μ`, ramified at a finite set of split places;
* `negCount s`: the number of signs `-1` among `s`.

modules.title: Exchange of theta integrals for matched functions and for data modulo an ideal
modules.note:
The exchange identity compares the theta integrals to U(W) from two spaces of complementary ranks.
For matched functions at the ramified places of a tame character, it holds with a constant whose
absolute value is expressed, up to a factor free of the character, through L-values and the ratio
`New.Exchange.equalRankThetaRatio`. This ratio is the squared absolute value of the theta integral
in equal rank, divided by the product of L-values `L_*` at half the rank of the space. For a
suitable Schwartz vector it is a nonzero constant that does not depend on the character. Together
these give the exchange theorem for finite data given by functions on matrices over `O_E / 𝔪`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Exchange.exchange_of_matches`: the exchange identity, with the constant measured by
  `New.Exchange.lValueProdInt` and `New.Exchange.equalRankThetaRatio`.
* `New.Exchange.exists_equalRankThetaRatio_eq_const`: the value of that ratio on `H ⊕ W`, for `W` of
  rank `2 k + 2 q` with `q` negative signs and `k ≤ μ`.
* `New.Exchange.exchange_theorem`, `New.Exchange.exchange_identity`: the exchange theorem, for one
  choice and for all choices of splitting characters.

Notions from other files:
* `New.PairFock E s t` is the Fock space of real data for a pair of spaces with signs `s`, `t`. A
  vector is a Schwartz vector (`New.Exchange.IsSchwartzVector`) if all its moments `fockMoment N v`
  are finite.
* `New.Exchange.thetaIntegral S T a b f` is the function g ↦ ∫ θ^{S,T}_{a,b}(f)(g,h) dh on U(S), the
  integral of the theta kernel `New.pairTheta` over [U(T)]. `New.Exchange.thetaLarge` and
  `New.Exchange.thetaSmall` are its cases for a datum v ⊗ Φ: Φ is read at the ramified places of a
  tame character, or Φ of the transpose is read at their conjugates.
* `New.Exchange.SplitTameChar.semilocalChar` is the character t ↦ ν(t/t̄) of ∏_{w∈S} E_w, t read as
  an idele supported on S, extended by 0 to non-invertible elements.
* `New.Exchange.lValueProd` is the number `L_*(e)` = (∏_{w ∈ S} Nw)^(e²) · ∏_{z=1}^{e}
  |L^S(z, ν)|²; `New.Exchange.lValueProdInt` extends it to integers by `L_*(-e) = L_*(e)⁻¹`.
* `υ` is the splitting character of the Weil data, `upsilonU1` its restriction to the norm-one
  ideles, and `rankTwist a n` is the character `a υ ^ ⌊|n| / 2⌋` of [U(1)].
* `AreMatched O σ χ Φ Ψ` says that `Φ` and `Ψ` are supported on the last rows of `k⁻¹` and the first
  columns of `k`, for `k` invertible over `O` and split by `σ`, and differ there by `χ (det k)`.
* `stdRowDatum σ χ z` and `stdColDatum χ z` are the standard functions of an integral matrix `z`:
  they send `x` to `χ⁻¹` of the determinant of `z` stacked on `x`, respectively of `z * x`, and to
  zero where this is not defined over the integers.
* `localDatum S T v Φ r` is the vector with real part `v`, the function `Φ` at the places that `r`
  reads, and the vacuum elsewhere; `modDatum S T 𝔪 Φ v` is the same for a function `Φ` modulo `𝔪`.
modules.literature:
Let V and V' be hermitian spaces of type `New.Space` over a CM field with `New.WeilData` whose ranks
and negative signs add up to those of W, which has q negative signs, with 2q + 2 ≤ rk W and rk
V − rk V' = 2e ≥ 0, and let the weights μ satisfy rk W ≤ 2μ + 2q. Then theta integrals over U(V) and
U(V') agree on matched ramified data up to a nonzero constant c, so theta lifts can be exchanged.
Only |c|² is given, up to an uncomputed factor: it is sized by the conductor and the Hecke L-values
at 1,…,e. Equal theta lifts of characters of complementary groups are known for trivial characters
(Siegel–Weil) and for O(3), O(1) to Mp(2). Related work: Snitz, Theta correspondence of automorphic
characters, J. Number Theory 122 (2007), arXiv math/0509486; Erez, Morphisms of global theta lifts
of non-trivial automorphic characters of orthogonal groups, arXiv 2401.13469, 2024; Gan–Qiu–Takeda,
The regularized Siegel–Weil formula (second term identity) and the Rallis inner product formula,
2014.

modules.title: One square: up then down against down then up
modules.note:
The exchange identity `New.Exchange.exchange_identity` for the space `U₁ ⊕ U₂`, read as a statement
on theta lifts of forms from `U₁` to `U₂`: its kernels are products of kernels for `U₁` and `U₂`.

* `New.Exchange.pairTransposedLift_comp_pairLift_mul`,
  `New.Exchange.pairLift_comp_pairTransposedLift_mul`: the path up to `A` and down, and the path
  down to `A'` and up, transform by the tame character.
* `New.Exchange.IsSquare`: the conditions on the four pairs of a square.
* `New.Exchange.exists_sum_pairLift_comp_pairTransposedLift_eq_smul`: for four pairs with their own
  splitting characters, the two paths agree on matched functions up to the factor `κ / c`, where `κ`
  may be zero.
* `New.Exchange.one_square_identity_of_isEdgeFamily`: the case of two families of characters indexed
  by finite types, in the form of the relation `New.Exchange.SquareLaw`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.modDatum S T 𝔪 Ψ v`: the theta datum on `Hom(S, T)` with real part the Fock vector `v`, given
  by the function `Ψ` on matrices modulo `𝔪` at the places dividing `𝔪` and by the vacuum elsewhere.
  The point datum at `x` is the case `Ψ = Pi.single x 1`, the indicator function of `x`;
* `New.Fock.fockMoment N v` is `∫ (1 + ‖z‖) ^ N * |v z| dz`, the moment of order `N` of the Fock
  vector `v`;
* a type of forms on a space is a function on its real unitary group, which prescribes the
  behavior of a form at the infinite places;
* `New.AutChar E`: the continuous characters of `[U(1)]`, the norm-one ideles of `E` modulo those
  from `E`;
* `New.Exchange.pairLift`, `New.Exchange.pairTransposedLift`: the lift and the transposed lift;
* `New.Exchange.IsPairEdge a b e e' P`, an edge `e → e'`: each of the families of characters `a`,
  `b` has a fixed weight, and for these weights the types `e`, `e'` and the Fock vector of `P` are
  such that the theta integral lifts forms of type `e` to forms of type `e'`;
  `New.Exchange.IsEdgeFamily` asks this of one family of characters indexed by finite types;
modules.literature:
A transposed lift followed by a lift is a multiple, possibly zero, of a lift followed by a
transposed lift. For forms on two unitary groups, the theta liftings through a group `A` and through
a group `A'` of no larger rank agree on matched ramified data, up to the L-value constant of the
exchange theorem and a factor free of the twist that may be zero. This moves lifts past each other
in chains. The seesaw principle and a rank-one exchange of periods are known in the literature.
Related work: Kudla, Seesaw dual reductive pairs, 1984; Chan, Period identities of CM forms on
quaternion algebras, 2020; He, Compositions of theta correspondences, 2005.

modules.title: Explicit real data: the exchange identity for a definite space with determinant data
modules.note:
`New.Rows.exists_stdClassSum_eq_mul_integral_modKernel` follows from the identity
`New.Exchange.exchange_identity` for the positive definite standard space `I_a` of rank `card a`,
with the real data made explicit as products of determinants.

Its archimedean step, `New.Rows.exists_mul_apply_eq_apply_matchedPoly`, takes an identity between
functionals on two Fock spaces that holds for one polynomial and its translates, and moves it to
explicit products of determinants.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Rows.matchedPoly`: the explicit polynomial for the pair of signs on `b` and on `n`.
* `New.Rows.realPairWeil_stackedDetProd`, `New.Rows.realPairWeil_matchedPoly`: the laws of
  `New.Rows.stackedDetProd` and `New.Rows.matchedPoly` under the real Weil representation
  `New.realPairWeil`.
* `New.Rows.exists_mul_apply_eq_apply_matchedPoly`: the matching of `New.Rows.stackedDetProd` with
  `New.Rows.matchedPoly`.
* `New.Rows.exists_stdClassSum_eq_mul_integral_modKernel`: a multiple, possibly zero, of the class
  sum equals a non-zero multiple of the integral over the group of the complementary space.
* `New.Rows.exists_mul_stdClassSum_eq_integral_modKernel`: the same identity divided by its non-zero
  constant, with the characters absorbed into the kernels and a free character for `I_a`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.GInf`: The archimedean unitary group G_∞ for signs s: one copy of the complex unitary group
  U(diag s) for each infinite place of E.
* `New.PairFock`, `New.Fock.polyVector`, `New.realPairWeil`: the Fock space of a pair of signs, the
  vector in it attached to a polynomial, and the real Weil representation of the pair on it.
* `New.Rows.stackedDetProd`: The product over τ and k of the determinants of M_{τk} stacked over the
  variable matrix x_τ (`New.Rows.stackedDet`), columns ordered by e.
* `New.AreMatched`: Φ lives on the rows `a` of k⁻¹ and Ψ on the columns `b` of k, for k in GL_n(O),
  and there the values differ by the factor χ(det k). Here the subring O is always `⊤`.
* `New.Exchange.lValueProd`: The number (∏_{w ∈ S} Nw)^(e²) · ∏_{z=1}^{e} |L^S(z, ν)|², for a
  natural number e.
modules.literature:
A multiple of a theta kernel summed over a definite unitary group equals a kernel integrated over a
unitary group of no larger rank, with explicit determinant polynomials on both sides. The size of
the multiple is given by Hecke L-values and the conductor up to one fixed factor, which may be zero.
The first term identity between theta integrals of complementary spaces and the harmonic polynomials
given by determinants are known in the literature. Related work: Gan–Qiu–Takeda, The regularized
Siegel–Weil formula, 2014 (after Kudla–Rallis, 1994; Ichino, 2004); Kashiwara–Vergne, On the
Segal–Shale–Weil representations and harmonic polynomials, 1978; Böcherer–Schulze-Pillot, Siegel
modular forms and theta series attached to quaternion algebras, 1991.

modules.title: The finite square law for theta lifts: special data, matched functions and Fourier form
modules.group: The norm of a chain of lifts
modules.note:
This is linear algebra over a finite ring `R` with a multiplicative character `χ`, behind the
commuting squares of theta lifts. A square law relates a function `L` on `a × n` matrices to a
function `L'` on `n × b` matrices. The rule for a square is the law written out for the weights `p`
and `nextDatum p`, and a second identity follows by applying the rule to a Fourier transform.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Exchange.SquareLaw`: `L` and `L'` transform by `χ ∘ det`, and `∑ Ψ L' = c ∑ Φ L` for all
  matched functions `Φ`, `Ψ`.
* `New.Exchange.pointDatum`, `New.Exchange.nextDatum`: the point datum, which is the indicator
  function of the matrix `(1; 0)`, and the datum built from a function `p` on `n × a` matrices,
  which has the value `p (-η)`, divided by the number of blocks `s`, at `(η s; 0 1)`.
* `New.Exchange.SquareLaw.sum_eq_nextDatum`: the square law for `p` and `nextDatum p`.
* `New.Exchange.SquareLaw.exists_sum_matrixFourier_eq_sum_nextDatum`: for primitive characters and
  the shapes `n = N`, `a = N ⊕ T`, `b = T`, an identity of the same kind between the Fourier
  transforms of the weights, with a constant of known modulus in place of the group orders.

Notions from other files:
* `New.firstCols e k`, `New.invLastRows e k`: for `k` invertible and indices split by
  `e : b ⊕ a ≃ n`, the columns `b` of `k` and the rows `a` of `k⁻¹`.
* `New.AreMatched ⊤ e χ Φ Ψ`: `Φ` vanishes off the matrices `invLastRows e k`, `Ψ` vanishes off the
  matrices `firstCols e k`, and `Φ (invLastRows e k) = χ (det k) Ψ (firstCols e k)` for all `k`.
* `New.inclMatrix R u`: for a map `u : m → n` of index sets, the `n × m` matrix whose `j`-th column
  is the standard basis vector of index `u j`.
* `New.Exchange.matrixFourier ψ f`: the function `ρ ↦ ∑ v, f v * ψ (tr (ρ v))`.
* `New.Exchange.IsPrimitiveMulChar χ`: for every `a ≠ 0` some `χ (1 + c * a)` is neither `0` nor
  `1`.

modules.title: Orders of block triangular groups and Gram forms of chains in triangles
modules.group: The norm of a chain of lifts
modules.note:
The group `New.parabolic (New.blockNumber j)` consists of the invertible block upper triangular
matrices whose diagonal blocks are one copy of `N` and `j` copies of `T`. Its order is
`#GL N R * (#GL T R) ^ j` times a power of `#R` whose exponent does not depend on the commutative
ring `R`.

An abstract triangle of spaces `F i n` has arrows `a t i n : F i n → F i (n + 1)` along row `i` and
`d t i n : F i (n + 1) → F (i + 1) n` down to the next row. The map `j i` embeds `V` in `F i 0`. The
arrows depend on a parameter `t : I`. An abstract relation `M c f` between functions `c : I → ℂ` and
`f : I → ℝ`, unital and multiplicative, is read "`c` has modulus `f`". For nonzero weights, weighted
chains along a row are injective on `V`. If the constants of the squares have prescribed moduli
`L r k`, the squares obey an adjoint law and the Gram forms of the first arrows are given, then the
Gram form of a full chain and the modulus of its constant are computed by induction. In the
application `F i n` is attached to the interval `[i + 1, i + n]`, the arrow `a` adds the greatest
element, and `d` stands for the adjoint of the map that adds the least element.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.exists_card_parabolic_blockNumber_eq`: the order of the group of block triangular matrices
  `New.parabolic (New.blockNumber j)`.
* `New.Exchange.IsTriangle`, `New.Exchange.weightedChain`: the conditions of a triangle; the
  weighted chain of a row.
* `New.Exchange.HasSquareModuli`: the moduli of the constants of the squares and the adjoint law.
* `New.Exchange.IsTriangle.eq_zero_of_weightedChain_eq_zero`: for nonzero weights, chains are
  injective on `V`.
* `New.Exchange.IsTriangle.exists_inner_weightedChain_eq`: for nonzero weights and under
  `HasSquareModuli`, the Gram form of a full chain is that of the product of the Gram operators
  `S t k` of the arrows `a t k 0`, times a ratio of weights and a constant of modulus `∏ L r k`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.BlockIndex N T j`, `New.blockNumber j`: the disjoint union of `N` and `j` copies of `T`, and
  the number of the block of an index (`0` on `N`, and `l` on the `l`-th copy of `T`).
* `New.compUpTo L j`: for linear maps `L i : M i → M (i + 1)`, the composite
  `L (j - 1) ∘ ⋯ ∘ L 0 : M 0 → M j`.

modules.title: Ratios of Hecke values and heights of functions of the twist
modules.group: The norm of a chain of lifts
modules.note:
This file treats functions of an `m`-fold twist `ϑ` with modulus Q. Here `ϖ` generates the product
of the chosen places, and `D.twistModulus ϑ e` is the modulus `ϖ ^ e Q`, with exponent e at the
chosen places and 1 at the places of Q. It defines the ratios of Hecke values and the absolute
value of a function of the twist up to a constant and a power of the norm of Q. Heights are
stated with `New.HeightLe c y`: the family y, indexed by the ι : ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_l, has height at most c.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.lRatioProd`, `New.Data.HasAbsUpToNormPower`: ratios of Hecke values, and the absolute
  value of a function of the twist up to a constant and a power of the norm of Q.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.isTameFor_mul_and_lValueProd_eq`: for a ramified pair with character ν and
  a twist ξ, the character νξ and its inverse are tame, and their products of `L`-values are
  expressed by the ratios of Hecke values.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.MFoldTwist`: a twist ϑ whose tame part has ψ_wⁿ non-trivial for all w in Q and
  1 ≤ n ≤ m.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair`: an integer 1 ≤ z ≤ t and a character ν of weight −c, z ≤ c ≤ 4b, with
  tame part supported on the chosen places.

modules.title: Theta lifts as a triangle of arrows: spaces, lifts, descents and the first lift
modules.group: The norm of a chain of lifts
modules.note:
This file arranges the theta lifts between the hermitian spaces `D.gridSpace i z 0 n` in a triangle
of positions `(i, n)`. The flag `z` selects one of two chains of spaces; see
`New.Determinant.Chain.ChainNorms`. The lift and the transposed lift of forms along an edge
(`New.Exchange.IsEdgeFamily`) with a finite datum modulo a modulus are `New.Exchange.modLift` and
`New.Exchange.modTransposedLift`, and this file writes them as integrals and treats the opposite
space. It defines the spaces and lifts of the triangle, and it proves, for `i < m`, the injectivity
and the norm of the first lift of row `i` on the subspace of fixed level. It also defines the left
and reversed pairs, the descents `New.Data.triangleTransposedLift` from `(i, n + 1)` to `(i + 1, n)`
along a left pair, and the ascents `New.Data.triangleReversedLift` from `(i + 1, n)` to `(i, n + 1)`
along the reversed pair.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.TriangleForm`, `New.Data.triangleLift`, `New.Data.triangleNegEquiv`,
  `New.Data.triangleBase`, `New.Data.triangleEmbedding`: the forms at `(i, n)`, the lift to
  `(i, n + 1)`, the copies at `(i, 0)` of the forms at `(0, 0)`, the subspace of fixed level, and
  its embedding at `(i, 0)`.
* `New.Data.triangleFirstLift`, `New.Data.exists_hasSum_inner_triangleFirstLift`: the first lift of
  a row, read on forms at `(0, 0)`; for `i < m`, its injectivity and norm on the subspace of fixed
  level, by Rallis' formula `New.SiegelWeil.rallis_inner_product_cosetTerm`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.gridSpace`: The hermitian space at the node (i, j) of grid z with offset o, for the
  signs `New.Data.gridSigns`.
* `New.Data.chosenLevel`: The level J_M consists of the elements of K₀ = `New.stdLevel` that are 1
  modulo the chosen places `New.Data.chosenPlace`.
* `New.Data.triangleModulus`, `New.Data.triangleGLCard`: the modulus 𝔪 of the triangle, and the
  order of the general linear group of a node modulo 𝔪. A lift times this order is the lift for the
  measure that gives the principal level of 𝔪 the volume 1.

modules.title: Norms along the chain of theta lifts and injectivity of ι_ϑ
modules.group: The norm of a chain of lifts
modules.note:
This file proves the two commutation relations in the squares of the triangle of lifts and
computes the adjoints of descents. With these, the lifts satisfy the conditions
`New.Exchange.IsTriangle`. This file then compares the chain ι_ϑ (`New.Data.lowerChainAtLevel`)
with the weighted chain of the triangle `z = false`. Here J_M is the principal level at the chosen
places `New.Data.chosenPlace`, and Q is the product of the places of the twist ϑ. The weighted
chain `New.Exchange.weightedChain` is the composite of the lifts `New.Data.triangleLift`, the n-th
multiplied by N_n = `New.Data.triangleGLCard` false ϑ n, an order of GL over a residue ring.

The node `(i, n)` of a triangle is the space of the interval `[i + 1, i + n]`: it has the stem and
the blocks `i + 1, …, i + n`. The nodes `(i, 0)` are the empty intervals; they carry the space at
`(0, 0)` negated `i` times. The lift `triangleLift` goes along a right pair and adds the last block.
The descent `triangleTransposedLift` is a transposed lift along a left pair and removes the first
block; it stands for the adjoint of the map that adds this block. The ascent `triangleReversedLift`
is a transposed lift along the reversed pair and adds the first block. The flag `z = false` selects
the chain Y₀, …, Y_m, and `z = true` the second chain, which is untwisted, has blocks of length
`t - 1` and starts from Y₀ plus a line.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.exists_triangleLift_triangleTransposedLift_comm`,
  `New.Data.exists_triangleTransposedLift_adjoint_comm`: the two commutation relations, with the
  moduli of their constants.
* `New.Data.exists_isTriangle`: with suitable descents these data satisfy the conditions
  `New.Exchange.IsTriangle`; for `z = false` also `New.Exchange.HasSquareModuli`, with the ratios of
  Hecke values `New.Data.quotientRatio` as moduli.
* `New.Data.inner_lowerChainAtLevel`: inner products of lifts are a multiple of those along the
  chain.
* `New.Data.lowerChainAtLevel_injective`: ι_ϑ is injective, because the chain is.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.RowIndex`, `New.Data.Y`: The basis index set of Y₀: e₁, …, e_ϱ, the indices of X₀, a
  middle vector, and e*₁, …, e*_ϱ. The basis index set of Y_j: the block `RowIndex`, then j blocks
  of t indices each.
* `New.Data.MFoldTwist`: a twist ϑ whose tame part ψ has ψ_wⁿ non-trivial for all places w in its
  set Q and 1 ≤ n ≤ m.
* `New.Data.chosenLevel`, `New.Data.lastLevel`: The level J_M consists of the elements of
  K₀ = `New.stdLevel` that are 1 modulo the chosen places `New.Data.chosenPlace`. The level J_ϑ(Y_m)
  on Y_m consists of those elements of J_M that are block upper triangular modulo Q.
* `New.Data.triangleModulus`, `New.Data.triangleGLCard`: the modulus 𝔪 of the triangle, and the
  order of the general linear group of a node modulo 𝔪. A lift times this order is the lift for the
  measure that gives the principal level of 𝔪 the volume 1.
* `New.Data.HasAbsUpToNormPower c f`: `‖c ϑ‖²` is `(f ϑ)²` times a constant, possibly zero, and a
  fixed integral power of the norm of Q.
modules.literature:
The chain of m theta lifts from U(Y_0) to the definite U(Y_m), mostly outside the range of Rallis's
formula, is injective at level J_M. On target forms its Gram form is that of a product of m Hecke
operators times a scalar whose modulus is a product of ratios of Hecke values. The norm and
injectivity of a single cuspidal theta lift, also below Weil's range, are known in the literature.
Related work: Gan–Qiu–Takeda, Regularized Siegel–Weil formula and Rallis inner product formula (Thm
1.3), 2014; Bruinier–Funke, Injectivity of the Kudla–Millson lift, 2010; He, Compositions of theta
correspondences, 2005.

modules.title: The volume of ι on the target forms as a product of volumes of theta lifts
modules.group: The norm of a chain of lifts
modules.note:
The volume of a linear map `u` between finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces is
`det (u* u) = u.normDet ^ 2`. For data `D`, the good forms (`New.Data.goodForms`) are the image of
the idempotent `New.Data.e₀`, and the target forms are the good forms on `Y₀`. `D.goodLift ϑ j` is
the restriction of the lift `D.singleLift ϑ j` to the good forms on `W_j`; its range is the space of
lifts.

* `New.Data.liftDeterminant`, `New.Data.chainDeterminant`: the volumes of the lift on the good forms
  and of `ι` on the target forms.
* `New.Data.exists_normDet_goodLift_sq_eq`: the volume of one lift in terms of the determinant on
  the target forms of the series of Rallis' formula.
* `New.Data.exists_adjoint_chain_comp_eq_smul_rallisProduct`: on the target forms `ι* ι` is the
  product `New.Data.rallisProduct` of these series times `c_Q ^ m`, up to a factor `c ϑ`, where the
  absolute value of `c ϑ` is a product of ratios of Hecke values, a power of the norm of the modulus
  of `ϑ` and a positive constant.
* `New.Data.exists_div_chainDeterminant_one_eq`: the resulting formula for
  `chainDeterminant ϑ / chainDeterminant 1`;
  `New.Data.exists_chainDeterminant_pos_and_div_chainDeterminant_one_eq` joins it with the
  positivity of the volumes.
* `New.Data.range_goodLift_le`: the space of lifts is spanned by lifts of good eigenforms.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.MFoldTwist`: a twist `ϑ` whose first `m` powers are twists.
* `New.Data.principalForms`: the forms of the fixed parameter on a space that are fixed by the
  principal level at the chosen places.
* `New.Data.singleLift`: the lift from principal forms on `W_j` to algebraic forms on `V_j`.
* `New.DescentPair.twistFactor`: the constant `c_Q` in the norm of one lift.
* `New.Data.lowerChainAtLevel`: the map `ι` from forms of principal level on `Y₀` to algebraic forms
  on `Y_m` of the last level of the twist.
* `New.Data.HasAbsUpToNormPower`: `D.HasAbsUpToNormPower c f` says that `‖c ϑ‖²` is `(f ϑ)²` times a
  constant, possibly zero, and a fixed integral power of the norm of the modulus of `ϑ`.
* `New.Data.quotientRatio`: `D.quotientRatio i j ϑ` is the product of the ratios of Hecke values of
  `D.untwistedLiftChar j / D.untwistedLiftChar i` at the twist `ϑ ^ (j - i)`.

modules.title: Monotone paths through two square grids, and their turns
modules.note:
The combinatorics of the paths along which forms are moved through the two grids of unitary groups,
the grid of the `Y^i_j` and the grid of the `Ỹ^i_j`. Here only the indices occur.

A path goes from `(m, 0)` to `(0, m)` by steps up (`j` grows) or left (`i` falls) and meets the
diagonal once, at some `(l, l)`. Its first half lies in the grid of the `Ỹ` and its second half in
that of the `Y`. Both halves are recorded in one shape, as paths from `(0, m)` to `(l, l)` by steps
down or right. The half in the grid of the `Y` is read backwards, the way conjugate forms move. The
half in the grid of the `Ỹ` is read forwards, the way forms move, with the two indices exchanged: a
step left is recorded as a step down, and a step up as a step right.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.GridPath`: a monotone path in one grid. `New.TwoGridPath`: a path through both grids, given
  by two halves that meet on the diagonal.
* `New.TwoGridPath.Turn`: a turn replaces a node `(i, j)` by `(i + 1, j + 1)`.
* `New.TwoGridPath.exists_turn`: every path but the last can be turned.
* `New.TwoGridPath.turn_induction`: induction backwards along turns, one at each `(i, j)` with
  `i, j < m`, from the last path to the first.

modules.title: Weights of regular parameters and bounds on boxes
modules.note:
A weight is a pair `(κ, e)`: `κ w h` is the number of columns of height `h` at the place `w`, and
`e w` is the power of the determinant. `New.IsHCParam κ e l` says that `l w` lists twice the
Harish-Chandra parameter of `(κ, e)` in some order. This file finds a weight for each regular
parameter `l = 2λ` (`New.HCParam.HasGap`). It also bounds a weight by its parameter: the number of
boxes and the power of the determinant.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Exchange.boxes_le_card_mul_of_isHCParam`, `New.Exchange.natAbs_le_of_isHCParam`: a bound `β`
  on the entries of `l` bounds the number of boxes and, for nonempty `n`, the determinant power.
* `New.Exchange.exists_isHCParam_of_hasGap`: every regular parameter comes from a weight;
  `New.Exchange.exists_isHCParam_of_le` adds control of the determinant power from below.

Notions from other files:
* `New.boxes κ N`: the number of boxes in the columns of height below `N`, over all places.

modules.title: Steep parameters of Y₀ and Ỹ^0_0; periods of Poincaré series of deep level
modules.note:
At every infinite place, the parameter of `Y₀` and minus the parameter of `Ỹ^0_0 = Y₀ ⊕ E ẽ` are
steep in the sense of `New.DiscreteSeries.IsSteep`. Separately, at deep level the period over `V`
of a Poincaré series on `V ⊕ ⟨1⟩` is approximated by the term of the identity coset.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.exists_isSteep`: for one numbering of the indices, the parameter of `Y₀` (`z = false`)
  and minus that of `Ỹ^0_0` (`z = true`) satisfy `New.DiscreteSeries.IsSteep` at every infinite
  place `τ`. That is, the highest weight `New.HCParam.lowestKType` of the lowest `K`-type vanishes
  on a block of indices of sign `+`. On the other indices the signs alternate and it decreases
  strictly within `[-3B, -B]`, `B = D.liftWeight 0 τ`. `New.Data.gridSigns` gives the signs and
  `New.Data.gridParam` twice these parameters.
* `New.Exchange.poincareKernel`: the function whose translates a Poincaré series sums. Its real
  factor here is `New.Exchange.translatedCoeff`, a translated product of matrix coefficients.
* `New.Space.IsLastColumn`: a rational vector of `V ⊕ ⟨1⟩` is the last column of a group element
  `γ`, that is, the vector `γ ẽ` for the last basis vector `ẽ`. Last columns index the cosets, and
  `New.Space.IsLastColumn.le_norm_archCoords_sub` separates them.
* `New.Exchange.norm_poincare_period_sub_le`: at deep level the period equals the term of the
  identity coset up to a small error.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.Φ`: the set of infinite places of the field `E` of the data `D`. Also, `D.ϱ` is the
  number of hyperbolic planes of `Y₀`, `D.InitIndex 0` the set of basis indices of `X₀` other than
  the last and `D.GridIndex z 0 0` the index set of `Y₀` or `Ỹ^0_0`.
* `Φ w` in the bounds `R ≤ ‖Φ w a‖`: the complex embedding of `E` at the infinite place `w`.
* `V.move x`, `vecAtPoint`, `archCoords`: the space `V` at the point `x` of the adelic group, the
  adelic coordinates of a rational vector there, and their infinite part as a Euclidean vector.
* `New.Data.liftWeight`: the number `κ_j(σ) = κ(σ) + (j + 1/2) Δ` at the infinite place `σ`, where
  `κ` is `D.weight`, `Δ = D.gap` the gap and `D.halfGap` half the gap.
* `New.GInf E s`: the product of one copy `New.USign s` of the complex unitary group `U(diag s)`
  for each infinite place of `E`. For an integer vector `l : New.HCParam s`, read as twice a
  Harish-Chandra parameter, `l.dsCoeff` is the Flensted-Jensen matrix coefficient on `U(diag s)`,
  and `l.HasLargeGap A` says that `l` has gap at least `500 n ^ 3 + A`, for `n` the rank.
* `New.signedSpace E s`: the standard space with matrix `diag(s)`; it needs a primitive root of
  unity of order `5040` in `E` (`New.HasPrimitiveRoot5040`).
* `New.Space.Γ`, `New.Space.quotMeasure`: the rational points of a hermitian space `V` inside the
  adelic unitary group `G E s`, and the measure on a fundamental domain for them.
* `New.principalLevel`: the finite adelic integral points congruent to `1` modulo an element `a`
  of the ring of integers of `E`.

modules.title: Moduli, spaces, moves, path data and periods on the two grids
modules.note:
This file sets up the two grids of hermitian spaces attached to admissible data `D` and an `m`-fold
twist `ϑ`. A node is a triple `(z, a, b)`: the space `Y^a_b` for `z = false` and `Ỹ^b_a` for
`z = true`. The element `ϖ = π_M = New.Data.piM`, of norm `M`, generates the product of the chosen
places, and Q is the product of the places of `ϑ`. This file defines the moduli of the grids, the
spaces, characters, levels and moves at the nodes and edges, then functions on tuples of matrices
and the periods formed with them.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.gridModulus`: the modulus `𝔪 = 𝔟 Q` with `𝔟 = ϖ ^ D.natB`. For the twist `1` it is `𝔟`
  (`New.Data.gridModulus_one_ideal`).
* `New.Data.liftMove`, `New.Data.transposedMove`: the theta lift `(a, b) → (a + 1, b)` and the
  transposed lift `(a, b + 1) → (a, b)` with a single matrix as finite datum.
* `New.Data.IsPathDatum`: functions of a matrix per edge of a path that are equivariant at the inner
  nodes and under the level `𝔟` at `Ỹ^m_0`, vanish unless the vertical edges (those whose character
  carries the twist) carry split injective matrices, and take sums of few roots of unity as values.
* `New.Data.gridPeriod`, `New.Data.IsProportional`: the period of path data, and the relation
  `Ψ ∝ Ξ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Modulus`: a nonzero ideal of O_E prime to its complex conjugate.
* `New.Data.MFoldTwist`: a twist ϑ whose tame part has ψ_wⁿ non-trivial for all w in Q and
  1 ≤ n ≤ m.
* `New.Data.GridIndex`, `New.Data.gridSigns`, `New.Data.gridParam`: the index set of a basis, the
  signs of the hermitian form and twice the parameter of the type at a node with an offset o; the
  grids have o = 0.
* `New.Exchange.IsEdgeFamily`: a family of characters over two pairs of conjugate cuspidal types
  which, with a polynomial, form an edge for the real Weil representation.

modules.title: Vanishing of forms on Y₀ orthogonal to the deep level on Ỹ^0_0
modules.note:
A form `y` of level `J_M = D.chosenLevel` on a hermitian space `V` is zero if it is orthogonal to
the restrictions of all forms of the deep level `J(𝔟)` on `V ⊕ ⟨1⟩`, translated by a suitable real
point `ω`. This requires size conditions on the level and a lower bound for the pairing of the
matrix coefficients for the parameter `l` of `V` and the parameter `l'` of `V ⊕ ⟨1⟩`.

Every bound `S` of `‖y‖` is halved. The smoothing of `y` is its convolution with the translated
coefficient for `l'`; the point `ω` with the lower bound for the pairing comes from steepness, in
the proof of `New.Data.exists_eq_zero_of_orthogonal_gridLevelForms`.

1. Decay: `New.Exchange.integral_typeKernelMajorant_le`.
2. The cusp: `New.Exchange.norm_le_half_of_firstMinimum_lt`.
3. A Poincaré series is a form, so its period is zero:
   `New.Exchange.poincare_period_translatedCoeff_eq_zero`.
4. Unfolding shows that the smoothing of `y` is small: `New.Exchange.norm_poincare_period_sub_le`
   and `New.Exchange.norm_realConv_translatedCoeff_le`.
5. Undoing the smoothing: `New.Exchange.norm_le_half_of_le_firstMinimum`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Exchange.HasDeepLevelSizes`: the size conditions. The real number `m` in them is at least a
  power of `β` that absorbs all constants in the estimates.
* `New.Exchange.eq_zero_of_petersson_translate_eq_zero`: the criterion at a given real point;
  `New.Exchange.exists_forall_eq_zero_of_petersson_restrict_eq_zero` chooses the point place by
  place.
* `New.Data.exists_eq_zero_of_orthogonal_gridLevelForms`: the forms of level `J(𝔟)` on `Ỹ^0_0`,
  restricted to `U(Y₀)` after translation by one real point, detect every nonzero form of level
  `J_M` on `Y₀`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.typeKernel`: `typeKernel l s` is the product over the infinite places `w` of the formal
  degree times the conjugate matrix coefficient `(l w).dsCoeff` of the parameter `l w`.
* `New.Space.IsForm`: `V.IsForm e F` says that `F` is automorphic, bounded, and fixed by the right
  convolution `New.realConv` with `e` over the real points (if `e` is integrable).
* `New.Space.firstMinimum`: the least norm of a nonzero vector of the lattice of a space, cut off at
  `1`; `V.move x` is the space `V` with its adelic frame multiplied by `x`.
* `New.Data.principalForms`, `New.Data.gridLevelForms`: the forms fixed by `D.chosenLevel`, and the
  forms on `Ỹ^i_0` fixed by the deep level, that is, the principal level of
  `D.gridLevelGen = D.piM ^ D.natB`, where `D.piM * star D.piM = D.M` is `M`.
* `New.Data.spaceY`: the hermitian space `Y_j` with its adelic frame, chosen as in
  `New.Data.exists_space_isStd_of_le_and_gram_eq_of_lt`.
* `(l w).HasLargeGap B`: the entries of `l w = 2λ` are distinct, of the parity of `card n - 1`, and
  entries of `λ` with different signs are at least `500 n³ + B` apart; `dsCoeff` is the matrix
  coefficient of the parameter and `dsKernel` its conjugate times the formal degree.
modules.literature:
Nonvanishing periods via Poincaré series of deep level and restriction results of Burger–Sarnak type
are known in the literature. Related work: Prasad–Schulze-Pillot, Generalised form of a conjecture
of Jacquet, 2008; Harris, Testing rationality of coherent cohomology of Shimura varieties, 2014;
Muić, Fourier coefficients of automorphic forms and integrable discrete series, 2015.

modules.title: Periods on the diagonal and path data on the first path
modules.note:
The first path goes from `Ỹ^m_0` to `Ỹ^0_0 = Y₀ ⊕ E ẽ₀` and from `Y₀` to `Y_m`. Its spaces are the
nodes `(z, 0, i)`, the first columns of the two grids: `(false, 0, i)` is `Y_i` and `(true, 0, i)`
is `Ỹ^i_0`. A form on `Ỹ^m_0` and a conjugate form on `Y_m` move down these columns by transposed
lifts and meet at `i = 0`. The product `Ψ¹` of the point data of the edges computes the period of
the two iterated transposed lifts `New.Data.transposedChain`. The sum `Ψ⁰` of the translates of
`Ψ¹`, weighted by the characters of the edges, is a path datum, and its period is the number of
translates times that of `Ψ¹`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.exists_petersson_eq_diagonalPeriodForm`: the period with a form on `Ỹ^0_0`, as a
  functional of the form on `Y₀`, is a Petersson product.
* `New.Data.diagonalPeriodForm_tupleAction`: translating the matrices by a family that is `1` at
  the ends and `diag(g, 1)` at `(0, 0)` of the `Ỹ`, `g` being its member at `(0, 0)` of the `Y`,
  multiplies the period by the characters of the edges.
* `New.Data.firstPointDatum`, `New.Data.firstPathDatum`: the functions `Ψ¹` and `Ψ⁰`.
* `New.Data.exists_isPathDatum_diagonalPeriodForm_eq`: the period of the iterated transposed lifts
  is a constant times the period of path data on the first path.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.triangleModulus`: the modulus `𝔪₀ = π_M Q` for the chain of the `Y` and `𝔟 = π_M ^ b`
  for that of the `Ỹ`, with `π_M = D.piM`. `New.Data.gridModulus` is `𝔪 = 𝔟Q`, where `Q` comes
  from the twist `ϑ`. `New.Data.triangleGLCard` is the index `n_𝔪₀(Y_i)` or `n_𝔟(Ỹ^i_0)`.
* `New.Data.levelIndex`: the index of the level `New.Data.nodeLevel` at a node, which is the level
  `𝔪` at the `Y_i` and the level `𝔟` elsewhere.
* `New.Data.diagonalPeriodForm`: the period of a conjugate form on `Y^j_j` and a form on `Ỹ^j_j`
  along the embedding of unitary groups, shifted on the line by a scalar from the twist, at a real
  point.
* `New.Data.EdgeTuple`: a matrix modulo `𝔪` for each pair of nodes. A `NodeFamily` of invertible
  matrices acts on it by `New.Data.tupleAction`; `New.Data.edgeCharProd` is the product of the
  characters of the edges at the determinants of such a family.
* `New.GridPath.formMap`: the composite of the maps by the matrices of a tuple along a path.

modules.title: Turning path data, and turns off the diagonal
modules.note:
A turn of a path replaces two sides of a square by the two other sides. The `m`-fold twist is `ϑ`,
the characters of the edges are built from `D.untwistedLiftChar j`, of weight `-D.liftWeight j`, and
the vertical edges, whose character carries a power of `ϑ`, go from `Y^i_j` to `Y^i_(j+1)` and from
`Ỹ^i_j` to `Ỹ^i_(j+1)`. The forms that move in the grid of the `Y` are conjugate forms.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.Corner.IsTurn.exists_isPathDatum`: the match of a path datum, after a Fourier transform
  in the column of the line if the turn is on the diagonal, is a path datum.
* `New.Data.exists_squareLaw_grid_hasAbsUpToNormPower`: the exchange
  `New.Exchange.one_square_identity_of_isEdgeFamily` on a square of a grid, with a constant
  `κ / c ϑ` whose denominator has, up to a power of the norm, the absolute value
  `New.Data.turnRatio`.
* `New.Data.TransfersPeriods`: path data pass forwards, and proportionality of periods passes
  backwards.
* `New.Data.exists_transfersPeriods_off_diagonal`: a turn off the diagonal transfers periods.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.GridNode`: a triple `(z, a, b)`, the node `Y^a_b` if `z = false` and `Ỹ^b_a` if
  `z = true`. Its index set is `D.NodeIndex`, which is `D.GridIndex z a b`.
* `New.Data.EdgeTuple`: a matrix over the residue ring modulo `gridModulus ϑ` for each pair of
  nodes. The modulus is that of the twist `ϑ` times a power of the product of the chosen places. A
  `New.Data.NodeFamily` is an invertible matrix `g q` for each node `q`; it takes the matrix `S e`
  on an edge `e = (p, q)` to `(g q)⁻¹ * S e * g p`. It is admissible (`New.Data.IsAdmissibleFamily`)
  if at each of the two starting nodes it lies in the level of the node and at each node
  `(true, a, a)` it is `g ⊕ 1` for its element `g` at `(false, a, a)`.
* `New.Data.IsPathDatum N w`: a function of the matrices on the edges `w` that admissible families
  fix up to `edgeCharProd`, that vanishes unless the vertical edges carry split injective matrices,
  and whose values are sums of at most `N` roots of unity.
* `New.AreMatched`: matched functions, `Φ(x_γ) = χ(det γ) Ψ(y_γ)` with both supported on such
  matrices, `y_γ` being the first columns of `γ` and `x_γ` the last rows of `γ⁻¹`. The subring
  argument, here `⊤`, is where the entries of `γ` and `γ⁻¹` lie. `New.Exchange.matchOf` is the match
  of a function.
* `New.Exchange.SquareLaw` with constant `C`, for functions `L` and `L'` on matrices over a finite
  ring: `∑ Ψ L' = C ∑ Φ L` for all matched `Φ`, `Ψ`.

modules.title: Turns on the diagonal, and the transfer of periods from the first path to the last
modules.note:
A turn on the diagonal replaces the node `(j, j)` of a path through the two grids by
`(j + 1, j + 1)`. A seesaw moves the period to the space `S = Ỹ^(j+1)_j = Y^(j+1)_j` common to both
paths, where the line contributes a theta kernel. There the line is reversed and the two maps are
exchanged, and a second seesaw moves the period on. Together with the turns off the diagonal this
transfers the periods from the first path to the last.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.columnPeriod`, `New.Data.rowPeriod`: the integrals over the group of `S`.
* `New.Data.isProportional_of_columnPeriod`, `New.Data.IsProportional.exists_rowPeriod_eq_mul`: the
  seesaws.
* `New.Data.exists_columnLineKernel_eq`: reversing the line.
* `New.Data.exists_transfersPeriods_of_turn`: one turn, with the absolute value of its constant.
* `New.Data.exists_transfersPeriods_first_last`: the `m ^ 2` turns composed.

Notions from other files:
* `D.gridSpace 0 false a b` is the space `Y^a_b` and `D.gridSpace 0 true a b` is `Ỹ^b_a`; their
  bases are indexed by `D.GridIndex`.
* `modKernel S T a b 𝔪 Ψ p` is the theta kernel of the pair `(S, T)` with characters `a`, `b` of
  `[U(1)]`, for a function `Ψ` on matrices modulo `𝔪` and a polynomial `p`. On a space of rank `k`
  the character `a` gives the splitting character `New.AutChar.spaceChar`, the base change of `a`
  times `υ ^ (-k)`.
* `D.GridForm false a b` holds the conjugate forms on `Y^a_b`, and `D.GridForm true a b` the forms
  on `Ỹ^b_a`. In sums over tuples of matrices, one for each edge, the letter `S` names the tuple.
* `IsProportional Γ Ψ Ξ`, written `Ψ ∝ Ξ`: the periods of `Ψ` on the path `Γ` are multiples of `Ξ`
  by numbers that depend neither on the twist nor on the forms.
* `TransfersPeriods Γ' Γ k c`: path data `Ψ'` on `Γ'` give path data `Ψ` on `Γ`, with the bound for
  the number of roots of unity in a value multiplied by `k`, and `Ψ ∝ Ξ` implies `Ψ' ∝ Ξ / c`.
* `D.HasAbsUpToNormPower c f`: `‖c ϑ‖² = C (Nm Q)ᵏ (f ϑ)²`, with `Q` the modulus of the twist `ϑ`
  and with `C`, `k` independent of `ϑ`.

modules.title: The maps `Θ^♭` and `res^♭`, and the first path
modules.note:
The first path consists of the spaces `Ỹ^m_0, …, Ỹ^0_0` and `Y₀, …, Y_m`, which are hermitian spaces
over the CM field `D.E`. These are the nodes `(z, 0, i)`, the first columns of the two grids:
`(false, 0, i)` is `Y_i` and `(true, 0, i)` is `Ỹ^i_0`. The iterated transposed lifts
`New.Data.transposedChain` along such a column are the transposes of the chain of theta lifts
`New.Exchange.weightedChain`. In the grid of the `Ỹ` the composite of all `m` of them is
`Θ^♭ = D.transposedChain 1 true 0`. The letter `ϑ` stands for an `m`-fold twist (`D.MFoldTwist`): a
tame character whose powers up to the `m`-th are non-trivial at each place of its modulus `Q`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.GridForm` and `New.Data.TriangleForm`: in the grid of the `Y` (the Boolean `false`) the
  conjugate forms and the forms at a node; in the grid of the `Ỹ` (the Boolean `true`) the forms and
  the conjugate forms.
* `New.Data.triangleModulus`: the modulus of the point data along the first column of a grid. It is
  `𝔪₀ = π_M Q` for the `Y` and `𝔟 = π_M ^ b` for the `Ỹ`, with `π_M = D.piM`.
* `New.Data.triangleGLCard`: the index `n_𝔪₀(Y_i)` or `n_𝔟(Ỹ^i_0)` of the level of that modulus.
  Each lift and each transposed lift along the column is multiplied by the index of its smaller
  space; for the `Ỹ` these factors are constants.
* `New.Data.principalForms`: the forms of the level `J_M = D.chosenLevel`, here on `Y₀`.
* `New.Data.lowerChainUpTo`: the chain of twisted lifts from `Y₀` to `Y_j`; for `j = m` it is `Θ_ϑ`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.eq_zero_of_weightedChain_triangleLift_eq_zero`,
  `New.Data.gridLevelForms_eq_map_transposedChain`: the chain of the `Ỹ` is injective on level `𝔟`,
  and its transpose `Θ^♭` is onto that level.
* `New.Data.IsFlatRestriction`: the map `res^♭`, given by its pairings;
  `New.Data.exists_isFlatRestriction_range_eq_top`: at a suitable real point it is onto.
* `New.Data.exists_isPathDatum_integral_eq`: the pairing with the lifts of a restriction is a
  constant multiple of a period of path data on the first path.

modules.title: The branching pairing and the periods on the last path
modules.note:
On the last path all spaces are positive definite. Forms are read as algebraic forms on the groups
`New.stdSpace`, and theta lifts become algebraic. Branching from `GL (n + 1)` to `GL n` for
interlacing parameters is an integral pairing with explicit bounds, so a period over the smaller
definite group is a constant times an integral of this pairing over the finite points. This gives
the finite sum `Ξ = New.Data.lastPathPeriod` to which all periods on the last path are proportional.
This is part of the construction of spanning forms on `U(Y_0)` with integral twisted lifts and
bounded conjugates; the denominators and the conjugates of `Ξ` are bounded in
`New.Determinant.AuxiliaryForms.SpanningForms`. The prefix `lastPath` of a name refers to the
last path, which consists of the edges between the nodes `(z, j, m)`, `j ≤ m`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Exchange.IsBranchingPairing`: an integer matrix whose pairing is equivariant for block
  matrices, is bounded, and computes the period of two algebraic forms over the smaller definite
  group as a constant times the integral of the pairing of their values at finite points.
* `New.Exchange.exists_isBranchingPairing`: such a matrix exists. It is the branching matrix of
  `New.exists_branching_matrix` followed by the duality of `New.exists_isDualPairing_of_isHCParam`.
* `New.Data.exists_lastPathPeriod_mem_smul_norm_le`: for a path datum, `Ξ` is a sum of a controlled
  number of terms, each with the bound that holds for the pairings of the vectors reached by the
  lifts.
* `New.Data.isProportional_lastPathPeriod`: every period on the last path is a constant times `Ξ`
  divided by the index of the level `J(𝔪₀)` on `Y_m`, which differs from the index of `J(𝔪)` by a
  constant factor.

Notions from other files:
* `New.IsHCParam`: `l` lists twice the Harish-Chandra parameter of the weight `(κ, e)`, in some
  order; `κ` counts the columns of each height and `e` is the exponent of the determinant.
* `New.ofAlgForm`: the function g ↦ ⟨v⁺, ρ(g_∞⁻¹) φ(g_f)⟩ on the adelic group attached to an
  algebraic form φ, with v⁺ = `New.highestVector` for the parameter.
* `New.classIntegral`: the integral over Γ \ G of a smooth left Γ-invariant function, for the Haar
  measure that gives the level K volume 1, written as a sum over classes.
* `New.StdClasses`: the double cosets of G_f by its rational points on the left and a level K on
  the right.
* `New.Data`: the admissible data `D` for the fixed parameters `P`. They give the CM field `D.E`,
  its infinite places `D.Φ` and the number `m = D.m` of lifts in the chain.
* `New.Data.gridSpace`: the Hermitian space at the node `(z, i, j)`, for the offset `0`. It is
  `Y^i_j` if `z = false` and `Ỹ^j_i` if `z = true`, and `Y_j = Y^0_j`.
* Moduli of a twist `ϑ` with places `Q`, where `ϖ = D.piM` and `b = D.natB`: `𝔪 = ϖ ^ b Q`
  (`New.Data.gridModulus`), `𝔪₀ = ϖ Q` and `𝔟 = ϖ ^ b` (`New.Data.triangleModulus`). The level
  `J(𝔞)` consists of the integral finite points that reduce to `1` modulo `𝔞`.

modules.title: Denominators and sizes on the last path, and the auxiliary forms
modules.note:
Let `Ξ = New.Data.lastPathPeriod Ψ y` be the sum attached to the last path. Its denominators are
small at the primes that do not divide `Nm Q` and, for the trivial twist, its conjugates are small.
Going back through the turns to the first path, and reading the values of a form from its pairings
with delta forms, we get integrality and size for the chain of lifts from `Y₀` to `Y_m` on the
restrictions of short forms. Throughout, `ϑ` is an `m`-fold twist, `Q` is its finite set of places,
`ϑ.normQ` is `Nm Q`, and sizes are measured by the parameters `x = D.x` and `b = D.b`. The
modulus `𝔪 = gridModulus ϑ` of the twist is the product of the chosen places to the power
`D.natB` (the number `b` as a natural number), times `Q`. The other numbers of the data that occur
are the level `D.M`, the order `D.q₁` of the root of unity that generates `E` over
`K = ℚ(√-P.d)`, the prime `P.d`, the ranks `D.n j` and the parameter `D.r`; at most
`D.natB * D.r ^ 4` boxes occur in each diagram of a weight on the last path.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.exists_mul_lastPathPeriod_mem_embValRing`, `New.Data.norm_lastPathPeriod_le`:
  denominators and conjugates of `Ξ`.
* `New.Data.exists_integral_lowerChainUpTo_eq_lastPathPeriod`: the index of the level times the
  pairing with the chain of lifts of a restriction is a constant multiple of `Ξ` divided by the
  constants of the turns.
* `New.Data.exists_dualPairing_eq_mul_lastPathPeriod`: the values of the chain of lifts, read by
  delta forms, with one constant for all twists, points and forms.
* `New.Data.exists_span_short_lifts_eq_top`: the space of forms on `Y₀` is spanned by forms with two
  properties: for every twist their scaled lifts are integral at the primes not dividing `Nm Q`, and
  for the trivial twist the conjugates of their lifts are small. The passage to target forms is
  `New.Data.exists_span_isAuxiliaryForm_eq_top`, in `New.Determinant.Twist.LongForms`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.lastPathPeriod Ψ y`: the sum over the tuples of matrices `S` of `Ψ S` times the pairing
  of the lifts of the two forms `y` along the halves of the last path, integrated over the finite
  points of `Y^m_m`.
* `New.Data.gridLevelForms m`: the forms of level `J(𝔟)` on `Ỹ^m_0`, where the half `true` of the
  last path starts; `𝔟` is generated by `New.Data.gridLevelGen`.
* `New.Data.levelY ϑ m`: the level `J(𝔪₀)` on `Y_m`, where `𝔪₀` is the product of the chosen places
  and `Q`.
* `New.weylGauge κ e g v`: the largest `p`-adic absolute value of a coordinate of `g⁻¹ v`.
* `New.weylNormSq v`: the squared norm of `v` for the integral Gram matrix of the Weyl module.
* `New.Data.lowerChain ϑ`: the chain of lifts, that is the composite of the `m` theta lifts from
  `Y₀` to `Y_m`, with values in algebraic forms. `New.Data.lowerChainAtLevel ϑ` is the same map with
  values in the forms of the last level and its character; `levelY ϑ m` fixes these forms.

modules.title: Point forms, Hecke adjoints and false lifts on the definite space of a descent pair
modules.note:
This file studies algebraic forms on the definite space `V = I_n` of a descent pair `O`
(`New.DescentPair`). The pair gives a space `W` of rank `r`, an embedding `O.incl` of `r` into `n`,
and places indexed by `O.ChosenIndex` (the set M of chosen places) and `O.TwistIndex` (the set Q of
the twist). For each `σ ∈ Aut ℂ`, `New.LevelPlaces.LevelForm.innerAt σ` is `σ⁻¹` of the inner
product of the `σ`-conjugates of two forms. Point forms, supported on one class, have explicit inner
