products and descents, and the Hecke polynomial `H_w(X)` at a split place has an explicit adjoint
for these pairings. Let `Z` (in use, the space of lifts) lie in the image of a central idempotent
`e₀` and be killed by `H_w(X_*)`, where `X_* = O.liftHeckeRoot w`. On forms orthogonal to the false
lifts, the orthogonal projection (for `σ = 1`) to `Z` does not increase the norm at any `σ`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Rows.IsPointLift`, `New.Rows.exists_isPointLift`, `New.Rows.pointLift`: an element `A` of the
  integral level with prescribed columns at `O.ChosenIndex` and rows at `O.TwistIndex`.
* `New.Rows.pointForm`: the point form at `h A`; `New.Rows.inner_pointForm` and
  `New.Rows.normalizedDescent_pointForm` compute its inner products and its descent
  `New.DescentPair.normalizedDescent`, whose finite datum is `New.Rows.pointFormDatum`.
* `New.LevelPlaces.LevelForm.innerAt_heckePolyOnForms` computes the adjoint of `H_w(X)` for the
  pairing `innerAt σ`.
* `New.DescentPair.falseLiftsAt`, `New.DescentPair.IsOrthogonalToFalseLifts`,
  `New.DescentPair.IsTestForm`: false lifts, the forms orthogonal to them, and the integral ones
  among these for a fixed `e₀` and `Z = ker O.normalizedDescent`.
* `New.Selmer.DenominatorLe`: a bound on the ℓ-adic denominator of the projection to a subspace Z.
* `New.DescentPair.normSqAt_starProjection_le`: on forms orthogonal to the false lifts the
  projection to Z does not increase the norm at σ.

Notions from other files:
* `New.DescentPair`: A descent pair: places M and Q, a space W of rank r with numbered basis
  vectors, an embedding of the index set r into the larger index set n, weights k⁺ and k⁻, and a
  character μ whose tame part is trivial off these places.
* `New.DescentPair.FormV`: the algebraic forms on V = I_n with the weight, level and character of
  the pair; the level sits at two finite sets of split places, M and Q.
* `New.DescentPair.heckePolyOnForms`: the operator H_w(X) = ∑_i (−X)^i q^{i(i−1)/2} T_{w,i} on
  forms, for a split place w that, with its conjugate, is off M and Q;
  `New.DescentPair.liftHeckeRoot` w is the value X_* at which it is taken.
* `New.DescentPair.normalizedDescent`: the descent, a linear map from forms Ξ on V to functions on
  U(W)(𝔸): its value at g is the class sum over h, for `New.DescentPair.levelGroup`, of
  `New.DescentPair.conjKernel` at g and h applied to Ξ(h). It is adjoint to the lift from W
  (`New.DescentPair.inner_thetaLift`).
* `New.LevelPlaces.placeAt`: the chosen places and the places of Q as one family, indexed by
  `O.ChosenIndex ⊕ O.TwistIndex`.

modules.title: The cost of one lift: a height bound for Z_j(1)/Z_j(ξ^j)
modules.note:
The comparison operators `U_ϑ = n_Aut hk² glue_ϑ glue_ϑ*` take lifts to forms orthogonal to the
false lifts. A tight frame of integral tuples writes them as sums of operators of rank one, so they
keep integrality away from `Q` and `U_1` is short (`IsComparisonOperator`). The product
`Z_j (ϑ) det (pr U_ϑ)` depends on the twist `ϑ` only through Hecke values. Eigenvalue bounds control
the denominator of `det (pr U_ϑ)` at `ι` and the conjugates of `det (pr U_1)`; this bounds the
height of `Z_j (1) / Z_j (ξ_ι ^ j)`, for m-fold twists `ξ_ι`.

Notions from other files:
* `D : Data P` fixes a CM field `E = D.E`, weights at its infinite places, a level, and the ranks:
  `m = D.m` lifts, from hermitian spaces `W_j = D.spaceW j` (`1 ≤ j ≤ m`) of rank `r = D.r` to the
  standard definite space `V_j` of rank `r + t`, where `t = D.t = 5 r`. The datum of the lift at a
  twist `ϑ` is `D.descentPair ϑ j`, and its `FormV` is the space of forms on `V_j`.
* `D.goodLift ϑ j` is the lift at the twist `ϑ` on the good forms on `W_j` (the range of the
  idempotent `D.e₀`), with values in the forms on `V_j`. `D.liftDeterminant ξ j`, written
  `Z_j (ξ ^ j)` for an m-fold twist `ξ`, is, at `ϑ = ξ ^ j`, the Gram determinant of this lift.
* `IsOrthogonalToFalseLifts O D.e₀ Z φ` says that the form `φ` is orthogonal to the false lifts: the
  forms that satisfy the conditions on a lift from `D.e₀` and lie in `Z`, here the complement of the
  lifts.
* `glue j ϑ` is the gluing map `glue_ϑ` from tuples of forms on `V°` (`FormTuples j`) to forms on
  `V_j`; `periodLift j` is `twistFactor j 1` times its adjoint after the lift, at the trivial twist.
  Here `V°` is the standard definite space with basis `D.SecondFactorIndex`.
* `heckeValueProd j ϑ` is a product of three real numbers `Exchange.lValueProd` (norms of places
  times squared moduli of partial Hecke `L`-values at integers), for the three characters of
  `exchangePair j` twisted by `ϑ` or its inverse.
modules.literature:
Bounding the norm of a lift by an integral form and a congruence denominator is known in the
literature for one eigenform.

Related work: Böcherer–Dummigan–Schulze-Pillot, Yoshida lifts and Selmer groups, 2012; X. Zhang,
Special L-values and Selmer groups of Siegel modular forms of genus 2, 2018; Hida, Congruences of
cusp forms and special values of their zeta functions, 1981.

modules.title: One exchange, and class sums at the level of a row stabilizer
modules.note:
The exchange identity compares class sums of theta kernels on a definite space `E^n` with integrals
over `[U(V')]`. For `W = E^b ⊕ W'` and an invariant datum it confines the twist to the kernel of
`(V', E^b)`, two spaces of equal rank. (`E^b` is the standard definite space with basis indexed by
`b`.) If `F` is invariant under a row stabilizer, the datum is a product for `z` in the stabilizer,
and the class sum at full level unfolds to the class sum of this product at the level of the
stabilizer.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Rows.rowStabilizer`: the invertible A with the columns of 1 off e and w · φ(A) = w.
* `New.Rows.columnDatum`: the factor that depends only on the columns e.
* `New.Rows.columnDatum_mul_ite_eq_ite_mem_rowStabilizer`: for F left invariant under
  `New.Rows.rowStabilizer`, the function χ(det z) F(z⁻¹ y), cut down to z in the stabilizer, is a
  product.
* `New.Rows.integrable_and_mul_stdClassSum_eq_integral_mul`: from the exchange identity for matched
  data on `E^b ⊕ W'`, with the constant `c`: for an invariant datum `Ψ'`, `c` times the class sum
  of the kernel of `χ (det x'') Ψ' (x''⁻¹ x')` is the integral of the kernel of `(V', E^b)` with
  datum `χ ∘ det` times the kernel of `(V', W')` with datum `Ψ'`.
  `New.Rows.mul_stdClassSum_eq_integral_mul_modKernel` sums this over the classes of `U(E^b)`.
* `New.Rows.stdClassSum_rowStabilizer_eq`: a class sum at full level equals a class sum at the level
  of a row stabilizer, with a datum supported on matrices of a special shape.

Notions from other files:
* `New.AutChar`: an automorphic circle-valued character of U(1)(𝔸). `HasWeight` e ψ gives its
  exponents e at the infinite places and its tame parts ψ at the finite places.
* `New.modKernelStdSpace` W α β 𝔪 Ψ P g h: the theta kernel of the pair of W and the standard
  definite space, with the twisting characters α and β, the datum Ψ modulo 𝔪 and the polynomial P,
  at the adelic point g and at the point with real part 1 and finite part h.
* `New.stdLevel`: the level K₀, the stabilizer of the standard lattice.
* `New.Fock.polyVector` ε P: the Fock vector P(ζ(x)) exp(-|x|²/2), where ζ conjugates the
  coordinates of positive sign. For a pair with signs s and t, `homSigns` s t gives the products of
  the signs as those of the coordinates, and `realSigns` repeats them at every infinite place.
* `New.Modulus`: a modulus, a nonzero ideal 𝔪 of O_E prime to its complex conjugate, that is, never
  divisible by both w and w̄; `New.Modulus.ResidueRing` is the residue ring O_E/𝔪.
* `New.Exchange.IsTameFor`: `IsTameFor 𝔪 ν e χ` says that 𝔪 ≠ (1), that ν has weight e and that its
  tame part is ramified exactly at the places dividing 𝔪 and gives the character χ modulo 𝔪.
* `New.Rows.liftMod`: a chosen lift of g ∈ GL_n(O_E/𝔪) to K₀, with component 1 outside the places
  dividing 𝔪 and their conjugates.
* `New.Space` E n s: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸)
  with xᴴJx equal to diag(s) at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.G` E s: the adelic unitary group G = G_∞ × G_f for signs s at the infinite places and the
  identity matrix at the finite places; `New.Gf` E n is G_f.

modules.title: Gluing: residue rings, divided lattices, the congruence group and glued lattices
modules.note:
This file sets up the change of lattice at the chosen places for a divided splitting
`V : New.Rows.DividedSplitting N m a O z` of `V = V″ ⊕ V°`. It introduces the residue rings
modulo `ϖ²` and `ϖ²Q`, the conjugate kernel vector and the kernel summed over classes. It then
defines divided lattices, the congruence group of matrices that are `1` modulo `ϖ`, and product
forms. It constructs, for every matrix `s` modulo `ϖ²`, a lattice glued for `s`, and writes the
datum of the lift at `γ⁻¹ x` as a sum over the congruence group.

Here `O` is a descent pair with the space `W = O.W` of rank `r`. `N` indexes `V″`, `m` indexes
`V°`, `z : r ↪ m` marks `r` basis vectors of `V°`, and `a` indexes the rows of a matrix `s` modulo
`ϖ²`, the linear forms on `V″` on which a finer congruence is imposed. The idele `ϖ = O.genIdele`
generates the product of the chosen places `O.chosenPlace i`, and `Q` is the product of the places
`O.twistPlace i`. We write `(1; 0)` for an inclusion matrix `New.inclMatrix` with `r` columns.
The datum of the theta lift from `W` to `V` asks for `x ≡ (1; 0)` modulo `ϖ`. A product datum asks
for conditions modulo `ϖ²` on the two blocks of `x`. The lattice that connects them is spanned by
the columns of the matrix that is `(1; 0)` on both summands, by `L″_s = {u | s u ≡ 0 modulo ϖ}` in
`V″` and by `ϖ` times the standard lattice of `V°`. The matrix of a basis is called `γ`, and it is
handled through the integral matrix `ϖ γ⁻¹`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Rows.DividedLattice`, `New.Rows.DividedLattice.reducedInverse`: a point `γ` of G_f supported
  at the chosen places such that `ϖ γ⁻¹` is integral, and the reduction of `ϖ γ⁻¹` modulo `ϖ²`.
* `New.Rows.DividedSplitting.congruenceGroup`: the invertible `r × r` matrices modulo `ϖ²` that are
  `1` modulo `ϖ`.
* `New.Rows.DividedSplitting.productForm`: the form supported on the class of `(h, h°) γ` with the
  product of two vectors as its value. The product of vectors is `New.Rows.cartanProduct`.
* The datum. `New.Rows.DividedSplitting.exists_isGlued`: for every `s` there is a lattice glued for
  `s`. `New.Rows.DividedSplitting.IsGlued.indicator_eq_sum`: the datum of the lift at `γ⁻¹ x` is the
  sum of the translates of the product datum under the congruence group.

Notions from other files:
* `New.DescentPair`: A descent pair: chosen places and twist places, a space W of rank r with
  numbered basis vectors, an embedding of indices into n > r, two diagrams given by their numbers of
  columns of each height, and a character μ whose tame part, a character `O.tamePart w` of the
  residue field at each place w, is trivial off these places.
* `New.LevelPlaces.levelModulus`: `levelModulus c` is the modulus ϖ^c·Q, and `levelModulus c false`
  is ϖ^c.
* `New.inclMatrix`: For a map u: m → n of index sets, the n×m matrix whose j-th column is the
  standard basis vector e_{u(j)}.
* `New.Rows.liftMod`: A chosen lift of an invertible matrix modulo an ideal to an integral point of
  G_f that is 1 outside the places dividing the ideal and their conjugates.

modules.title: Gluing: the descent of product forms and the denominators
modules.note:
This file treats forms on the definite space `V = V″ ⊕ V°` glued, in
`New.OneLift.ComparisonOperator.GluedLattices`, from a vector for `V″` and a vector for `V°`
across a change of lattice at the chosen places.

The data are a descent pair `O` (`New.DescentPair`), with the space `W = O.W` of rank `r`, and a
splitting `V : New.Rows.DividedSplitting N m a O z`. Here `N` indexes `V″`, `m` indexes `V°`,
`z : r ↪ m` marks `r` basis vectors of `V°`, and `a` indexes the rows of a matrix `s` modulo `ϖ²`,
the linear forms on `V″` on which a finer congruence is imposed. The idele `ϖ = O.genIdele`
generates the product of the chosen places `O.chosenPlace i`, and `Q` is the product of the places
`O.twistPlace i`. We write `(1; 0)` for an inclusion matrix `New.inclMatrix` with `r` columns.

The datum of the theta lift from `W` to `V` asks for `x ≡ (1; 0)` modulo `ϖ`. A product datum asks
for conditions modulo `ϖ²` on the two blocks of `x`. The lattice that connects them is spanned by
the columns of the matrix that is `(1; 0)` on both summands, by `L″_s = {u | s u ≡ 0 modulo ϖ}` in
`V″` and by `ϖ` times the standard lattice of `V°`. The matrix of a basis is called `γ`, and it is
handled through the integral matrix `ϖ γ⁻¹`.

This file computes the descent to `W` of product forms on a glued lattice, from which the slices
of a lift are read off. It also bounds the p-adic gauge of the Cartan product at the point
`(h, h') γ`.

## Main definitions and results

* Slices of lifts. `New.Rows.DividedSplitting.normalizedDescent_productForm`: if `V.IsGlued s L` and
  `b * b' = O.charV`, the descent to `W` of a product form is the complex conjugate of the product
  of `L.weilScalar` with a sum over the congruence group, whose terms are products of a kernel on
  `V″` and one on `V°`. `New.Rows.DividedSplitting.normalizedDescent_stdClassSum_productForm`: the
  same for the sum of product forms over the classes, with `New.Rows.kernelClassSum` on `V″`.
* The denominators. `New.Rows.DividedSplitting.weylGauge_cartanProduct_le`: for a glued lattice, a
  natural number `M ≠ 0` divisible by `ϖ` and points `h`, `h'` on the two summands, the gauge of
  the product of two vectors at the point `(h, h') γ` (with `(h, h')` made block diagonal along
  `V.ε : N ⊕ m ≃ n`) is at most `‖M‖⁻¹ ^ V.denominatorExponent` times their gauges.

Notions from other files:
* `New.DescentPair`: A descent pair: chosen places and twist places, a space W of rank r with
  numbered basis vectors, an embedding of indices into n > r, two diagrams given by their numbers of
  columns of each height, and a character μ whose tame part, a character `O.tamePart w` of the
  residue field at each place w, is trivial off these places.
* `New.LevelPlaces.levelModulus`, `New.Rows.liftMod`: `levelModulus c` is the modulus ϖ^c·Q, and
  `levelModulus c false` is ϖ^c. `liftMod` is a chosen lift of an invertible matrix modulo an
  ideal to an integral point of G_f that is 1 outside the places dividing the ideal and their
  conjugates.
* `New.inclMatrix`: For a map u: m → n of index sets, the n×m matrix whose j-th column is the
  standard basis vector e_{u(j)}.
* `New.modKernel`: The theta kernel at (g, h) of the datum given by a function on matrices modulo an
  ideal and the Fock vector of a polynomial.
* `New.WeylIndex`: `WeylIndex n κ` indexes the standard basis of the vectors of weight κ in n
  letters. Here `κ τ h` is the number of columns of height h at the infinite place τ.

modules.title: Data of the three exchanges: the carrier, the choices and the functions 𝖥_i
modules.note:
For admissible data `D`, the element `ϖ = New.Data.piM` of 𝓞_E generates the product of the primes
at the places `New.Data.chosenPlace`. The file defines the objects of the three exchanges that turn
a twist into a number on `W_j = New.Data.spaceW`, `1 ≤ j ≤ m`: the carrier φ° with its coefficients
𝖺, the modulus `ϖ^c`, the index sets of the spaces, the characters, the choices `i`, the fixed
polynomial `P` and the functions `𝖥_i`.

The standard definite space `E^n` is also written `I_n`, and `υ = New.WeilData.upsilonU1` is the
character `ν_η` of weight 1 and trivial tame part. The letter `ϑ` denotes a tame character
(`New.Data.TameChar`); it is a twist only where this is said.

| object | Lean name | object | Lean name |
|---|---|---|---|
| `S = E^{2m,m}` | `CarrierIndex` | `χ′` | `twistedChiMPow` |
| `W♭ = E^{6m+1}` | `FlatIndex` | `ν″` | `firstFactorChar` |
| `V″`, `W′` | `FirstFactorIndex` | `ν♭ υ^m` | `carrierChar` |
| `V°` | `SecondFactorIndex` | `φ°`, `𝖺 χ′` | `carrierForm`, `carrierCoeff` |
| columns of `μ⁺`, plus Δ′ indices | `DetIndex` | `P`, `𝖥_i` | `paddedMinorProd`, `choiceFn` |
| choices `i` | `ChoiceIndex` | `u`, `u°` | `conjHolomorphicWeight`, `kernelWeight` |

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Rows.carrierForm`: the carrier φ°, the theta lift of the constant function from the unitary
  group of a negative definite space to that of a space with signs `+1` on `2 m` and `−1` on `m`
  coordinates.
* `New.Rows.carrierCoeff`: the coefficients 𝖺 times a character, a class sum of theta kernels
  between two definite spaces.
* `New.Data.choiceFn`: the function `𝖥_i` on `U(W_j)`, the integral of the carrier against a theta
  kernel.
* `New.Data.isTameFor_of_hasWeight`, `New.Data.isTameFor_twistedChiMPow`: let `ϑ` be a twist,
  `c ≠ 0`, and take a character whose tame part is `ψ * ϑ.tamePart`, with `ψ` non-trivial exactly at
  the chosen places. It ramifies exactly at the places dividing `D.twistModulus ϑ c`, that is, the
  chosen places and the places in `ϑ.Q` (`New.Exchange.IsTameFor`). This applies to
  `New.Data.twistedChiMPow`.
* `New.Rows.exists_int_weylRep_invariant_fockPoly_eq_smul_monomial`: for a monomial of the right
  degrees there is an integral vector whose Fock polynomial is a nonzero multiple of the monomial.
  The vector is fixed by the elements that act trivially on the rows of the monomial.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Modulus`: a nonzero ideal of 𝓞_E that is never divisible by both a place w and its conjugate
  w̄.
* `New.Data.spaceW`: the diagonal hermitian space `W_j` of rank r over E with signs `D.signsW j`.
* `New.Data.liftWeight`: the natural number `κ_j`, a function of the infinite place; the character
  `New.Data.liftChar` of the `j`-th lift has weight `−κ_j`.
* The numbers of `D`: the rank `r` of `W_j`, the number `m` of lifts, `k = r + 1 − m`, `t = 5 r`,
  the gap `Δ = New.Data.gap = 2 r ^ 8` and `Δ′ = New.Data.reducedHalfGap = Δ / 2 − (t + 1) / 2`.
* `New.Data.descentPair`: the data (`New.DescentPair`) of the lift from `W_j` to `I_{r+t}`. They
  include a `numbering` of the basis vectors of `W_j` and, at each infinite place, two partitions
  `μ⁺`, `μ⁻` given by their numbers `colsPlus`, `colsMinus` of columns of each height.
* `New.Data.TameChar`, `New.Data.Twist`: a character of U(1)(𝔸) of weight 0 whose tame part is
  trivial outside a finite set Q of places; it is a twist if the tame part is non-trivial on all of
  Q.

## Use in the argument

* The carrier φ° and the coefficients 𝖺: the class sum of a twisted square kernel against 𝖺 is a
  multiple of φ°. See `New.OneLift.ComparisonOperator.ThreeExchanges`.
* Moduli, index sets, polynomial and functions `𝖥_i`: the third exchange and its left side as a
  theta series. See `New.OneLift.ComparisonOperator.ThreeExchanges` and
  `New.OneLift.ComparisonOperator.FirstFactors`.
* Order, weights and gaps on `W_j`: the functions `𝖥_i` separate good forms. See
  `New.OneLift.ComparisonOperator.ProductsSpan`.
* Integral vectors with a monomial Fock polynomial: the height bound for inverse ratios of twisted
  to untwisted Hecke L-values. See `New.OneLift.HeckeValues.TwistedValueHeights`.

modules.title: Products of determinants and first-column coordinates under substitution
modules.note:
This file studies polynomials in the entries of variable matrices `x_τ`, one for each `τ : Φ`, with
rows indexed by `N` and columns by `L`. It studies how these polynomials transform under the
two-sided linear substitutions `New.Rows.twoSidedSubst`, `x_τ ↦ c_τᵀ x_τ g_τᵀ`. It treats products
of determinants of constant matrices stacked over `x_τ`. It also treats the coordinates of a
polynomial in its first `p` columns, where `p` is a number of columns.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Rows.stackedDetProd`, `New.Rows.twoSidedSubst_stackedDetProd`: a product of determinants of
  constant matrices stacked over `x_τ` (`New.Rows.stackedDet`). The substitution sends the product
  for the matrices `M τ k * (g τ)ᵀ` to a scalar multiple of the product for the matrices `M τ k`.
* `New.Rows.firstColsCoord`, `New.Rows.twoSidedSubst_firstColsCoord`: the coordinates of a
  polynomial in its first `p` columns; if the substitution with column matrices
  `fromBlocks 1 0 0 (g τ)` (fixing the first `p` columns) sends `F'` to a multiple of `F`, the
  coordinates of `F'` and `F` are related by the Schur matrix (`New.schur`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.nablaBasis`, `New.schur`: products of minors indexed by families of standard fillings
  (`New.WeylIndexFamily`), and the matrix of a substitution of rows in these polynomials.

modules.title: Decay of Fock matrix coefficients, sparse theta sums and the isolation estimate
modules.note:
This file holds the estimates behind the theorem that products span. The Heisenberg matrix
coefficients of a homogeneous Fock vector decay faster than any power. So in a theta sum over a
sparse lattice the term of `0` dominates, and a mean over additive characters produces such a sum.
Bounds for integrals of matrix coefficients of holomorphic discrete series then give the isolation
estimate `New.Data.norm_apply_one_le_of_forall_isPeak`, the last step of the proof: the mean over a
circle of peaks.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Fock.norm_fockInner_realHeisenbergOp_le`: the decay of the coefficient `⟨v, ϱ(y) ω(σ) v⟩` in
  `y`.
* `New.Rows.firstMinimum_mul_le_hom`: the first minimum of `Hom (S, T)` is bounded below by the
  product of the first minima of `S` and `T`, up to an explicit constant.
* `New.Rows.exists_norm_modKernel_sub_fockInner_le`: for a suitable finite datum `Ψ` modulo `𝔪`, the
  theta kernel at real translates of `(g, h)` differs from a Fock matrix coefficient by a small
  error if the lattice of `Hom (S, T)` has no short vectors.
* `New.Data.integral_norm_holMinorsPi_mul_pow_le`: the integral of the basic function of a weight
  with a large gap against a power of the norm, compared with a squared `L²` norm.
* `New.Data.norm_apply_one_le_of_forall_isPeak`: let a bounded function `K₀` be close, for every
  peak of a holomorphic `F`, to a holomorphic `K` whose weighted integral against the translate of
  `F` vanishes. Then `K₀ 1` is small.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Fock.fockSpace`: The Fock space: integrable functions c on ℂ^ι with c(x) = ∫ c(y)β(y,x)e(x−y)
  dy, β the Heisenberg bicharacter, e the Gaussian exp(−|x|²/2), under the L¹ norm.
* `New.Fock.fockInner`: The bounded sesquilinear form on the Fock space, conjugate-linear in the
  first variable, (c, c′) ↦ ∫ c̄ c′.
* `New.Space`: a hermitian space with a point, given by a matrix J over E and x in GL_n(𝔸) with xᴴJx
  equal to the diagonal matrix of its signs at the infinite places and 1 at the finite places.
* `New.GInf`: The archimedean unitary group G_∞ for signs s: one copy of the complex unitary group
  U(diag s) for each infinite place of E.
* `New.IsPosFirstOrder`: The order o has distinct values and puts every index of sign +1 before
  every index of sign −1.
* `New.Space.vecAtPoint`: the adelic vector x⁻¹y of a rational vector y at the point x of a space;
  the lattice `New.Space.baseLattice` consists of the y for which it has integral finite part.
* `New.realCoord`: the Fock coordinates of an adelic vector: its components at the infinite places
  τ, times √(2π Im τ(j)), with j the element fixed by the Weil data.
modules.literature:
See `New.OneLift.ComparisonOperator.ProductsSpan` for related work. See
`Lib.Weil.DualPair.ThetaLiftConvergence` and `Lib.Adelic.Reduction.FiniteVolume` for sources.

modules.title: The polynomial map ζ, the datum Ψ^add and the series Υ; norm, degree and denominator of ζ
modules.note:
Fix admissible data `D`, a tame character `ϑ` and an index `1 ≤ j ≤ m`. Write `E^n` for the standard
definite space of rank `n`, V″ for the one on `New.Data.FirstFactorIndex` and
W^add = E^{3m−j} ⊕ W♭ ⊕ E^{3m} for the one on `New.Data.AddedIndex`. Throughout, k = `D.k`,
m = `D.m`, M = `D.M`, and W_j is the space on `D.RowIndex` with r₊ = `D.posRank j` = k + j − 1 plus
signs. This file defines the constant rows 𝖼, the datum Ψ^add and the series Υ, which is built from
theta kernels of definite spaces. It also defines the polynomial map ζ to the Weyl module of μ⁺ with
P_V = P_{ζ(z)}(X). Here P_V has one determinant det(𝖼; X z) for each column of μ⁺, with variables X
in the positive basis vectors of W_j and variables z in W^add. This file bounds the norm, the degree
and the denominator of ζ.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.HasWeightNormSqLe`, `New.HasWeightNormSqLeIf`: "F has weight κ and squared norm at most b",
  outright or under a condition. Under finite products the weights add and the bounds multiply.
* `New.Data.constantRows`, `New.Data.stackedDetProdCoords`: the matrices 𝖼 of 2m constant rows, one
  for each column of μ⁺ at each infinite place (`New.Data.DetIndex`), and the coordinates of ζ.
* `New.Data.addedDatum`, `New.Data.leftSideSeries`: the datum Ψ^add on W^add and the series Υ.
* `New.Data.toPoly_stackedDetProdCoords`, `New.Data.weylNormSq_comp_eval_stackedDetProdCoords_le`:
  P_V is the polynomial of ζ, and when the entries of Y and the values of z are small, the squared
  norm of ζ(z) is bounded.
* `New.Data.exists_isHomogeneousOverEntries_smul_stackedDetProdCoords`: ζ is homogeneous of one
  degree `d`, and one integer `H ≤ (d ^ d) ^ 3` clears its denominators.

Notions from other files:
* `New.toPoly`, `New.weylNormSq`: the polynomial of a coordinate vector of weight κ, and the squared
  norm of the vector for the Gram matrix of κ. Here `κ τ h` counts the columns of height `h` at `τ`.
* `New.Data.DetIndex`: the columns of μ⁺ at the place τ. The number of those of height h < r₊ is
  `(untwistedDescentPair j).colsPlus τ h`, and Δ′ = `D.reducedHalfGap` have height r₊.
* `New.Data.FirstFactorIndex`: the indices of W_j, (E^j)⁻, E^{3m−j} and W♭ = E^{6m+1}.
* `New.Data.ChoiceIndex`: the choices, each a matrix Λ modulo ϖ² with a class h♭ of U(W♭) and rows
  for the columns of height r₊ (`New.Data.RowChoice`).
* `New.Data.TameChar`, `New.Data.twistModulus`: a character `ϑ` of U(1)(𝔸) of weight 0 with tame
  part on a finite set Q = `ϑ.Q` of places, and the moduli ϖ^c Q.

modules.title: The first factors: P_V along W_j and W^add, integrality and size
modules.note:
Fix admissible data `D`, a tame character `ϑ` and an index `1 ≤ j ≤ m`. Write `E^n` for
the standard definite space of rank `n`, V″ for the one on `New.Data.FirstFactorIndex` and
W^add = E^{3m−j} ⊕ W♭ ⊕ E^{3m} for the one on `New.Data.AddedIndex`. Throughout, k = `D.k`,
m = `D.m`, M = `D.M`, and W_j is the space on `D.RowIndex` with r₊ = `D.posRank j` = k + j − 1
plus signs. This file writes P_V as a sum of products of a polynomial in X and a coordinate of
ζ(z), where X are the variables in the positive basis vectors of W_j and z those in W^add. Each
value of Υ is a double class sum of products of three theta kernels of definite spaces, and this
file bounds these kernels. By `New.Data.exists_isIntegralAndSmall_leftSideSeries`, for one constant
`c″ ≠ 0` the first factors φ″, the complex conjugates of c″Υ, are integral away from the norm of Q
and, if Q is empty, all their images under automorphisms of ℂ are small
(`New.Data.IsIntegralAndSmall`).

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.renameRowsCols_stackedDetProd_eq_sum`: P_V as a sum of products of a polynomial in X and
  a coordinate of ζ(z).
* `New.Data.exists_isIntegralAndSmall_leftSideSeries`: for 1 ≤ j ≤ m there is one c ≠ 0, independent
  of i, ϑ and h, such that every first factor y = conj (c · Υ) is integral and small in the sense of
  `New.Data.IsIntegralAndSmall`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.toPoly`, `New.weylNormSq`: the polynomial of a coordinate vector of weight κ, and the squared
  norm of the vector for the Gram matrix of κ. Here `κ τ h` counts the columns of height `h` at `τ`.
* `New.Data.FirstFactorIndex`: the indices of W_j, (E^j)⁻, E^{3m−j} and W♭ = E^{6m+1}.
* `New.Data.TameChar`, `New.Data.twistModulus`: a character `ϑ` of U(1)(𝔸) of weight 0 with tame
  part on a finite set Q = `ϑ.Q` of places, and the moduli ϖ^c Q.
* `New.Data.stackedDetProdCoords`: the coordinates of the polynomial map ζ.
* `New.Data.leftSideSeries`: the series Υ, built from theta kernels of definite spaces.
modules.literature:
The first factors enter the comparison of twisted theta forms on U(W_j) with twist-free ones,
`New.Data.exists_mul_thirdExchangeLeftSide_eq_choiceFn` in
`New.OneLift.ComparisonOperator.ThreeExchanges`: for every twist, an explicit theta form times a
number is a twist-free function, and the squared modulus of the number is a constant independent of
the twist divided by a product of squared Hecke L-values and powers of norms of places. This file
proves that the first factors are integral off the conductor and small when untwisted. The rank one
case (the lift is a scalar of square modulus an L-value), twisting on a square block and integral
theta data are known in the literature. Related work: T. Yang, Theta liftings and Hecke L-functions,
1997; Böcherer–Schmidt, p-adic measures attached to Siegel modular forms, 2000; Harris–Li–Skinner,
The Rallis inner product formula and p-adic L-functions, 2005.

modules.title: Three exchanges: the carrier, the third exchange and its left side as a theta series
modules.note:
The exchange identity (`New.Rows.exists_mul_stdClassSum_eq_integral_modKernel`) is applied three
times, until only a number is left of the twist. The first two exchanges evaluate a class sum of
twisted square kernels on the space S of signature (2m, m) as a multiple of the carrier φ° =
`New.Rows.carrierForm`, the theta lift of the constant function 1 from the definite group U(0, m) to
U(S). The third exchange equates a multiple of a double class sum of kernels with 𝖥_i =
`New.Data.choiceFn j i`, the function on U(W_j) given by the integral of the carrier against a theta
kernel. The modulus of the product of the three constants is given by the product Γ_j of Hecke
values at three pairs (ν, z) of a character and an integer.

Letters: the twist is ϑ, υ = `upsilonU1` is the splitting character on U(1), and I_m = E^m is the
standard definite space of rank m.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.exchangePair`: three pairs for each `1 ≤ j ≤ m`, indexed by `none` and the two signs.
* `New.Data.heckeValueProd`: the product `Γ_j` of the values `Exchange.lValueProd` at the inverses
  of the characters of these pairs, twisted by a tame character or its inverse. It is not divided by
  its value at the trivial twist.
* `New.Rows.exists_mul_stdClassSum_eq_carrierForm`, from the first two exchanges: for even `m` and a
  character c of weight 0 that is tame for (𝔪, χ), the carrier is a constant γ of known size times a
  class sum of `New.Rows.carrierCoeff` times a theta kernel twisted by χ∘det.
* `New.Rows.carrierForm_mem_rapidOfLevel_and_isAdelicHol`: for even `m`, if there is a tame
  character of weight 0, the carrier lies in `New.Rows.rapidOfLevel` for every level. So it has full
  level and is rapidly decreasing. It is also holomorphic.
* `New.Data.exists_mul_thirdExchangeLeftSide_eq_choiceFn`,
  `New.Data.thirdExchangeLeftSide_eq_kernelClassSum`: a number times a double class sum of kernels
  is 𝖥_i, and this double sum is a theta series on U(W_j).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.chiM`, `New.Data.chiMLocal`: a fixed character χ of U(1)(𝔸) of weight 0 and its tame
  part ω, which is trivial off the chosen places and has order greater than 8m at each of them.
* `New.Data.goodForms`: The good forms on V: the image of the idempotent e₀ of ℂ[𝖦] acting on forms
  of principal level at the chosen places above p₀ and p₁.
* `New.Data.signsW`: Signs ±1 on the indices i in `New.Data.RowIndex` for W_j: −1 when
  `New.Data.basisNumber`(i) ≥ `New.Data.posRank` j, and +1 otherwise.
* `New.Rows.IsAdelicHol`: For every adelic g, the function h ↦ F(g·(h,1)) on the archimedean group
  is holomorphic of the given weight for the given order (`New.IsHolOfWeight`).
* `New.Data.kernelWeight`: The weight `New.staircaseWeight` on W_j for the pair (W_j, V°).
modules.literature:
The twisted theta kernel of an indefinite and a definite unitary group of equal rank, summed against
an explicit form, is a non-zero multiple of one fixed non-zero holomorphic, rapidly decreasing form
of level one, for even m. The factor has modulus given by Hecke L-values, so the twist survives only
as a number. Non-vanishing and holomorphy of the stable-range theta lift of a character are known in
the literature. Related work: J.-S. Li, Non-vanishing theorems for the cohomology of certain
arithmetic quotients, 1992; Gan–Qiu–Takeda, The regularized Siegel–Weil formula, 2014; T. Yang,
Theta liftings and Hecke L-functions, 1997.

The theta kernel of two definite unitary groups of the same even rank 2e with determinant data,
summed over the classes of one group, is a non-zero constant whose modulus, up to a fixed factor and
conductor norms, is a product of Hecke L-values at 1,…,e. This is the first step in turning the
twist into a number. It is Rallis's formula at equal rank 2e for a character, whose central value
folds by the functional equation into Hecke L-values at 1,…,e and a conductor power, with the
ramified local data computed explicitly. Related work: Yamana, L-functions and theta correspondence
for classical groups, 2014; C. Li, Geometric and arithmetic theta correspondences (§2.4–2.5), 2024;
Yang, Theta liftings and Hecke L-functions, 1997.

See `New.OneLift.ComparisonOperator.FirstFactors` and `New.OneLift.ComparisonOperator.ProductsSpan`
for related work.

modules.title: Products span
modules.note:
For admissible data D (`New.Data`) and 1 ≤ j ≤ m, let 𝖥_i = `New.Data.choiceFn j i` be the functions
on the unitary group of W_j = `New.Data.spaceW j`, one for each choice i, and let θ° be the theta
kernel of (W_j, V°). A good form (`New.Data.goodForms`) is a form of principal level at the chosen
places in the image of the idempotent `New.Data.e₀`. We show that a good form y on W_j with
∫ y(g) 𝖥_i(g) θ°(g, ·) dg = 0 for all i is zero.

We write λ₁(g) for the first minimum `New.Space.firstMinimum` of the lattice at g, cut off at 1, |h|
for the largest operator norm `New.Rows.maxOpNorm` of a real point h, and m_u for the basic
holomorphic function `New.holMinorsPi` of a weight u, a quotient of products of minors. A peak
(`New.Rows.IsPeak`) of a bounded function is a point where its modulus exceeds half of the supremum.
Suppose y ≠ 0. The peaks of y are not deep in a cusp, and the proof has four steps.

1. The integral 𝖥^g of the carrier times a kernel on (S, W̃) times m_u₁ over the real group of S is
   a combination of the 𝖥_i (`New.Data.exists_sum_choiceFn_eq_integral`).
2. For every combination 𝖥 of the 𝖥_i, the integral of y 𝖥 m_u° over the real group at any point is
   zero (`New.Data.integral_mul_sum_choiceFn_eq_zero`).
3. At every peak g, 𝖥^g(g h) is close to 𝖥⁰(h), for one bounded function 𝖥⁰ with 𝖥⁰(1) ≠ 0
   (`New.Data.exists_choiceFn_approx`).
4. The mean over a circle of peaks makes 𝖥⁰(1) too small
   (`New.Data.norm_apply_one_le_of_forall_isPeak`).

Steps 1 and 3 do not involve y and come first in this file.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.exists_datum_norm_modKernel_sub_polyMatrixCoeff_le` (sparse sums): for V, V' of ranks at
  most t and Q homogeneous of degree at most b^(3/2), if λ₁(g) λ₁(g') ≥ b^(−13), then for some datum
  Ψ the theta kernel `New.modKernel` at (g h, g' h') is close to the coefficient c_Q(h, h').
* `New.Data.exists_isPeak_carrierForm`: the carrier `New.Rows.carrierForm` has a peak g₁, and
  λ₁(g₁) ≥ (5 b √b)^(−1/2).
* `New.Data.exists_choiceFn_approx`: there is a bounded F₀ with F₀(1) ≠ 0 such that, when λ₁(g) ≥ (5
  b²⁴)^(−1/2), some combination F of the 𝖥_i satisfies |F(g h) − F₀(h)| ≤ 2 b^(−19 n_*) |F₀(1)|
  |h|^(6 n_*).
* `New.Data.thetaKernelPairing`: the pairing of a form on V°, given by its values at the classes,
  with the kernel θ°.
* `New.Data.eq_zero_of_integral_choiceFn_thetaKernelPairing`: products span.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.b`: The large scale b of the data, the weight at the b-places, as a real number.
* `New.Data.nStar`: The number n_* = 2ft³, where f is the number of infinite places of E and t = 5r.
* `New.Data.SecondFactorIndex`: The index set of V°: the r indices of W_j and t − 9m − 1 − r further
  ones.
* `New.Data.CarrierIndex`: The index set of the space S of signature (2m, m).
* `New.Data.conjHolomorphicWeight`, `New.Data.kernelWeight`: The weights u of the conjugate of y and
  u° of θ° on W_j. The 𝖥_i have the weight u − u°.
modules.literature:
For a finite family of choices with small integral data, a good form on U(W_j) orthogonal to all
products of the twist-free theta forms with theta kernels of the complementary block is zero. This
makes the map Θ° on good forms injective. It is a basis problem, the spanning of a space of forms by
theta series (Eichler, The basis problem for modular forms and the traces of the Hecke operators,
1973; Waldspurger, Engendrement par des séries thêta de certains espaces de formes modulaires,
1978/79; Böcherer, Siegel modular forms and theta series, 1989). It is known that stable-range theta
kernels reach all forms, that maxima of forms avoid the cusps, and that products span for GL(2).
Related work: J.-S. Li, Non-vanishing theorems for the cohomology of certain arithmetic quotients,
1992; Poor–Yuen, Linear dependence among Siegel modular forms, 2000; Khuri-Makdisi, Moduli
interpretation of Eisenstein series, 2012.

modules.title: The first factors and the gluing maps
modules.note:
The first factors `φ″_{ϑ,i}` on `V″` are integral away from `Q` and small for `ϑ = 1`, and their
theta series satisfy `c′_ϑ Ξ_{ϑ,i} = c″ 𝖥_i` with functions `𝖥_i` that do not depend on the twist.
Gluing them to forms on `V°` gives the map `glue_ϑ` to forms on `V_j`. Its adjoint, the period,
satisfies `c′_ϑ glue_ϑ* Θ_{j,ϑ} = Θ°`, where `Θ°` does not depend on the twist and is injective,
because products span. The map `glue_ϑ` keeps integrality away from `Q`, is short for `ϑ = 1`, and
takes the image of `Θ°` to forms orthogonal to the false lifts. The comparison operator, an integer
multiple of `glue_ϑ glue_ϑ*`, is built from it in `New.OneLift.LiftVolumeHeight`.

In the code `φ″` is `firstFactor`, `Ξ` is `firstFactorPairing`, `𝖥` is `choiceFn`, `glue_ϑ` is
`glue j ϑ` and `Θ°` is `periodLift`. The integer `M` is `D.M`, its factor `ϖ` is `D.piM`, and `Q` is
the set of places of the twist `ϑ`.

Notions from other files:
* `descentPair ϑ j`: the spaces `W_j` and `V_j` with the characters and levels for the twist `ϑ`;
  `untwistedDescentPair j` is its untwisted form. The diagram of the values of the forms on `V″` is
  `μ⁺` (`colsPlus`), that on `V°` is `μ⁻` (`colsMinus`).
* `ChoiceIndex j`: the choices `i`, each a matrix `Λ` with a class `h♭` and constant rows.
* `FirstFactorIndex j` indexes the basis of `V″`, `D.SecondFactorIndex` that of `V°`, and
  `D.SecondFactorClasses` is the set of classes of `U(V°)` at the level `J (ϖ²)`.
* `goodLift ϑ j`: the theta lift `Θ_{j,ϑ}` from good forms on `W_j` to forms on `V_j`.
* `normalizedDescent`: the descent, which sends a form on `V_j` to a function on `U(W_j)` by pairing
  it with the theta kernel over the classes of `U(V_j)`.
* `weylGauge`, `weylNormSq`: the gauge at a place over `l` and the squared norm of a vector in a
  representation given by a diagram.
modules.literature:
Integral forms pairing with a lift to an explicit L-value (pullback, seesaw) are known in the
literature in low rank.

Related work: Böcherer–Dummigan–Schulze-Pillot, Yoshida lifts and Selmer groups, 2012; Y.-S. Lee,
Hida family of theta lift from U(1) to definite U(2), 2024; Prasanna, Integrality of a ratio of
Petersson norms and level-lowering congruences, 2006.

modules.title: The bottom of the tower: from the block datum to all data
modules.note:
Let `O` be a descent pair with spaces `W` and `V`, and let `y` be a form on `V` whose descents to
`W` by the data `v_P ⊗ Ψ_bl ⊗ vac` vanish, where `v_P` is the Fock vector of a polynomial `P` and
`Ψ_bl` is the block datum. Suppose that the characters `χ_w` at the places of `Q` are not trivial
and that the hyperplane sums at the chosen places annihilate `y`. This file proves that the descents
vanish for all data that are the vacuum at the finite places other than the chosen places, the
places of `Q` and their conjugates (`DescentPair.descentsVanish_of_hyperplaneSumsAnnihilate`). By
the descents of `y` we mean those of the matrix coefficient of `y` for a fixed linear form `u`.

It suffices to treat the indicator of a small class around each point `x`. If `x` has an integral
block ratio (`HasIntegralBlockRatio`) at every place of `O`, the mean of the translates of this
indicator under the level group is a multiple of a translate of `Ψ_bl` under `U(W)`. Otherwise an
annihilating row at a place where `x` has no integral block ratio gives integral elements `h_v`
(`rowShear`) that fix the components of `x` at the places of `O` and whose sum annihilates `y`.
Classes are taken modulo `i!` (`factorialIdele`) for large `i`, and the mean is taken over the
finitely many translates under the whole level group.

The pair `O` carries two families of split finite places, the chosen places and the places of `Q`,
indexed by `O.ChosenIndex` and `O.TwistIndex`. The family `O.placeAt` lists all these places, and
`O.places` is their set. The pair also carries the space `W = O.W` of rank `r`, an embedding
`O.incl : r ↪ n` and the residue characters `χ_w = O.tamePart w`. The space `V` is `stdSpace E n`,
and `O.FormV` are the forms on `V` of the level of `O`. The level group `O.levelGroup` consists of
the elements of the maximal level whose reductions fix `(1, 0)ᵀ` at the chosen places and are block
lower triangular at the places of `Q`. For an `n × r` matrix `x` we write `x'` for the square block
of the rows `O.incl` and `x''` for the block of the other rows.

The field `E` is CM and carries Weil data (`WeilData E`): a purely imaginary element, a finite idele
and a splitting character, from which the Weil representation is defined.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Space.lift` for the swapped kernel goes from `U(V)` to `U(W)`; the descent of `y` is the
  conjugate of this lift of the conjugate of `y`.
* `New.Space.schrodingerOp`: for a set `S` of split places, `schrodingerOp V S Ψ f` is the vector of
  the Weil representation with the function `Ψ` of finite adelic vectors above `S` and `f`
  elsewhere; `New.Space.integrated` sets the component at infinity, and `New.Space.vacElem` is the
  vacuum.
* `New.cosetIndicator`: `cosetIndicator S t z` is the indicator function of the `x` such that
  `t⁻¹ (x - z)` is integral at every place of `S`.
* `New.DescentPair.blockDatum` is the vector `Ψ_bl ⊗ vac`. The function `Ψ_bl` of a finite adelic
  `n × r` matrix `x` is `∏_{w ∈ Q} χ_w(det x' mod w)` if `x` is integral at all places of `O` and
  `≡ (1, 0)ᵀ` (`New.inclMatrix`) at the chosen places, and `0` otherwise.
* `New.DescentPair.formAction` is the action `s̄ y` on forms of the product of the groups `GL r`
  over the residue fields of the chosen places.

modules.title: Vanishing of theta descents from W to W plus hyperbolic planes
modules.note:
`New.SiegelWeil.DescentsVanish W V a S Y` says that all theta descents of a function `Y` on
`U(V)(𝔸)` to `U(W)(𝔸)` vanish. The descents are twisted by the character `a` of `U(1)`, with data
that are the vacuum at the places of `S` and their conjugates. This file proves the inductive step
`New.SiegelWeil.descentsVanish_add_planes`: the vanishing passes from `W` to `W'`, the sum of `W`
and hyperbolic planes, each plane multiplying `a` by `New.WeilData.upsilonU1`. This holds when `V`
is definite of large rank and `Y` is killed by a Hecke polynomial at a suitable point.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.SiegelWeil.descentsVanish_add_planes`: The inductive step of the tower of descents.
* `New.SiegelWeil.eq_zero_of_heckePolyOp_eq_zero`: Small roots: let `F` be a bounded function on
  the adelic unitary group of signs `t`, of rank `card m`, that is spherical at the split place
  `w` of norm `q`. If the Hecke polynomial at `w`, taken at a point `X` with
  `q ^ (card m + 1) * |X| ≤ 1`, kills `F`, then `F` is zero.

## The steps of the argument

* The inductive step `New.SiegelWeil.descentsVanish_add_planes`: the zero term contributes nothing
  (`New.SiegelWeil.DescentsVanish.integral_homSlice_eq_zero`), the rest is bounded
  (`New.SiegelWeil.exists_norm_theta_sub_zeroTerm_le`), the descent inherits a Hecke equation
  (`New.SiegelWeil.lift_eq_zero_of_heckePolyOp_eq_zero`), and its root is too small
  (`New.SiegelWeil.eq_zero_of_heckePolyOp_eq_zero`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.pairWeil`: the Weil representation of U(W) × U(V) on the data space 𝒮(Hom(W, V)), twisted by
  two characters of U(1); `New.Space.θ` is the theta functional on that space.
* `New.Space.projOn`: the projection whose fixed vectors are the data that are the vacuum at the
  places of a set `S` and their conjugates. For `S` the complement of the places of the level and
  their conjugates, these are the test vectors.
* `New.heckePolyOp`: the operator ∑ (−X)^i q^(i choose 2) T_{w,i}, q the order of the residue field
  at w; `New.sphericalAt π w` is the space of vectors spherical at w.
* `New.Space.Splitting`: `D : W'.Splitting W p` writes `W'` as `W` plus `card p` hyperbolic planes,
  with isotropic frame `D.k`; it is adapted (`IsBaseAdapted D`) if its adelic frames are orthonormal
  at the infinite and integral at the finite places. `D.homSource V` is the splitting of
  `Hom(W', V)` that it induces, `D.zeroTerm` is the constant term along the isotropic frame, and the
  slice `D.homSlice V x` is the zero term of the translate by `x`, a datum on `Hom(W, V)`.

modules.title: The tower of descents and the periods of false lifts
modules.note:
This file applies the inductive step of `New.OneLift.FalseLifts.HyperbolicPlaneStep` to false lifts
`Ξ` on a definite space `I_n`. Such a `Ξ` is killed by the descent `O.normalizedDescent` to `W`, by
the hyperplane sums at the chosen places, and by one Hecke polynomial. The file builds the tower of
vanishing descents to `W ⊕ ℍ^N` and deduces that the periods of `Ξ` over the block `I_l` of
`I_n = I_N ⊕ I_l` vanish, written as class sums. Here `O` is a descent pair `(W, I_n)`
(`New.DescentPair`) of ranks `r < n`. It carries two finite families of finite places, the chosen
places `O.chosenPlace` and the twist places `O.twistPlace`, which together form the level
`O.places`, and a character `O.tamePart w` of each residue field; the results on the tower and on
periods assume `2 r + 2 N + 3 < n`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Rows.stdClassSum_gramForm_eq_zero`: Periods of false lifts vanish, as class sums.

## The steps of the argument

* The bottom of the tower: `New.Rows.lift_polyVector_blockDatum_eq_zero` passes from the harmonic
  polynomial to all polynomials, and `New.DescentPair.descentsVanish_of_hyperplaneSumsAnnihilate`
  passes from the block datum to all data.
* The tower `New.Rows.descentsVanish_hyperbolicSum`: all descents of the coefficients of `Ξ` to
  `W ⊕ ℍ^N` vanish, for data that are the vacuum off the places of the level.
* From descents to periods, for `I_n = I_N ⊕ I_l`:
  `New.Rows.integral_conj_pairTheta_mul_algFormCoeff_eq_zero` absorbs the kernel of `W` and applies
  `New.SiegelWeil.integral_blockEmb_eq_zero_of_descentsVanish`, which takes a Fourier coefficient
  and varies the datum.
* The theorem `New.Rows.stdClassSum_gramForm_eq_zero` writes the periods over the block `I_l` as
  class sums `New.stdClassSum`. `New.Rows.stdClassSum_gramForm_eq_zero_of_rank_one` is the case of
  false lifts from a line; that of false lifts on `V_j` is in
  `New.OneLift.ComparisonOperator.GluingMaps`.
* Two uses: `New.Rows.stdClassSum_period_eq_zero` for point forms, and
  `New.Rows.DividedSplitting.stdClassSum_inner_productForm_eq_zero` for the product forms
  `New.Rows.DividedSplitting.productForm` of the kernel vectors.

Notions from other files:
* `New.pairWeil`: the Weil representation of U(W) × U(V) on the data space 𝒮(Hom(W, V)), twisted by
  two characters of U(1); `New.Space.θ` is the theta functional on that space.
* `New.Space.projOn`: the projection whose fixed vectors are the data that are the vacuum at the
  places of a set `S` and their conjugates. For `S` the complement of the places of the level and
  their conjugates, these are the test vectors.
* `New.heckePolyOp`: the operator ∑ (−X)^i q^(i choose 2) T_{w,i}, q the order of the residue field
  at w; `New.sphericalAt π w` is the space of vectors spherical at w.
* `New.algFormCoeff`: the matrix coefficient `g ↦ L (ρ(g_∞⁻¹) φ(g_f))` of a form `φ` at a functional
  `L`, with `ρ` the representation `New.conjWeylRep` on the vectors `New.WeylIndex n κ → ℂ` and `L`
  often `New.gramForm ζ`, the invariant inner product with `ζ`.
* `New.SiegelWeil.descentsVanish_add_planes`: vanishing of descents passes from `W` to `W` plus
  hyperbolic planes for `Y` killed by a Hecke polynomial at a small point.
modules.literature:
Let V=V₁⊕V₂ with V₁ of small rank, and take a form on a definite U(V) that is killed by theta
descent, by the hyperplane sums at the chosen places (as good forms are), and by a Hecke polynomial
at one split place at the smallest root of lifts. Then it has zero theta periods over U(V₂), so the
forms built from these kernels are orthogonal to it. It is known that vanishing of lifts in a theta
tower kills theta periods on a subgroup. Related work: C. Wu, Poles of Eisenstein series and theta
lifts for unitary groups, arXiv 2104.11954, 2021; Ginzburg–Jiang–Soudry, Poles of L-functions and
theta liftings for orthogonal groups, 2009; Jiang–Wu, On (χ,b)-factors of cuspidal automorphic
representations of unitary groups I, 2016; Rallis, On the Howe duality conjecture, 1984.

modules.title: The lift of a character from U(1): kernel, descent and Galois conjugates
modules.group: Hecke L-values as squared norms, and their valuations
modules.note:
Let `χ` be a character of `U(1)` over the adeles. Its lift is the algebraic form `φ` on the standard
definite space `V` of rank `card n` that is the sum, over the classes of `U(1)` at the level of
the chosen places, of the theta kernel formed with `χ` and the block datum. It is a multiple of the
theta lift of the constant function `1`. This file defines `φ`, computes its inner products through
the descent from `V` to the line, and shows that a Galois conjugate of `φ` is, up to simple factors,
the lift of the conjugate character.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.LValueData`: the chosen places and the places of the twist, the row lengths `rowLength τ`
  and the character `u1Char` of `U(1)`. `New.LValueData.descentPair` is the descent datum
  (`New.DescentPair`) whose source `W` is the definite line and whose weight has one row of length
  `rowLength τ` at `τ`.
* `New.LValueData.kernelForm`: the theta kernel at a finite point `g` of `U(1)`, as a form on `V`;
  the lift `New.LValueData.trivialLift` is its class sum over `U(1)`.
* `New.LValueData.theta_pairThetaKernel_omega_fockDatum`: the pairings of the kernel with vectors of
  the weight are theta values of Fock vectors.
* `New.LValueData.normalizedDescent_eq_inner_kernelForm`, `New.LValueData.inner_trivialLift`: the
  descent `New.DescentPair.normalizedDescent` of a form is its inner product with the kernel, so the
  inner product with the lift is the class sum of the descent.
* `New.DescentPair.heckePolyOnForms_liftHeckeRoot_eq_zero`: the Hecke polynomial
  `New.DescentPair.heckePolyOnForms`, evaluated at the number `New.DescentPair.liftHeckeRoot`,
  annihilates every form with the Hecke polynomials of a lift
  (`New.DescentPair.HasLiftHeckePolynomial`).
* `New.LValueData.map_trivialLift`: the Galois conjugates of the lift.

Notions from other files:

* `New.DescentPair`: a descent datum, that is places, a hermitian space `W` of rank less than
  `card n`, two weights and a character; `New.DescentPair.FormV` is the space of algebraic forms on
  `V` of its weight and level, and `New.DescentPair.blockDatum` is the block datum on `Hom(W, V)`
  times the vacuum.
* `Gf E n`, `stdLevel E n`: the finite adelic points of the unitary group of `V` and their integral
  subgroup; `levelOf w H` is the level of elements of `stdLevel` that reduce into `H` at the places
  `w`.
* `classSum Γ K f`: the weighted sum of `f` over `Γ \ G / K`; `stdClassSum` takes `Γ` rational.
* `schurJet κ`: the jets of a power series along the Schur matrix of the weight `κ`.

up, for the data `New.LValueData`, steps of the known expression of critical Hecke L-values of CM

modules.title: The lift of a character and its squared norm as a Hecke L-value
modules.group: Hecke L-values as squared norms, and their valuations
modules.note:
Let `p = (ν, z)` be a critical pair (`New.Data.CriticalPair`) with `z ≥ 2` and `ϑ` a tame character
with set of places `Q`. The first section defines the lift `φ` of `ν ϑ` from `U(1)` to the definite
`U(2 z)`, a denominator for its values, and its normalized squared norm. The second section works
with any lift data `X` (`New.LValueData`) and the lift `X.trivialLift`, which differs from `φ` by
the scales of the vacuum and of the derivatives. For even rank `2 k ≥ 4` its squared norm is an
explicit multiple of the value at `k` of the partial Hecke `L`-function of `X.u1Char⁻¹`, where
`X.u1Char` is the character of the data.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.CriticalPair.trivialLift`: the lift `φ` of `ν ϑ`, which is the lift for these data times
  `vacuumScale ^ card n` and `(π̄ * jetScale) ^ rowLengthSum`, where `π = D.piMBar`.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.denomBound`: a denominator `n_ν` for the values of `φ`.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.algPart`: the squared norm of `φ` divided by `N(Q) ^ (2 z - 1)`;
  `New.Data.CriticalPair.integralAlgebraicPart` is its multiple by
  `n_L = chosenGroupOrder * denomBound ^ 2`.
* `New.LValueData.trivialLift_eq_smul_thetaLift`: `X.trivialLift` is the theta lift of the constant
  function `1` times the index of the level of `U(1)`.
* `New.LValueData.hasLiftHeckePolynomial_trivialLift`: at split places off the level,
  `X.trivialLift` is spherical, with the Hecke polynomials of a lift of the trivial system
  (`New.DescentPair.HasLiftHeckePolynomial`).
* `New.LValueData.inner_thetaLift_constForm_self`: Rallis' inner product formula
  `New.SiegelWeil.IsSharp.petersson_lift_eq_integral` for the constant `1`. It gives the squared
  norm of the theta lift of `1` as a multiple of the sum of the coefficients of the vacuum.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.TameChar`: a character of `U(1)(𝔸)` of weight `0` whose tame part is supported on a
  finite set `Q` of places of norm prime to `D.M * D.N`, with `Q` disjoint from its conjugate.
* `New.LValueData`: two families of split places (`chosenPlace`, and `twistPlace` for `Q`), row
  lengths `rowLength`, and a character `u1Char` of `U(1)(𝔸)` whose tame part is trivial off these
  places.
* `New.LValueData.descentPair`: the descent datum (`New.DescentPair`) attached to the data. Its
  source is the definite line, and its weight has one row of length `rowLength τ` at each infinite
  place `τ`.
* `New.Parameters.vacuumScale`, `New.Parameters.jetScale`: the scaling factor of the vacuum, and the
  scale at which Taylor series of theta functions are taken.
* `New.Data.chosenGroupOrder`: a common multiple of the orders of the stabilisers in the class sums.
* `New.placeSign`: signs on the places of `E` whose Euler product at `k` is the value at `2 k` of
  the zeta function `ζ_F` of the maximal real subfield `F`, over which `E` is unramified.

modules.title: The algebraic part as a Hecke L-value, and products of L-values of twists
modules.group: Hecke L-values as squared norms, and their valuations
modules.note:
Let `p = (ν, z)` be a critical pair and `ϑ` a tame character of modulus `Q`. For the statements on
`algPart` and `integralAlgebraicPart` assume `z ≥ 2` and fix an index set with `2 z` elements
(`New.Data.CriticalPair.HasLiftRank`). The number `New.Data.CriticalPair.algPart` is the normalised
squared norm of the lift `New.Data.CriticalPair.trivialLift` of `ν ϑ`. It is positive and equals a
constant independent of `ϑ` times an `L`-value of `ν ϑ`, so the ratio of the absolute values of the
twisted and untwisted `L`-values, which is nonzero, is a ratio of values of `algPart`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.CriticalPair.algPart_pos`, `New.Data.CriticalPair.exists_ne_zero_algPart_eq_mul_L`: the
  number `New.Data.CriticalPair.algPart` is positive, and it is a nonzero constant independent of
  `ϑ` times an `L`-value of `ν ϑ`. `New.Data.CriticalPair.exists_algPart_eq_mul_L` states the value
  with the positivity.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.ratio_eq_algPart_div`: the ratio `New.Data.CriticalPair.ratio` of the
  absolute values of twisted and untwisted `L`-values is a ratio of values of `algPart`.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.exists_integralAlgebraicPart_eq_mul_L`,
  `New.Data.CriticalPair.ratio_eq_integralAlgebraicPart_div`: the same value and ratio for the
  multiple `New.Data.CriticalPair.integralAlgebraicPart`, with the `L`-value of `(ν ϑ)⁻¹`.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.exists_ofAlgForm_trivialLift_eq_smul_lift`,
  `New.Data.CriticalPair.formAction_trivialLift`: the lift is a nonzero multiple of the theta lift
  of the constant function `1`, and the finite group of rank one at the chosen places fixes it.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.lValueProd_eq_mul_prod_ratio_sq`: the product `New.Exchange.lValueProd` of
  squared L-values for the twist is the untwisted one times a power of the norm of `Q` and the
  squared ratios at `1, …, p.z`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.CriticalPair`: a critical pair `p = (ν, z)`, of an integer `1 ≤ z ≤ D.t` and a character
  `ν` of U(1)(𝔸) of weight `-c` with `z ≤ c ≤ 4 D.b`, whose tame part is supported on the chosen
  places (`New.Data.IsChosen`).
* `New.Data.TameChar`: a character `ϑ` of U(1)(𝔸) of weight 0 with tame part supported on a finite
  set `Q` of places; `ϑ.normQ` is the product `N(Q)` of the norms of the places of `Q`.
* `New.AutChar.L`: `ν.L S` is the `L`-function of `x ↦ ν (x / x̄)` without the Euler factors at `S`
  and at the conjugates of the places of `S`, as an Euler product at real points `s > 1` and as
  its limit from the right at `s = 1`.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.lValueData`: the data (`New.LValueData`) of the theta lift from U(1) to the
  definite `U(2 z)` for the character `ν ϑ`.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.trivialLift`: the lift of `ν ϑ`, a nonzero multiple of the unscaled lift
  `New.LValueData.trivialLift`, which is the sum of the theta kernels over the classes of U(1).
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.algPart`: the number `‖φ‖ ^ 2 / N(Q) ^ (2 z - 1)`, where `φ` is the lift of
  `ν ϑ`; `integralAlgebraicPart` is a multiple of it by a natural number that does not depend on
  `ϑ`.

modules.title: The lift of a character: denominators, and one group ring element for all twists
modules.group: Hecke L-values as squared norms, and their valuations
modules.note:
Let `p = (ν, z)` be a critical pair with `z ≥ 2`, let `ϑ` be a tame character with set of places
(modulus) `Q`, and let `New.Data.CriticalPair.trivialLift` be the lift of `ν ϑ`, a normalised theta

modules.literature:
This file proves, for this data, versions of known results: integral group-ring elements that
interpolate twisted values of Hecke L-functions (see `New.Congruences.Selmer.ClassSums`), which are
squared norms of theta lifts from U(1) (see `Lib.SiegelWeil.RallisInner.SharpData`). Here only the
side of the squared norms is treated.

modules.title: Archimedean bounds and heights of squared norms of rank-one theta lifts
modules.group: Hecke L-values as squared norms, and their valuations
modules.note:
This file bounds the absolute values of the conjugates under `Aut(ℂ/K)` of the squared norm `‖φ‖²`
of the lift `φ = New.Data.CriticalPair.trivialLift` of a critical pair for the trivial twist. It
also bounds the conjugates of `New.Data.CriticalPair.integralAlgebraicPart` for flat pairs
(`New.Data.CriticalPair.HasEmptyRow`, `c = z`). A conjugate of the squared norm is a multiple of the
squared norm of the lift for the conjugate character, and this is an `L`-value times explicit
factors. The file shows that flat pairs exist over a given character of weight zero and bounds the
range of the jet degrees of a main pair (`New.Data.CriticalPair.IsMainPair`). It bounds the height
(`New.HeightLe`) of the squared norm of the untwisted lift of a main pair.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.heightLe_norm_trivialLift_sq`: for a main pair, a bound for the height of the squared
  norm of the untwisted lift.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.norm_map_integralAlgebraicPart_le`: for a flat pair, every conjugate under
  `Aut ℂ` of `integralAlgebraicPart` at the trivial twist has absolute value at most
  `exp (x ^ 34)`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.CriticalPair`: An integer 1 ≤ z ≤ t and a character ν of U(1)(𝔸) of weight −c, z ≤ c(v)
  ≤ 4b, with tame part supported on the chosen places.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.integralAlgebraicPart`: The product of
  `n_L = chosenGroupOrder * denomBound ^ 2` and the algebraic part `‖φ‖² / N(Q) ^ (2 z - 1)`
  (`New.Data.CriticalPair.algPart`); the first factor of `n_L` clears the orders of automorphism
  groups, the second the denominators of `φ`.
