modules.title: Central action on lifts from U(1) and a rank-one denominator bound
modules.group: Hecke L-values as squared norms, and their valuations
modules.note:
For a lift from the definite `U(1)` to the definite `U(n)` (data `New.LValueData`, kernel
`New.LValueData.kernelForm`, lift `New.LValueData.trivialLift` of the trivial character), the finite
adelic `U(1)` acts on forms on `U(n)` through the centre. This file defines this action,
`New.LValueData.centralRep`, and its twist `New.LValueData.normalizedCentralOp`, which fixes the
lift. The central translations commute with Hecke polynomials at split places off the level. The
file uses this action to bound the denominator of the product of the projections of two test forms
to the line of the lift, given a bound `New.Selmer.DenominatorLe` on that line.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Selmer.DenominatorLe.norm_inner_starProjection_le`: a bound `New.Selmer.DenominatorLe` on the
  line of the lift bounds the denominator of the product of the projections of two test forms to
  that line, at the cost of the class number of `U(1)` at the chosen level.
* `New.LValueData.normalizedCentralOp_trivialLift`: the twisted central translations fix the lift
  of the constant function.

modules.title: Heights of ratios of twisted to untwisted Hecke values via rank-one theta lifts
modules.group: Hecke L-values as squared norms, and their valuations
modules.note:
This file builds a test form (`New.DescentPair.IsTestForm`: integral above `ℓ` and orthogonal to the
false lifts) from class sums on four blocks of indices. Its pairing with the lift of a main pair has
small valuation at `ℓ`. With the bound for the denominators of the projections to the line of the
lift, this bounds the valuation of the squared norm of the twisted lift from above. Here
`New.HeightLe c y` says that the family `y ι`, one number for each `ι : ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_ℓ`, has height at
most `c`; the file bounds the heights of inverse ratios of twisted to untwisted Hecke values, with
twists along a family `θ` with `New.Data.IsRegularFamily`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Data.exists_isTestForm_le_norm_inner_trivialLift`: at every prime `l` coprime to `ϑ.normQ` of
  a twist `ϑ`, some test form has a pairing of small valuation with the lift
  `New.Data.CriticalPair.trivialLift` of a main pair.
* `New.Data.heightLe_inv_ratio`: the inverse ratios of a main pair have height at most
  `6 denominatorBudget - directionAmount`.
* `New.Data.exists_heckeValueProd_eq_mul_prod_ratio`: the quotient of the Hecke values
  `New.Data.heckeValueProd j` at a twist and at `1` as a product of ratios of L-values.
* `New.Data.heightLe_inv_heckeValueProd_div`: a bound for the height of the inverse of this
  quotient.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.CriticalPair`: An integer 1 ≤ z ≤ t and a character ν of U(1)(𝔸) of weight −c,
  z ≤ c(v) ≤ 4b, with tame part supported on the chosen places.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.integralAlgebraicPart`: The product of
  `n_L = chosenGroupOrder * denomBound ^ 2` and the algebraic part `‖φ‖² / N(Q) ^ (2 z - 1)`
  (`New.Data.CriticalPair.algPart`); the first factor of `n_L` clears the orders of automorphism
  groups, the second the denominators of `φ`.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.ratio`: The ratio |L(z, (νϑ^s)⁻¹)| / |L(z, ν⁻¹)| for a sign s (by default
  1), without the Euler factors at the level.

The data `D` over the parameters `P` supply the CM field `D.E`, with `f` infinite places and
`D.towerExp` its index in the tower over `K = ℚ(i√d)`, the natural numbers `m`, `k`, `r`, `t`, `M`
and `a`, and the reals `b`, `x`, `x₁` of the bounds. Here `M ^ f` is the norm of the product of the
chosen places, `x` the length of the prime sum, `denominatorBudget = f a log³ b / (m k)` and
`directionAmount` the sum over the infinite places `σ` of `jetSize (κ σ) - primeSum (κ σ) σ`, where
`κ = D.weight`, `jetSize` is the size of a derivative and `primeSum` measures its guaranteed
divisibility.

`P.vacuumScale D.towerExp` scales the vacuum of rank one to integral values, `P.jetScale D.towerExp`
scales Taylor series of theta functions, `modKernel` is the theta kernel given by a function on
matrices modulo an ideal and a polynomial, and `p.rowLengthSum` is `∑ τ, (p.negWeight τ - p.z)`.
modules.literature:
Norms of lifts of Hecke characters as L-values, their divisibility via congruences, and divisibility
at inert primes are known from the literature. Related work: Prasanna, Integrality of a ratio of
Petersson norms, 2006; Coates–Liang–Sujatha, Tate–Shafarevich group for elliptic curves with CM II,
2010 (after Katz, 1977); Y.-S. Lee, Hida family of theta lift from U(1) to definite U(2), 2024.

modules.title: The period of a determinant theta kernel (used in rank two for the L-value at z = 1)
modules.group: Hecke L-values as squared norms, and their valuations
modules.note:
The period of a theta kernel for the pair `(I_n, I_n)` of standard definite spaces (`New.stdSpace`),
with polynomial `∏ τ, det ^ c τ` and finite datum a character of the determinant modulo `𝔪`.

* `New.Rows.detKernel`, `New.Rows.detPeriod`: the kernel on the finite adelic group and its class
  sum.
* `New.Rows.detPeriod_eq_stdClassSum_sum`: the period is the class sum of the sums, over
  `GL_n(O/𝔪)`, of the kernel values for the indicator of the unit matrix.
* `New.Rows.detPeriod_insert`: if `α` has weight `-c` and tame part `ψ` trivial outside `𝔪`, adding
  a prime `v` to `𝔪` multiplies the period by `∏ l < card n, (1 - q ^ l X)`. Here `q` is the norm of
  `v` and `X` is the inverse of the scalar `α.frobValue n v` (`New.AutChar.frobValue`).

`New.stdClassSum K f` is the sum of `f g / #Aut g` over the classes of level `K`; `New.stdLevel` is
the stabiliser of the standard lattice; `α.HasWeight e ψ` says that `α` has weight `e` and tame part
`ψ`; `𝔪.places` is the set of primes of the modulus `𝔪` and `𝔪.charOfTamePart ψ` the character
modulo `𝔪` made of `ψ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Modulus`: a nonzero ideal of O_E prime to its complex conjugate, that is, never divisible by
  both w and w̄.
* `New.WeilData`: the fixed choices on the CM field E that define the Weil representations (a purely
  imaginary element, a self-dual finite idele and a splitting character).
* `α.frobValue n v`: the number χ(ϖ) q ^ (N/2), where N is the cardinality of `n`, χ is the Hecke
  character `α.spaceChar N`, ϖ a uniformiser at `v` and q the norm of `v`.

modules.title: All data have regular families of m-fold twists
modules.group: Congruences and the choice of twists
modules.note:
This file states the conclusion of the Selmer group argument.

* `New.exists_isRegularFamily`: for all data `D` there is a family of `m`-fold twists, one for each
  prime `ℓ` and isomorphism `ι : ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_ℓ`, that is regular (`New.Data.IsRegularFamily`): for the
  first `m` powers of its members the inverse ratios of `L`-values have height at most `D.x₁`, and
  the logarithms of the denominators of the projections to lifts sum over the primes to at most
  `D.denominatorBudget`.
* `New.Selmer.exists_mFoldTwist_hasDenominatorsLe`: the twist for one prime and one isomorphism.
* `New.Selmer.range_goodLift_le_span_hasLiftHeckePolynomial`: the lifts are spanned by forms that
  lift one of finitely many eigensystems, which do not depend on the twist.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.MFoldTwist`: a twist ϑ whose tame part ψ has ψ_wⁿ non-trivial for all places w in its
  set Q and 1 ≤ n ≤ m.
* `New.Data.IsNegligible`: reals `e l` with `∑ e l log l ≤ x ^ C` over every finite set
  of primes, where `x = D.x` is the length of the prime sum, the smallest scale of the data.
* `New.Selmer.IsMainSummand`: an `ℓ`-adic Galois representation satisfies the local and global
  conditions `IsMainSummandLike` and, up to a twist and a string of characters, gives the traces of
  the representations attached to the lifts of a Hecke eigensystem, for all twists of a descent
  pair.
* `New.Selmer.DenominatorLe`: an operator `Λ` on a space `Z` of forms, with determinant of norm at
  least `exp (-(dim Z · r · β))` at `ι`, clears the denominators of the orthogonal projection to
  `Z`. Here `r` is the rank of the source of the lift.
modules.literature:
For each prime ℓ and each identification of the complex numbers with the algebraic closure of the
ℓ-adic numbers, there is a twist whose first m powers have few congruences. For these twists, the
denominators of projections to theta lifts and the divisibility of ratios of Hecke values sum over
all ℓ to a total that the heights afford. It is known that denominators of projections to lifts give
Selmer classes and that twisting lowers Selmer ranks. Related work: Prasanna, Integrality of a ratio
of Petersson norms, 2006 (after Ribet, 1976; Wiles); Klosin, Congruences among modular forms on
U(2,2) and the Bloch–Kato conjecture, 2009; Mazur–Rubin, Ranks of twists of elliptic curves, 2010.

modules.title: Bad places, ℓ-adic avatars and hypotheses on conjugate self-dual representations
modules.note:
Fix data `D`, a prime `ℓ` and a descent pair `O` (`New.DescentPair`) with chosen places
`O.chosenPlace`. This file introduces the bad places and the `ℓ`-adic avatars of characters of
`U(1)`. It states the hypotheses on conjugate self-dual `ℓ`-adic representations `R` of the
absolute Galois group of the CM field `D.E` under which Selmer groups are bounded: conjugate
self-dual representations of given level, main summands and representations of a type. It also
defines lift settings and the idempotents of tuples of types acting on forms. The two primes
`p₀`, `p₁` of the data are `D.levelPrime 0` and `D.levelPrime 1`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Selmer.IsConjSelfDual`: `R` is continuous, has a non-degenerate trace form on the span of its
  image, and is conjugate self-dual up to a twist.
* `New.Selmer.IsConjSelfDualOfLevel`: moreover `R` has given jumps and is of finite type at the
  places off a set `S` and at those above `ℓ p₀ p₁`, and has good reduction at those of them prime
  to `p₀ p₁`.
* `New.Selmer.IsMainSummandLike`: the case `S = ∅`, with conditions on the jumps, the ramification
  above `p₀ p₁` and the size of the image.
* `New.Selmer.IsLiftSetting`, `New.Selmer.typeProjection`: descent pairs with type polynomials
  suited to a twist, and the idempotents of tuples of types acting on forms.

Notions from other files:
* `New.DescentPair`: A descent pair: places M and Q, a space W of rank r with numbered basis
  vectors, an embedding of its r indices into a set of n > r indices, weights k⁺ and k⁻, and a
  character μ whose tame part is trivial off these places.
* `New.DescentPair.FormV`: the algebraic forms on the definite space `V = I_n` with the weight and
  level of `O`; the product of the groups `GL_r(k_w)` at the chosen places acts on them.
* `New.conjGal`: The map `g ↦ g^c = c g c`, with `c` complex conjugation.

modules.title: Lift settings and conjugate self-duality of attached Galois representations
modules.note:
This file shows that good tuples of labels form lift settings with the descent pairs of the data.
It also shows that, for a main pair, the constant label `X - 1` forms a lift setting for the lift
from `U(1)`. It bounds the `ℓ`-adic valuation of `p_i ^ d - 1` and gives basic facts on lattices
in a representation. It proves that representations attached to Hecke eigenforms are conjugate
self-dual. It also shows that representations of a type arise from labelled eigenforms and are
preserved by twisting with avatars.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Selmer.isConjSelfDual_of_attached`: a Galois representation `r` of rank `n` attached to a
  Hecke eigenform (`New.GaloisRep.Attached`) satisfies `New.Selmer.IsConjSelfDual`. In particular,
  tr r(g^c) = χ(g)^(n-1) tr r(g⁻¹) with χ = `New.Selmer.cyclotomicInv`. The Hecke operators at w and
  w̄ are dual (`New.heckeSplit_dual`), which gives the relation for most Frobenii. It passes to
  every g along the filter `New.mostFrobeniiAt`.
* `New.Selmer.isRepOfType_of_hasProductLabel`: the representation attached to a labelled eigenform
  is a representation of a type.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.descentPair`: The j-th descent pair (`New.DescentPair`) for ϑ: W = W_j of rank r,
  V = I_{r+t}, the character μ_j⁰ϑ of weight −w_j, and the places `New.Data.levelPlaces`.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.IsMainPair`: A pair `p = (p.character, z)` with `p.character` of weight
  `-c` is a main pair for `j` if the index type `RankOneIndex z` has `2 z` elements and `2 ≤ z`
  (`HasLiftRank`), `m < z ≤ r`, `1 ≤ j ≤ m`, the tame part of `p.character` is `D.chiMLocal ^ j`
  (`D.chiMLocal` the tame character of the data), and `w_j + r - t ≤ c ≤ w_j` at every infinite
  place, with `w_j = D.liftWeight j`.
* `New.Selmer.IsConjSelfDual`: `R` is continuous, has non-degenerate trace form, and is conjugate
  self-dual up to twist on traces, tr R(g^c) = χ(g)^(t-1) tr R(g⁻¹), with `g^c = c g c`
  (`New.conjGal`) and χ = `New.Selmer.cyclotomicInv`.
* `New.Selmer.IsLiftSetting`: the descent pair `O` with the labels `c` is a lift setting for the
  twist `ϑ`.
* `New.Selmer.IsRepOfType`: `R` is a conjugate self-dual representation of level `S`, and inertia
  at the chosen places acts through the roots of the labels `c`.

modules.title: Main summands and conjugate self-dual representations from type polynomials
modules.note:
Let `O` be a descent pair (`New.DescentPair`) with type polynomials `c` in a lift setting
(`New.Selmer.IsLiftSetting`). This file describes inertia on representations of a type for `O` and
on representations attached to its eigenforms.

* `New.Selmer.exists_inertiaGroup_isInertiaSpectrum`: inertia elements above the primes
  `D.levelPrime 0` and `D.levelPrime 1` are killed by polynomials whose roots are roots of unity of
  controlled order (`New.Selmer.IsInertiaSpectrum`).
* `New.Selmer.IsRepOfType.isMainSummandLike`: a representation of a type of rank `card r` and empty
  level, with jumps as in `New.Selmer.IsMainSummandWeights`, is a main summand
  (`New.Selmer.IsMainSummandLike`).
* `New.Selmer.isFiniteTypeAt_and_polyKillsAt_of_mem_conjClosure`: a representation attached to an
  eigenform of parahoric type at the auxiliary places (`New.Selmer.HasTwistParahoricType`) has no
  monodromy above `ϑ.Q` and its conjugates, and a quadratic polynomial kills inertia there.
* `New.Selmer.normalisedRep_quadratic_on_inertia`: its normalised representation satisfies the same
  quadratic relation on inertia above `ϑ.Q` and its conjugates.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Selmer.IsLiftSetting O c ϑ`: the places of `O` are the chosen places above `D.levelPrime 0`,
  `D.levelPrime 1` and those of `ϑ.Q`, its character is a power of `D.chiMLocal` times `ϑ.tamePart`,
  and `c` are type polynomials of degree `card r`.
* `New.Selmer.IsRepOfType O k J c S R`: `R` is a conjugate self-dual representation of given level
  (`New.Selmer.IsConjSelfDualOfLevel`: on traces `R^c ≅ R^∨(1 - k)`, with Hodge–Tate jumps `J` and
  local conditions off the level `S` and above `ℓ M`), and inertia at the chosen places acts through
  the roots of the type polynomials `c` over the residue fields.
* `New.ClosurePlace`: a place of the algebraic closure `Ω` of `ℚ`, that is, a valuation subring;
  `conjPlace A` is the complex conjugate place, and `AbsGal D` is `Gal(Ω/D.E)`.
* `New.Data.IsChosen`: a place of `D.E` is chosen if it divides `D.piM`, an integer whose product
  with its conjugate is `M = D.levelPrime 0 * D.levelPrime 1`.
* `New.GaloisRep.PolyKillsAt R A s P`: `P` kills `s` at the place `A`, that is, `P (R s) = 0` off
  `ℓ`, and an analogue for Weil pairs (`New.Period.IsKilledBy`) above `ℓ`.
* `New.Selmer.scaledTypePoly`: the scaled type polynomial, `c i` with its roots multiplied by the
  element of the residue field that names the character `(O.tamePart w)⁻¹`, `w = O.chosenPlace i`.
* `New.ellVal`: the `ℓ`-adic valuation with values in `[0, ∞]`.
* `New.Data.Twist`: a tame character (`New.Data.TameChar`) whose tame part is non-trivial at every
  place of its set `Q`.

modules.title: Base data whose forms contain those with given labels in a lift setting
modules.note:
Let `O` be a descent pair (`New.DescentPair`): hermitian spaces `W` and `V` with bases `r` and `n`,
with chosen places, twist places, weights and a character. Let `c` be a tuple of labels
(polynomials over the residue fields) at the chosen places, forming a lift setting with a twist `ϑ`
(`New.Selmer.IsLiftSetting`); `typeProjection O c` is the idempotent on forms that cuts out the
labels `c`.

* `New.Selmer.IsFormOfType`, `New.Selmer.IsFormOfType.isRepOfType_normalisedRep`: the eigenforms
  of type `c` with the level and character of `O` off a set of places, and their normalised
  representations as representations of a type.
* `New.Selmer.exists_baseLevel`: base data (`New.Patching.BaseLevel`) whose forms contain the image
  of the idempotent and whose eigensystems have normalised representations that are representations
  of a type with a quadratic relation on inertia, when the modulus of `ϑ` is auxiliary; also,
  `New.Data.chosenGroupOrder` times the idempotent keeps integral forms.
* `New.Selmer.normalisedJumps_eq_range_add_map`: the Hodge–Tate jumps of the normalised
  representations are, when the rank of the larger space is even, `0, …, t - 1` and the
  `(t - 1) / 2 ∓ (λ_c + κ')`, where `t` is the difference of the ranks, `λ` the parameter on the
  smaller space and `-κ'` the weight of the character.

Notions from other files:
* `New.levelSpace`: the vectors `v` of a representation `π` with `π k v = χ k • v` for all `k` in
  the subgroup `K`.
* `New.Gf.componentOn`: keeps the components of an element at the places of `S` and their
  conjugates, and replaces the others by 1.
* `New.DescentPair.columnCount`: the weight datum `(τ, i) ↦ k⁺(τ, i) + k⁻(τ, n − i)` of forms on the
  definite space of rank `n`, with `k⁺`, `k⁻` the two weights of the pair.
* `New.DescentPair.FormV`: the algebraic forms on the definite space of rank `n` with the weight
  `(O.columnCount, O.detExp)`, the level group and the level character `O.levelChar` of the pair
  `O`.
* `New.DescentPair.chosenGLRep`: the action of `∏ GL_r(k_w)`, over the chosen places `w`, on the
  vectors of `π` with the level and character of `O`, twisted by `∏ ψ_w (det g_w)`, where `ψ_w` is
  the character `O.tamePart w` of the residue field `k_w`.
* `New.levelOf`, `New.descentResidueLevel`, `New.DescentPair.levelChar`: the level of `O` is the
  group of integral elements whose reductions at its places lie in `descentResidueLevel`;
  `levelChar` is its character.
* `New.Data.chosenGroupOrder`: the order of a product of groups `GL` over the residue fields of the
  chosen places of `D`; `New.Patching.BaseLevel.ellIntegralForms`: the forms whose values at the
  points integral above `ℓ` are sent to `ℓ`-adic integers by `ιℓ : ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_ℓ`.
* `New.HasProductLabel`: a label of a form at a place, made from a polynomial and characters of
  blocks of given sizes; `New.faithfulChar`: the faithful character by which it is formed.
* `New.Selmer.IsRepOfType`: a conjugate self-dual representation of given jumps and level on which
  inertia at the chosen places acts through the roots of the labels; `New.Selmer.normalisedRep`: the
  twist of a representation by `normalizingAvatar O`; `ϑ.invAvatar`: the `ℓ`-adic avatar of `ϑ⁻¹`
  over `D.E`.

modules.title: Main summand conditions on Hodge–Tate jumps and existence of main summands for Hecke eigensystems
modules.note:
This file passes from Hecke eigensystems of forms to the main summands (`New.Selmer.IsMainSummand`)
that enter the Selmer groups. The Hodge–Tate jumps occurring for the main summands of the descent
pairs (W_j, V_j) satisfy the numerical conditions `New.Selmer.IsMainSummandWeights`. Each such jump
is small or near `∓ w_j`, and few jumps are small. At a pair of conjugate embeddings at most
rank-many jumps are negative.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Selmer.isMainSummandWeights_mainPair`: the single jump of a main pair obeys
  `New.Selmer.IsMainSummandWeights` in rank `1`.
* `New.Selmer.isMainSummandWeights_descentPair`: the jumps built from `New.Data.targetParameter` and
  `New.Data.liftWeight` obey `New.Selmer.IsMainSummandWeights` in rank `D.r`.
* `New.Selmer.exists_isMainSummand_of_isRepOfType`: take a representation `R` with admissible labels
  whose shifted jumps obey `New.Selmer.IsMainSummandWeights`. Assume its traces are limits of the
  values of `b`. Then it gives a representation `T` with `New.Selmer.IsMainSummand O b T`.
* `New.Selmer.exists_isMainSummand_descentPair`: a Hecke eigensystem of a good form on
  `D.spaceW D.m` gives a main summand for each descent pair of the trivial twist.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Selmer.IsMainSummandWeights D r t J`: numerical conditions on the jumps `J σ`, a multiset of
  integers for each complex embedding `σ` of the CM field `D.E`.
* `New.Selmer.IsMainSummand O z T`: `T` is like a main summand, and for every twist of the pair `O`
  by a tame character `ϑ` the normalised representation attached to a lift of the system `z` has the
  trace of `T` twisted by `ϑ⁻¹` plus a string of powers of the inverse cyclotomic character.
* `New.Selmer.IsLiftSetting O c ϑ`: the descent pair `O` fits the twist `ϑ` and the labels `c` are
  admissible.
* `New.Selmer.IsRepOfType O k J c S R`: `R` is a conjugate self-dual representation of level `S`
  (`New.Selmer.IsConjSelfDualOfLevel`) with jumps `J`, and inertia at the chosen places acts through
  the roots of the labels `c`.
* `New.Data.goodForms`, `New.Data.eigenPart`: the image of the idempotent e₀ on forms of principal
  level at the chosen places, and the forms on which the Hecke operators act by given scalars.
modules.literature:
The Galois representation of each eigenform in a space of theta lifts has the trace of a twisted
block, which does not depend on the twist, plus a string of powers of the inverse cyclotomic
character. This shape follows from the unramified theta correspondence. Related work: Rallis,
Langlands' functoriality and the Weil representation, 1982; Khare–Larsen–Savin, Functoriality and
the inverse Galois problem, 2008; Arias-de-Reyna–Dieulefait–Shin–Wiese, Compatible systems of
symplectic Galois representations III, 2015.

modules.title: Amitsur's formula and Ribet's method for matrices over an algebra
modules.note:
This file proves Amitsur's formula for block matrices and derives Ribet's method from the
Cayley–Hamilton theorem. Here `u x` (`x : Y`) is a family of matrix representations of `G`. The
coefficients of their characteristic polynomials, as functions of `x`, lie in an algebra `S` of
functions `Y → L`. 'In the image of `R`' is written `∈ (algebraMap R L).range`. The file ends with
Ribet's element for a square matrix of tied rows, a matrix whose rows give relations modulo a left
ideal whose traces are controlled.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Selmer.exists_ribet_polynomial`: Ribet's method. Let `ρ` represent an `R`-algebra `Λ` with
  characteristic polynomials over `R`, let `𝔞` be a two-sided ideal containing its kernel, and let
  `I` be the left ideal spanned by a vector `y`. If `B y` has entries in `𝔞 + I ρ₀`, then some
  polynomial `P` has constant term `det B`, read through `ρ`, and `I P(ρ₀) ⊆ 𝔞`.
* `New.amitsur_charpoly_comp_coeff_mem_range`: Amitsur's formula for block matrices. If all
  characteristic polynomials of the `ρ w` have their coefficients in the image of `R`, the same
  holds for every square matrix `P` over `Λ`, read as the block matrix with blocks `ρ (P i j)`.
* `New.Selmer.exists_ribet_element_of_tied_rows`: Ribet's element for a matrix of tied rows, for
  representations `u x` (`x : Y`) of `O[G]` and an algebra `S` of functions `Y → L` that contains
  the constants from `O` and, as functions of `x`, the coefficients of the characteristic
  polynomials of the group elements.

modules.title: Modules of functions, Fitting ideals and trace ideals for Ribet's method
modules.note:
This file bounds Fitting ideals of modules `R^s / N` over `R = O[X j]`, `O` a discrete valuation
ring, through modules of functions, and states the conditions on traces and on common Ribet
elements. Each index `j : J` carries two pairs `τ j`, `τ' j` and `φ j`, `φ' j` of elements of `G`.
In the application `τ' j` is the inverse of the conjugate of `τ j`, so that `c (τ j) - c (τ' j)`
is the value at `τ j` of the sum of a cocycle `c` and its conjugate, an even class; likewise for
`φ`. The file also gives the linear algebra for several characters and for the main summand.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Selmer.HasTriangleCost`, `New.Selmer.exists_mul_prod_X_mem_fittingIdeal`: if the module of
  functions `New.Selmer.formsMod` attached to `N ⊆ R^s`, `R = O[X j]`, satisfies a triangular
  condition along a finite set `I` of indices and a bound on lengths, then the Fitting ideal of
  `R^s / N` contains `∏ j ∈ I, X j` times a polynomial whose constant coefficient has bounded
  valuation.
* `New.Selmer.IsTraceIdeal`: an algebra `S` of families of polynomials in variables `X j` holds the
  characteristic polynomials, and an `S`-submodule `𝒥` holds the traces of given relations.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Selmer.fittingIdeal N`: the ideal of `R` generated by the determinants of square matrices
  with all rows in `N ⊆ R^ι`, the zeroth Fitting ideal of `R^ι / N`.
* `New.Selmer.formsMod Φ z N p`: the functions `g ↦ Ψ (z g)` on `G`, where `Ψ : O^n → O / p` runs
  over the `O`-linear maps that vanish on `Φ⁻¹ N`.
* `New.Selmer.ribetCocyclesIn u ρ B`: the cocycles `G → B^d` for `ρ` that obey the linear relations
  among the families `(u x g - 1)_x`.

modules.title: Tied rows and the matrices of Ribet's method to first order
modules.note:
This file sets up Ribet's method to first order: the action of `O[X j][G]` through representations
and characters, the tie ideal and the tied rows. It then finds matrices of tied rows with bounded
determinant on the main summand, and matrices of tied rows that serve all characters at once
through Fitting ideals.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Selmer.tieIdeal`, `New.Selmer.tiedRows`: the left ideal of `O[X j][G]` spanned by what every
  `u x` kills, `p I`, the relations that tie `τ k` to `φ k`, and `I ρ₀`, with `I` the augmentation
  ideal; and the rows whose element lies in it. The actions are `polyAction` and `polyChar`; the
  relations are `coordRows_cocycle_mem_tiedRows` and the lemmas after it.
* `New.Selmer.exists_tiedRows_addVal_det_le`: the main summand, for the tied rows: matrices of
  tied rows whose determinant on the block is bounded by the length of a module of cocycles.
* `New.Selmer.nonempty_characterRows`: matrices of tied rows that serve all characters at once.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Selmer.fittingIdeal N`: the ideal of `R` generated by the determinants of square matrices
  with all rows in `N ⊆ R^ι`, the zeroth Fitting ideal of `R^ι / N`.
* `New.Selmer.ribetCocyclesIn u ρ B`: the cocycles `G → B^d` for `ρ` that obey the linear relations
  among the families `(u x g - 1)_x`.
* `New.Selmer.IsTraceIdeal` (`FittingBlock`): `S` holds the characteristic polynomials, and the
  `S`-module `𝒥` holds the traces of given relations.
* `New.Selmer.IsCharacterCocycle` (`FittingBlock`): a cocycle `c : G → O / p` for the character
  `χ` that obeys the linear relations among the `(u x g - 1)_x` and vanishes at the `δ v`; if
  `c γ = 0`, then every `χ g - 1` kills `c a`.
* `New.Selmer.IsDetectedBy` (`FittingBlock`): an element of the module that vanishes on `s` is zero.

modules.title: Ribet's method to first order over a discrete valuation ring
modules.note:
This file proves an algebraic form of Ribet's method to first order that does not involve Galois
groups. Here `u x` (`x : Y`) is a finite family of representations of a group `G` over a discrete
valuation ring `O`; at certain `x`, `u x` is the sum of a main summand (the block) and of
characters. The file glues the matrices of tied rows for the block and for the characters, so that
one element serves the determinants of all combinations `∑ ω g (u x g - 1)`, and passes from
coefficients modulo powers of `p` to coefficients in `K/O`. The result is applied to Galois
representations in `New.Selmer.ribet_columns`.

In that application the data of `New.Selmer.exists_isCommonRibetElement_addVal_le` are as follows.
The elements `τ (j, true)` and `φ (j, true)` are a tame generator and a Frobenius element at the new
place `j`, and `τ (j, false)`, `φ (j, false)` are the inverses of their conjugates. The `δ v` are
tame generators at the old places, `γ x` acts on the summand by a scalar `y x` with `y x - 1` a
unit, `a` generates the cyclotomic quotient, `p` is `ℓ ^ ν`, and `C : O` is the cost of telling the
characters apart. The `X j` are free variables; only the coefficients of the monomials that divide
`∏ X j` are read.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Selmer.exists_isCommonRibetElement_addVal_le`: the determinants of all combinations
  `∑ ω g (u x g - 1)` have one Ribet element whose coefficient comes from `O` and has bounded
  valuation. The proof finds matrices of tied rows with bounded determinant on the block
  (`exists_tiedRows_addVal_det_le`) and on the characters (`nonempty_characterRows`), and glues them
  (`exists_traceIdeal_multiplier_eq_sum_det`).
* `New.Selmer.exists_traceIdeal_multiplier_eq_sum_det`: the gluing, on the set where `u x` is the
  block `ρ x` plus the characters `ξ e`, with `ξ 0 = 1`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Selmer.ribetCocyclesIn u ρ B`: the cocycles `G → B^d` for `ρ` that obey the linear relations
  among the families `(u x g - 1)_x`.
* `New.Selmer.IsCommonRibetElement` (`FittingBlock`): one `f : S` that serves as Ribet element for
  a family `β` of functions `β i : Y → L`.
* `New.Selmer.IsTraceIdeal` (`FittingBlock`): `S` holds the characteristic polynomials, and the
  `S`-module `𝒥` holds the traces of given relations.
* `New.Selmer.tiedRows` (`RibetMatrices`): the rows whose element `∑ r i (gen i - 1)` lies in the
  tie ideal.

modules.title: Norms, logarithms and first-order deformations of the norm
modules.note:
The algebra behind the family of operators at the auxiliary places. A finite group maps to a ring
`R`, and a congruence `a ≡ b` is an equality `σ a = σ b` after a ring map `σ`. The file treats the
norm `Nm` (the sum of the group elements), the coefficients of a product of first-order deformations
`Nm j + α j ∂ j` of the norms `Nm j` of the factors of a product group (the `α j` are variables
and `∂ j ∈ R`), the first entry on the stabiliser of a line in `GL_N`, and logarithms, that is,
norms weighted by a homomorphism to `ℤ/m`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Patching.familyCoeff`, `New.Patching.exists_empty_eq_sum_and_insert_eq_mul`: the coefficients
  of `∏ (Nm j + α j ∂ j)` and their properties.
* `New.Patching.map_top_coeff_mul_C_sub_X_mul_C_eq_zero`,
  `New.Patching.exists_map_pow_mul_family_eq_mul_norm`: this product times any multiple of
  `t - α j r` has top coefficient `≡ 0` when `Nm j t = 0` and `∂ j t ≡ Nm j r`, and suitable
  multiples of the coefficients factor through the norm.
* `New.Patching.transfer_firstEntry`: over a finite field, the transfer to `GL_N` of the first entry
  on the stabiliser of a line is the determinant.
* `New.Patching.map_cosetNorm_mul_weightedSum_mul_cosetNormInv`,
  `New.Patching.map_sub_one_mul_weightedSum_valMinAbs`,
  `New.Patching.exists_map_valMinAbs_mul_sub_one`: three congruences for logarithms.
* `New.Patching.map_valMinAbs_eq_zero_of_shift`: a map on weights that kills all differences
  `f (· - k) - f` kills the logarithm modulo `m / (2 k)`.
* `New.Patching.cosetDerivative`, `New.Patching.exists_map_nsmul_mul_sub_one_eq_sum_mul`: the
  operator `∂` built from a logarithm on a subgroup; `n ∂ (g - 1)` is congruent to a multiple of the
  norm.

Notions from other files:
* `New.LocField w`, `New.LocInt w`, `New.ResField w`: for a finite place `w` of a number field, the
  completion `E_w`, its ring of integers `O_w` and its residue field, which has `w.q` elements.
* `New.localIntGL n w`: the subgroup `GL_n(O_w)` of `GL_n(E_w)`.

modules.title: Even classes and auxiliary places for Selmer cocycles
modules.note:
The file concerns cocycles of `Gal(Ω/E)` in the twists `O/ℓ^ν(-e)`. Here `Ω` is the algebraic
closure of `ℚ`, `E ⊆ Ω` is a CM field containing the `5040`-th roots of unity
(`New.CMFieldWithRoot5040`), and `O` is the ring of integers of a finite Galois extension of `ℚ_ℓ`
(`New.CoeffRing`). Further, `cyc` is the `ℓ`-adic cyclotomic character (`New.cyclotomicChar`),
`cyc mod N` is the one modulo `N` (`New.cyclotomicCharMod`), and `g^c = conjGal g` is the conjugate
of `g` by the chosen complex conjugation. The reciprocity law for even classes is in
`New.Congruences.FirstOrder.KummerMaps`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Selmer.evenClasses`: the even classes, that is the cocycles unramified off `ℓ` and a set of
  places and its conjugate that are invariant under `g ↦ g^c` and zero on the kernel of
  `cyclotomicChar` in the decomposition groups above `ℓ`.
* `New.Selmer.IsTameGeneratorFamily`: places `w j` off `ℓ`, tame generators `τ j`, and `φ j` fixing
  `μ_{ℓ^ν}`; `New.Selmer.withConjInv f` doubles a family by the `(f j ^ c)⁻¹`, which serve the
  conjugate places.
* `New.Selmer.IsPrimeTriangle`: an even class that kills the earlier elements `τ i`, and `φ i` of
  the same exponent, is killed at `τ j` up to a bounded power of `ℓ`.
* `New.Selmer.IsAuxTwist`: an auxiliary set of places with an anticyclotomic character whose values
  at tame generators are not too close to `1`.
* `New.Selmer.IsTameGeneratorFamily.mem_selmerModule_of_tame_eq_zero`: killing the doubled tame
  generators removes the ramification at the places `w j` and their conjugates.
* `New.Selmer.eq_zero_of_forall_mem_Z1_of_mem_evenClasses`: to show that an element `b` of
  `O / ℓ ^ ν` vanishes, given an even class `c`, it is enough to test `b` with the additive maps `u`
  to `ℤ/ℓ ^ ν` for which `u ∘ c` is a cocycle of the twist `-e`; in fact every `u` has this
  property.

Notions from other files:
* `New.selmerModule ρ S L B`: the locally constant cocycles of `ρ` with values in `B` that
  are unramified outside `S` and satisfy the relations `L`.
* `New.Selmer.tateTwist ℓ E O e`: the character `cyclotomicInv ℓ E O ^ e` as `1 × 1` matrices, where
  `cyclotomicInv` is `cyc⁻¹` with values in `O`.
* `New.Selmer.shaLocalSet ℓ E 1`: the elements of decomposition groups above `ℓ` with `cyc = 1`.
* `New.Z1` and `New.charRep`: the continuous cocycles of a representation, and the representation
  given by scalars through a character.

modules.title: Kummer maps
modules.note:
Throughout, `ℓ` is a prime and `E` is a CM field in the algebraic closure `Ω` of `ℚ` that contains a
primitive `5040`-th root of unity (`New.CMFieldWithRoot5040`). We pass from `E` to its maximal real
subfield `F`. We write `G = Gal(Ω/E)` and `G_F = Gal(Ω/F)`, `c` for the chosen complex conjugation
and `G_ν` for the elements of `G` that fix the `ℓ ^ ν`-th roots of unity. A Kummer map is the
restriction to `G` of a relation over `F` for the module `ℤ/ℓ^ν` on which `G_F` acts by a power of
`cyc⁺`, the extension to `G_F` of the cyclotomic character of `G` that is `1` at `c`.

* `New.Selmer.IsNuSplitPlace`: a prime of degree one off `ℓ` with a Frobenius element in `G_ν`.
* `New.Selmer.IsKummerMap`, `New.Selmer.IsKummerMap.hasKummerType`: Kummer maps are odd
  homomorphisms on `G_ν`, and conjugation by `g` multiplies those of exponent `e` by
  `cyc(g) ^ (e + 1)`.
* `New.Selmer.IsKummerMap.sum_eq_zero`: the reciprocity law for Kummer maps and even classes;
  `New.Selmer.IsKummerMap.nsmul_apply_tameGenerator_eq_zero` is the case where one term is left.
* `New.Selmer.exists_card_lt_finrank_kummerReductions`: there are many Kummer maps modulo `ℓ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.FrobeniusDatum`: a prime `w` of `E` of prime norm, a place `valuationSubring` of `Ω` above it
  and a geometric Frobenius element `frob` at that place.
* `New.RelationSetting`: a discrete Galois module with local conditions;
  `New.RelationSetting.relations` is the module of relations off a finite set `T` of primes, in
  place of dual cocycles; `New.Selmer.IsKummerMap` spells the notion out in the case used here.
* `New.Selmer.evenClasses`: for a coefficient ring `O` and a set `S` of primes of `E`, the even
  classes in `(O/ℓ^ν)(-e)` that are unramified off `ℓ`, `S` and `S̄` and vanish on
  `shaLocalSet ℓ E 1`, the elements of `ker cyc` in decomposition groups above `ℓ`.
* `New.cyclotomicCharMod`: the cyclotomic character modulo `N`; `New.cyclotomicChar` is the `ℓ`-adic
  one, written `cyc`.

modules.title: Cocycles of Tate twists: the even part and the triangle cost
modules.note:
This file studies cocycles of `Gal(Ω/E)` with values in a twist `(O/ℓ^ν)(-e)`
(`New.Selmer.tateTwist`). It shows that the even part of a cocycle lies in the even classes.
It shows that a cocycle that obeys the crystalline relations above `ℓ` vanishes on
`New.Selmer.shaLocalSet`. It also shows that a triangle of primes gives a triangle cost.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Selmer.add_conjGal_mem_evenClasses`: let `e ≠ 0`, and let a cocycle with values in
  `(O/ℓ^ν)(-e)` be unramified off ℓ, S and S̄ and zero on `New.Selmer.shaLocalSet`. Then its even
  part `c + c ∘ New.conjGal` lies in `New.Selmer.evenClasses`.
* `New.Selmer.hasTriangleCost_tateTwist`: let the tame generator family `w j`, with elements `τ j`,
  `φ j` and exponents `ty j`, form a triangle for `g₀` that holds up to `ℓ ^ h`
  (`New.Selmer.IsPrimeTriangle`), and let `e < t`. Let `Z` be a module of cocycles with values in
  `(O/ℓ^ν)(-e)`, unramified off `ℓ`, the `w j` and their conjugates, and let
  `cyclotomicInv g₀ ^ e - 1` kill the value at `g₀` of each member unramified off `ℓ`. Then the
  triangle cost of `Z` (`New.Selmer.HasTriangleCost`) is bounded by its length relative to the
  cocycles obeying the crystalline relations plus the length of the odd classes.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Selmer.tateTwist`: the rank-one representation `O(-e)`, given by the power `e` of the inverse
  `New.Selmer.cyclotomicInv` of the cyclotomic character. `New.conjGal`: the map g ↦ g^c = cgc,
  with c the chosen complex conjugation.
* `New.Selmer.shaLocalSet`: the union of the inertia groups above `ℓ` if `e = 0`; otherwise the
  elements of the decomposition groups above `ℓ` with trivial cyclotomic character.
* `New.Selmer.evenClasses`, `New.Selmer.shaOdd`: cocycles in `(O/ℓ^ν)(-e)` with local conditions
  above `ℓ`. Even classes are invariant under `New.conjGal`; odd classes are unramified off `ℓ` and,
  if `e ≠ 0`, change sign under it.
* `New.Selmer.IsPrimeTriangle`: a linearly ordered tame generator family `w j` with monotone
  exponents `ty j`. An even class of exponent `ty j` that kills the earlier `τ i`, and the earlier
  `φ i` of the same exponent, has its value at `τ j` killed by `ℓ ^ h`. Finitely many test points
  and `g₀` detect the cocycles unramified off `ℓ`, and `g₀` separates the characters up to `ℓ ^ h`.
* `New.Selmer.HasTriangleCost Z τ τ' φ φ' I C b`: for the members `Z₀` of `Z` that vanish on some
  set, agreement at the earlier pairs `τ i`, `τ' i` and, for `i ∈ I`, `φ i`, `φ' i` gives agreement
  at `τ j`, `τ' j` up to `C` for `j ∈ I`. The length of `Z / Z₀`, plus the length modulo `C`-torsion
  of any submodule of `Z₀` that is zero at all `τ j`, `τ' j` and agrees at the `φ j`, `φ' j` with
  `j ∈ I`, is at most `b`.

modules.title: Tied traces and the dictionary at one auxiliary place
modules.note:
Forms of the base data `D` are taken at principal level at the auxiliary places `Q.place j`. Each
isotypic space `x` has a Galois representation `N x`. This is the twist of `x.galRep` by a character
`a` that is trivial at the tame generators. This file shows that the coefficients of the
characteristic polynomials of the `N x` lie in the Hecke algebra, and so does the indicator function
of the systems congruent to a given one. It defines traces as members of the Hecke algebra, and the
ideal of the tied relations. At one place it gives the dictionary between Galois elements and
operators on forms: the tame generator acts as a diamond operator, and the Frobenius element acts
through the polynomial `p(Ũ)` in a normalised Hecke operator.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Patching.BaseLevel.charpoly_coeff_mem_heckeAlgebra`,
  `New.Patching.BaseLevel.exists_indicator_isCongruent`: the coefficients of characteristic
  polynomials, and the indicator function of the systems congruent to a given one, lie in the Hecke
  algebra.
* `New.Patching.BaseLevel.traceElement`, `New.Patching.BaseLevel.tiedIdeal`: traces as members of
  the Hecke algebra, and the ideal generated by the traces of the tied relations.
* `New.Patching.BaseLevel.tameTrace_smul_eq_diamond_sub_one`,
  `New.Patching.BaseLevel.tameTrace_smul_eq_aevalHecke`: operators on forms for the tame generator
  and for Frobenius.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Patching.BaseLevel.formsOfLevel`: the forms of the type fixed by `D` that have principal
  level at the places `L j` and maximal level at other places off `D.places` and its conjugate. The
  empty family `L = ![]` gives the base level.
* `New.Patching.BaseLevel.Eigensystem`, `New.Patching.BaseLevel.IsOffLevel`: the systems of level
  `L`, that is, the isotypic spaces (`New.Patching.Isotypic`, spaces of forms with given Hecke
  eigenvalues at almost all places) that contain a nonzero form of level `L`. For such an `x`,
  `(x : Isotypic V κ).val` is the space of forms. `w` is off level `L` if it lies off `D.places`,
  its conjugate and `ℓ`, and the forms of level `L` in each system are Hecke eigenforms at `w`.
* `New.Patching.BaseLevel.integralEnd`, `New.Patching.BaseLevel.localOperators`: the endomorphisms
  of the forms of level `L` that preserve the integral forms, and those among them that come from
  integral combinations of translations supported at `Q.place j` and its conjugate.
* `New.Patching.BaseLevel.heckeAlgebra`, `New.Patching.BaseLevel.heckeAction`: the `ℓ`-adic
  functions `t` on systems such that scaling each system `x` by `ιℓ.symm (t x)` preserves the
  integral forms, and the operator that such a function defines.
* `New.Patching.weightedSum`: `weightedSum ρ ind g = ∑ γ, g (ind γ) • ρ γ` for `g : ZMod m → ℤ`.

modules.title: Taylor–Wiles places in a triangle for the even classes, with prescribed Frobenii
modules.note:
Auxiliary (Taylor–Wiles) places that cut down the even classes of the Tate twists, with Frobenius
data in a prescribed set.

The places are indexed by an exponent e > 0 and a test point, and are chosen one after another. Step
1 finds a new Kummer map (`New.Selmer.IsKummerMap`) and an element that the earlier maps kill and at
which the value of the new map is a given product. Step 2 gets from Chebotarev's theorem a place
whose Frobenius element has twice these values under the maps, and at which even classes take twice
their value at the test point. Step 3 applies the reciprocity law of each Kummer map at its own
place and the later ones.

Throughout, ℓ is a prime, Ω is the algebraic closure of ℚ, and E is a CM field embedded in Ω that
contains a primitive 5040-th root of unity (`New.CMFieldWithRoot5040`); F is its maximal real
subfield, and `New.Selmer.primeBelowPlus` w is the prime of F below a prime w of E.
`New.cyclotomicChar` (written cyc) is the ℓ-adic cyclotomic character; G_ν is the kernel of its
reduction `New.cyclotomicCharMod` modulo ℓ^ν, and `New.conjGal` is the conjugation of Galois
elements by complex conjugation. The letter γ denotes a Galois element that separates the exponents;
in `New.Selmer.exists_isPrimeTriangle` it generates the Galois group modulo the kernel of cyc, and
the triangle is stated for γ⁻¹.

* `New.Selmer.exists_isPrimeTriangle`: for each ν > 0 there are Taylor–Wiles places of level ℓ^ν,
  indexed by one finite ordered set, that satisfy `New.Selmer.IsPrimeTriangle` and have their
  Frobenius data in a prescribed set.

Notions from other files:
* `New.CoeffRing`: The coefficient rings: rings of integers of the finite Galois extensions of ℚ_ℓ
  inside its algebraic closure.
* `New.Selmer.evenClasses`: The even classes: cocycles c in (O/ℓ^ν)(−e), O a coefficient ring,
  unramified off ℓ and a given set of places with their conjugates, with c(`conjGal` g) = c(g), that
  vanish on the elements of trivial cyc in the decomposition groups above ℓ.
* `New.Selmer.IsNuSplitPlace`: A condition on Frobenius data (w, A, σ), which consist of w of prime
  norm, A a place of Ω above w and σ a geometric Frobenius at A: w is not above ℓ, σ fixes μ_{ℓ^ν}.
* `New.Selmer.HasKummerType`: A continuous map to ℤ/ℓ^ν, an odd homomorphism on G_ν, that
  conjugation by a multiplies by cyc(a)^(e + 1); Kummer maps of exponent e have it.
* `New.Selmer.IsKummerMap`: A Kummer map of exponent e for a finite family x of split places, off a
  finite set T of primes of F: the restriction to Gal(Ω/E) of a relation over F. It has the Kummer
  type of exponent e and is unramified off T. For a finite family w of split places above distinct
  primes of F outside T it satisfies a reciprocity law: a linear relation among the values of a
  cocycle over F at the tame generators of w, with the values of the map at the Frobenius elements
  of w as coefficients. The cocycle must satisfy local conditions at the primes above ℓ and below
  the places of x.
* `New.Selmer.IsPrimeTriangle`: Ordered places whose tame generators and Frobenius elements cut down
  the even classes one after another, up to given powers of ℓ.
* `New.mostFrobenii`: The filter of most Frobenii. A set X of data (w, A, σ) belongs to it if each
  nonempty open set of Galois elements has a nonempty open part U such that, for almost all w, X
  contains every datum with σ ∈ U.
* `New.mostFrobeniiAt`: The filter of most Frobenii near g: the same filter, refined by the
  condition that σ lies near g.
modules.literature:
Taylor–Wiles primes, equally many at every ℓ-power level, are chosen in triangular form by means of
a count over the real subfield, which gives reciprocity laws for even classes in Tate twists. Each
new Frobenius kills the earlier Kummer maps but not the new one, and their reciprocity laws remove
the even classes. No bound for the even classes is needed; for small ℓ congruences between the
twists cost a power of ℓ for each prime. Tame ramification governed by Frobenius in the Kummer field
of units and the inductive choice of primes at every level are known. Related work: Gras–Munnier,
Extensions cycliques T-totalement ramifiées, 1998; Hajir–Maire–Ramakrishna, Tame Z/pZ-extensions
with prescribed ramification, 2022; Taylor–Wiles, Ring-theoretic properties of certain Hecke
algebras, 1995; Darmon–Diamond–Taylor, Fermat's Last Theorem (2.19), 1995; Dotto–Thorne, Residually
reducible representations of rank 2, 2026.

modules.title: The family of operators at the auxiliary places
modules.note:
Forms of the base data `D` are taken at principal level at the auxiliary places `Q.place j`. Each
isotypic space `x` has a Galois representation `N x`. This is the twist of `x.galRep` by a character
`a` that is trivial at the tame generators. This file builds the first-order term `∂` at one place.
It then builds the family `∏ (Nm j + α j ∂ j)` that kills the ideal of the tied relations. Finally
it shows that the top coefficient of Ribet's element clears the denominator of the projection to the
lifts.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Patching.BaseLevel.exists_mul_traceElement_tameGenerator_eq_frob`: the first-order term `∂`
  at one place.
* `New.Patching.BaseLevel.exists_deformed_norm_family`: the family `∏ (Nm j + α j ∂ j)`, with `Nm j`
  the sum over `GL_n` of the residue field of `Q.place j` and `α j` variables, kills the ideal of
  the tied relations and, up to powers of a Hecke operator `δ`, factors through the base level; both
  hold modulo `ℓ ^ ν / (2 n!)`.
* `New.Patching.BaseLevel.smul_top_coeff_mem_ellIntegralForms`,
  `New.Patching.BaseLevel.exists_diagOp_mem_ellIntegralForms`: the top coefficient of Ribet's
  element clears the denominator of the projection to the lifts.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Patching.BaseLevel.formsOfLevel`, `New.Patching.BaseLevel.Eigensystem`: the forms of the type
  fixed by `D` that have principal level at the places `L j` and maximal level at the other places
  off `D.places` and its conjugate. The empty family `L = ![]` gives the base level. Systems of
  level `L` are the isotypic spaces (`New.Patching.Isotypic`, spaces of forms with given Hecke
  eigenvalues at almost all places) that contain a nonzero form of level `L`.
* `New.Patching.BaseLevel.integralEnd`, `New.Patching.BaseLevel.localOperators`: the endomorphisms
  of the forms of level `L` that preserve the integral forms, and those among them that come from
  integral combinations of translations supported at `Q.place j` and its conjugate.
* `New.Patching.BaseLevel.heckeAlgebra`, `New.Patching.BaseLevel.heckeAction`: the `ℓ`-adic
  functions `t` on systems such that scaling each system `x` by `ιℓ.symm (t x)` preserves the
  integral forms, and the operator that such a function defines.
* `New.Patching.BaseLevel.traceElement` (in `New.Congruences.FirstOrder.TiedTraces`): the trace
  `x ↦ tr (P(N x h) N x g)` on systems of level `L`, as a member of the Hecke algebra.
* `New.Patching.BaseLevel.tiedIdeal` (in `New.Congruences.FirstOrder.TiedTraces`): the ideal of
  `𝕋[α]` generated by the `ℓ ^ ν tr[g]` and the traces of the tied relations
  `r j = γ j - 1 - α j (φ j - 1) H j (φ j)`.
modules.literature:
The norm map from one deep auxiliary level to the base level is deformed in parameters, one per
place, that tie tame inertia to Frobenius. The top coefficient of Ribet's Hecke element, a
polynomial in these parameters, clears the denominator of the projection to lifts up to a known
factor; the orders of the even classes do not enter the bound. Auxiliary tame level and first-order
derivatives in diamond operators occur in the literature in other settings. Related work: Wiles, The
Iwasawa conjecture for totally real fields, 1990; Lecouturier, Mazur–Tate conjecture for prime
conductor, 2019; Dotto–Thorne, Residually reducible representations of rank 2, 2026.

At a suitable Frobenius element, the Hecke polynomial of a weak lift is a full chain of roots times
a factor that is integral once normalised. With the chain lemma this gives, at each added place, an
integral operator on forms under which the tie of inertia to Frobenius holds and weak lifts do not
move. In the literature the chain lemma follows from the spherical unitary dual and Jacquet modules.
Related work: Tadić, Spherical unitary dual of GL(n), 1986; Casselman, Unramified principal series
of p-adic groups I, 1980; Clozel–Harris–Taylor, Automorphy for some l-adic lifts (Lemma 3.1.3,
§3.4), 2008.

modules.title: Chains of roots for weak lifts, and Hecke-stable subspaces of forms
modules.note:
Let `O` be a descent pair, with spaces W and V of ranks r < n, put t = n − r, and let `f` be a
nonzero eigenform on V with Galois representation R. Its normalised representation is u = R ⊗ χ. The
case of interest is that det (1 − u(g)) = 0 for all g, the condition that defines weak lifts.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Parameters`, `New.Data`: the fixed parameters P and admissible data D over them (numerical
  scales, ranks, levels); D determines the CM field E = `D.E`.
* `New.DescentPair`: places, weights and a hermitian space W of rank r, beside the definite space
  V = `New.stdSpace` of rank n > r; `New.DescentPair.rankDiff` is t = n − r. The forms on V have
  the weight (`columnCount`, `detExp`): column numbers and a power of the determinant at each
  infinite place.
* `New.Patching.Isotypic`: spaces of forms with given Hecke eigenvalues at almost all places; such a
  space `x` has Hecke polynomials `x.heckePolyAt w` and a Galois representation `x.galRep`.
* `New.Selmer.normalisedRep`: the twist of a Galois representation by the ℓ-adic character
  χ = `New.Selmer.normalizingAvatar`, the avatar of an algebraic Hecke character made from W.
* `Ω`: a fixed algebraic closure of ℚ, so that Gal(Ω/E) is the absolute Galois group of E.
* `New.mostFrobenii`: a filter on the triples of a place, a place of `Ω` over it and a geometric
  Frobenius element there.
* `ιℓ`: the fixed isomorphism ι from `ℂ` to `ℚ̄_ℓ`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Selmer.exists_diagonal_mem_norm_ge`: diagonal operators, one for each vector of a basis, are
  combined into one operator with an eigenvalue at each vector at least as large in norm.
* `New.Selmer.isRoot_hecke_chain`: if det (1 − u(g)) = 0 for all g, the Hecke polynomial at a split
  place w ∤ ℓ has the chain of roots X₀, X₀q, …, X₀q^(t−1), where q is the norm of w and
  ι(X₀) = χ(Frob_w)⁻¹.
* `New.Selmer.eventually_exists_hasRootChain`: for most Frobenius elements φ, if u has integral
  characteristic polynomials with root 1 and that of u(φ) is congruent to a product of S and ∏_{j<t}
  (X − c(φ)^j), with c the inverse cyclotomic character, for a polynomial S with ‖S(1)‖ ≥ 1, the
  rescaled Hecke polynomial is ∏ (X − q^i) times a divisor of an integral polynomial with value 1 at
  1.
* `New.Selmer.orthogonal_mem_invtSubmodule_heckePolyOnForms`, `New.Selmer.le_of_isotypic_mem`: the
  orthogonal complement of a Hecke-stable subspace Z is Hecke stable, and Z lies in a subspace N
  once every nonzero form of Z in an isotypic space lies in N.

modules.title: Constants, trace relations, lattices and local defects for Ribet's method
modules.note:
This file fixes the constants of Ribet's method: the bound `New.Selmer.oddClassBound` for the odd
classes, the local defect bound, the error term `New.Selmer.denominatorError` and the clearing
bound `New.Selmer.clearingBound`. It checks the trace relations and chooses block diagonal lattices
for representations with the trace of a twisted main summand plus `t` powers of the cyclotomic
character. It adds up the crystalline colengths of the summands and bounds the local defects.
Here `New.ellVal` is the valuation on `ℚ̄_ℓ` with `ellVal ℓ = 1`, with negative values replaced
by 0, and `New.inertiaAbove S` is the union of the inertia groups above `S`. The primes
`p₀ = D.levelPrime 0` and `p₁ = D.levelPrime 1` give the principal level.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Selmer.exists_blockDiagonal_lattice`: let the trace form be non-degenerate on the span of the
  image of `R'`, let `R'` have the trace of the twisted main summand `ψ R` plus the characters
  `O(-e)`, `e < t`, and let the twisted lattice `ψ' R₀` span all matrices over `O`. Then `R'` has a
  lattice that is block diagonal with summands `ψ' R₀` and the characters.
* `New.Selmer.crystallineColength_le_sum_dualDefect`: at each place `v` above `ℓ` let the lattices
  of all `u x` and of `ρ` lie in the class `InClass (F v) (C v) (U v)`. Then the crystalline members
  have colength, among Ribet's cocycles modulo `ℓ ^ M`, at most the sum over `v` of the defects
  `dualDefect`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.CoeffRing`: rings of integers of finite Galois extensions of `ℚ_ℓ` inside `ℚ̄_ℓ`; their
  `normLength` is length over `O`, scaled so that `O/ℓ` has length 1.
* `New.Selmer.tateTwist`: the rank-one representation `O(-e)`, given by the power `e` of the inverse
  `New.Selmer.cyclotomicInv` of the cyclotomic character.
* `New.Selmer.crystallineColength`: the length of the cocycles of a summand that obey the linear
  relations among the `u x g - 1`, modulo those that obey the crystalline relations above `ℓ`.
* `New.Selmer.IsLiftSetting`: a descent pair `V` (`New.DescentPair`) has the places of the data and
  of the twist `ϑ`, an odd rank `card r ≤ D.r` and an odd difference of ranks `V.rankDiff ≤ D.t`.
  Its type polynomials `c i` are monic squarefree polynomials of degree `card r` over the residue
  fields at the chosen places above `p₀` and `p₁`, with conditions on their roots.
* `New.Lift.InClass F C U`: the local lattices `Y` such that `Bmax ⊗ Y` is spanned by the periods
  fixed both near `1` and along the filter `F`, the Hodge–Tate jumps lie in the sets `U`, and every
  polynomial `Q` with `C s Q` kills the inertial element `s` on the periods.
modules.literature:
The torsion cocycles that Ribet's method produces in the summands of a lift's Galois representation
need not reduce from crystalline ones. Local duality and a case analysis on ℓ bound their total
distance from the crystalline condition, over all summands and places above ℓ, by an explicit bound.
It is known that torsion crystalline classes can miss reductions of crystalline ones by a bounded
defect that vanishes for small weights. Related work: Sweeting, Bloch–Kato conjecture for
four-dimensional symplectic representations, 2025; Chang–Diamond, Extensions of rank one
(φ,Γ)-modules, 2011; T. Liu, Torsion p-adic Galois representations and a conjecture of Fontaine,
2007.

modules.title: Ribet's element for conjugate self-dual representations
modules.note:
This file chooses the coefficient ring: polynomials over the integers of `ℚ̄_ℓ`, and models of the
representations, are defined over every large coefficient ring. It bounds the valuation at the lift
and counts the cocycles of the main summand at the lift by its loss and its Selmer group. It then
constructs Ribet's element for a finite family of conjugate self-dual `ℓ`-adic representations of
the Galois group of `E`, some of which have the trace of a twisted main summand plus `t` powers of
the cyclotomic character.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Selmer.exists_length_le_loss_add_crystallineSelmerLength`: with divisible coefficients, the
  cocycles of the main summand at the lift are counted by its loss, free of the level, and its
  Selmer group.
* `New.Selmer.ribet_columns`: Ribet's element and the bound on its coefficient of `∏ X j`.

Letters: the new places are `w j`, with tame generators `τ j`, Frobenius elements `φ j` and tied
relations `τ j - 1 - X j * (φ j - 1) * H j (φ j)`. The primes `p₀ = D.levelPrime 0`
and `p₁ = D.levelPrime 1` give the principal level; `g₀` is the element of the Galois group that
separates the characters.

Notions from other files:
* `New.CoeffRing`: rings of integers of finite Galois extensions of `ℚ_ℓ` inside `ℚ̄_ℓ`; their
  `normLength` is length over `O`, scaled so that `O/ℓ` has length 1.
* `New.Selmer.IsLiftSetting`: a descent pair `V` (`New.DescentPair`) has the places of the data and
  of the twist `ϑ`, an odd rank `card r ≤ D.r` and an odd difference of ranks `V.rankDiff ≤ D.t`.
  Its type polynomials `c i` are monic squarefree polynomials of degree `card r` over the residue
  fields at the chosen places above `p₀` and `p₁`, with conditions on their roots.
* `New.Lift.InClass F C U`: the local lattices `Y` such that `Bmax ⊗ Y` is spanned by the periods
  fixed both near `1` and along the filter `F`, the Hodge–Tate jumps lie in the sets `U`, and every
  polynomial `Q` with `C s Q` kills the inertial element `s` on the periods.
* `New.Selmer.IsPrimeTriangle`: a linearly ordered tame generator family `w j` with monotone
  exponents `ty j`. An even class of exponent `ty j` that kills the earlier `τ i`, and the earlier
  `φ i` of the same exponent, has its value at `τ j` killed by `ℓ ^ h`. Finitely many test points
  and `g₀` detect the cocycles unramified off `ℓ`, and `g₀` separates the characters up to `ℓ ^ h`.
* `New.Selmer.IsTameGeneratorFamily`: `w j` is not above `ℓ`, `τ j` is the chosen tame generator at
  a place over `w j`, and `φ j` fixes the `ℓ ^ ν`-th roots of unity.
* `New.Selmer.clearingBound` (in `New.Congruences.FirstOrder.TraceRelations`): the clearing bound
  `β_ℓ` per unit of rank of a main summand at `ℓ`.
* `New.Selmer.denominatorError` (in `New.Congruences.FirstOrder.TraceRelations`): the error term
  `e_ℓ`, with crude constants.
modules.literature:
Ribet's method in any rank, with congruent summands and tied primes, gives a Hecke element,
polynomial in the tie parameters, that kills all determinants det (1 - u g) modulo the ties. On
lifts it has no term properly dividing the product of all parameters, and the coefficient of that
product has bounded valuation; the orders of the even classes do not enter. Fitting-ideal forms of
Ribet's method are known for distinct summands in any rank and for congruent characters in rank 2.
Related work: Dasgupta–Kakde–Silliman–Wang, The residually indistinguishable case of Ribet's method
for GL2, 2023; Bellaïche–Chenevier, Families of Galois representations and Selmer groups, 2009;
Urban, Selmer groups and the Eisenstein–Klingen ideal, 2001.

modules.title: The bound for denominators
modules.note:
The bound that Ribet's method gives for the denominator of the orthogonal projection to `Z`: an
operator on `Z`, with eigenvalues of bounded valuation, takes the projection of every integral form
orthogonal to the false lifts to an integral form. `O` is a descent pair of hermitian spaces of
ranks `r < n` (`New.DescentPair`). `Z` is a subspace of its forms spanned by vectors in the ranges
of the idempotents `New.Selmer.typeProjection O c` of types `c` in lift setting.

The *chain* at a place of norm `q` is `∏ (X - q ^ i)`, `i < t'`, with `t' = O.rankDiff`.

* `New.Selmer.typeProjection_sub_starProjection_mem_of_isOrthogonalToFalseLifts`: a form orthogonal
  to the false lifts differs from its projection to `Z`, in each type, only outside the weak lifts.
* `New.Selmer.exists_operator_ellVal_le_liftValuationBound`: the bound for denominators. An operator
  on `Z` preserves the Hecke eigenspaces, has eigenvalues of valuation at most
  `New.Selmer.liftValuationBound` and takes projections of integral forms orthogonal to the false
  lifts to integral forms.
* `New.Selmer.denominatorLe_clearingBound`: if `Z` is spanned by lifts whose twisted main summands
  have small Selmer groups with divisible coefficients (`New.Selmer.IsLiftGenerator`), then
  `New.Selmer.DenominatorLe` holds with exponent `β log ℓ`, where
  `β = New.Selmer.clearingBound D ℓ`. Its operator is `D.chosenGroupOrder` times that of
  `exists_operator_ellVal_le_liftValuationBound` (`New.Selmer.exists_operator_det_clearingBound`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Selmer.AbsGal`: the absolute Galois group of the CM field `D.E` of the data `D`.
* `New.Data.chosenGroupOrder`: the product, over the chosen places above `D.levelPrime 0` and
  `D.levelPrime 1`, of the orders of the groups `GL (D.r * D.t)` over the residue fields.
* `New.Patching.Isotypic`: a system, that is the space of forms with given Hecke eigenvalues at
  almost all places. `B.Eigensystem L` is the set of systems that contain a nonzero form of level
  `L` over the base data `B`; the base level is `L = ![]`.
* `New.Selmer.normalisedRep`: the twist of a Galois representation by the character
  `normalizingAvatar O`.
* `New.Selmer.IsAuxTwist`: the character is anticyclotomic, its modulus avoids the given places and
  its ramification has bounded valuation.
modules.literature:
For a twist with short Selmer groups, an operator of bounded ℓ-adic valuation clears the denominator
of the projection to theta lifts on integral forms orthogonal to the false lifts. The bound counts
local losses, class number, level, odd classes and congruences between the characters; the orders of
the even classes, where Vandiver's conjecture lives, do not enter. Ribet-type bounds, Taylor–Wiles
primes in the residually reducible case and the mass formula case are treated in the following
works. Related work: Dasgupta–Kakde–Silliman–Wang, The residually indistinguishable case of Ribet's
method for GL2, 2023; Dotto–Thorne, Modularity of residually reducible representations of rank 2,
2026; Martin–Wakatsuki, Mass formulas and Eisenstein congruences in higher rank, 2024.

modules.title: Auxiliary primes, anticyclotomic characters, slopes and ties
modules.group: Anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups
modules.note:
The setting is a CM field `E` and anticyclotomic characters of `Gal(Ω/E)` with values in `ℤ/q`. The
file defines data at auxiliary primes and sets of auxiliary primes. Chebotarev's theorem yields
auxiliary primes carrying such data.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.IsAuxPrimeDataAt`: a prime `P ≠ P̄` of norm `≡ 1 mod q` outside `T`, with a Frobenius
  element, a generator of tame inertia and a character to `ℤ/q` that comes from an idele class
  character of level `P` (`New.IsFromU1`).
* `New.IsAuxiliary`: finite sets of primes of prime norm, disjoint from their conjugates, with
  neither the primes nor their conjugates in `S`.
* `New.Selmer.exists_anticyclotomicChar_of_frob_fixes_roots`: a Galois character that sends the tame
  generator above a prime `P` to the generator `1 ∈ ℤ/q` and comes from an idele class character of
  level `P`.
* `New.Selmer.exists_isAuxPrimeDataAt`: an auxiliary prime `P` of `E` of prime norm with data
  `New.Selmer.AuxPrimeData`. These include a Frobenius element close to a given element of the
  normal closure of the inertia groups at the places of a finite set `R` outside `S ∪ S̄` and not
  above `ℓ`, and a character of `Gal(Ω/E)` to `ℤ/ℓ^N` that is trivial at this Frobenius element. The
  data satisfy `New.IsAuxPrimeDataAt` for every `T` contained in `S ∪ {v ∣ ℓ}`.
* `New.Selmer.IsTiedPrimes`: a set `J` of auxiliary primes with their data (place, tame generator
  `γ = tameGenerator`, Frobenius `φ = frob`, character, slopes) and a first prime `P₀`.
* `New.Selmer.tieRelations`: the relations `z γ = s • z φ` imposed on cocycles at the primes of `J`
  and their conjugates.

Notions from other files:
* `New.IsFrob`: `σ` stabilises the valuation subring `A` and `σ • x ≡ x ^ q` modulo the maximal
  ideal for all `x ∈ A`.
* `New.IsPlaceOver.tameGenerator`: a chosen generator of tame inertia at a place above `w`, as an
  element of the inertia group.
* `New.idOrConjInv`: `g` if `b` is true, and `g^{-c} = (conjGal g)⁻¹` if `b` is false.

modules.title: Selmer data, tied Selmer groups and classes as functions
modules.group: Anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups
modules.note:
A lattice `T` is given by matrices `ρ g` over `O`, and `W = (O / a) ^ n` is its reduction modulo
`a`. The datum includes an element `γ_*` of the Galois group that acts on `T` by a scalar `ζ_*`
with `ζ_* ^ 2 - 1` a unit. A class in `H¹(E, W)` is identified with its cocycle that vanishes at
`γ_*`.

* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum`: a lattice with modules `Z_w` of local cocycles above `ℓ`;
  `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.β` is the sum of a global term and local terms.
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.localRelations`,
  `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.length_localCocycles_le_finrank_mul`: the linear relations that hold on
  the `Z_w`, and the length of the local cocycles that obey them.
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.tiedSelmer`: the classes with ties at auxiliary primes.
* `New.Selmer.IsNewAuxiliaryPrime`: the primes that may be added.
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.sahGroup`, `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.span_image_sahGroup_eq_top`: the group
  `H` generated by commutators with `γ_*` and `γ_*^c`, on which classes are detected.
* `New.Selmer.congruenceTerm_le`: a bound for the global term from one element that acts by scalars.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Selmer.IsTiedPrimes`: a set `J` of auxiliary primes ("tied primes") with places, Frobenius
  elements `φ`, tame generators `γ`, characters to `ℤ / ℓ ^ N` and slopes, and a first prime
  `P₀ ∈ J`.
* `New.IsAuxPrimeDataAt`: for auxiliary data at a prime `P`, says that they consist of a place
  over `P`, a Frobenius, the tame generator `γ` and a character with value `1` at `γ` that is
  unramified outside `P` and its conjugate and kills the decomposition groups above a given set.
* `New.idOrConjInv`: `g` if `b` is true, and `g^{-c} = (conjGal g)⁻¹` if `b` is false.
modules.literature:
Known result: Sah's lemma, by which cocycles vanishing at an element that acts by a scalar `ζ` with
`ζ - 1` a unit are detected on commutators.

See `New.Congruences.Selmer.Descent` for related work.

modules.title: The dual of a tied Selmer group and the count
modules.group: Anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups
modules.note:
The dual group is a module of relations at split primes, and the count is the Greenberg–Wiles
inequality with the local terms estimated above `ℓ`, at the other places of `S`, and at the ties.

* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.dualSelmer`: the dual of the tied Selmer group.
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.exists_length_tiedSelmer_le`: the tied group is no longer than its dual,
  up to the local terms at the places of `S` prime to `ℓ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum`: a lattice `T = O ^ n` with Galois action `T.ρ`, unramified outside the
  finite set `S = T.places ⊆ S₀`, a module `Z_w = T.Z w` of local cocycles for each `w ∣ ℓ`, and an
  element `γ_* = T.γ` that acts by a scalar. The local conditions `T.localRelations` are the linear
  relations that hold on the modules `Z_w`. The module `T / a` is `n → QuotSpan a`.
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.tiedSelmer T R J x i a`: the cocycles with values in `T / a` that are
  unramified outside `S ∪ R ∪ R̄` and obey `T.classRelations` (the local conditions
  `T.localRelations` and vanishing at `γ_*`) and the ties of index `i` on `J`.
* `New.Selmer.IsTiedPrimes ℓ S₀ V W N P₀ J x`: a set `J` of auxiliary primes, which with their
  conjugates lie outside `S₀`. Here `(x v).1` holds a tame generator `γ_v` and a Frobenius element
  `φ_v` at `v ∈ J`, and `(x v).2 i` is the slope at `v` for the index `i`. The first prime `P₀ ∈ J`
  has slope `0` and `φ_{P₀} ∈ W`. Where the slope for `i` is not zero, `φ_v` and `φ_v^{-c}` satisfy
  the condition `V i`.
* `New.Selmer.tieRelations`: the ties `z(γ_w) = s • z(φ_w)` with slope `s` at the primes `w` of `J`
  and of `J̄`; `New.Selmer.unionWithConj S J` is the set `S ∪ J ∪ J̄`.
* `New.Selmer.localCocycles`: the restrictions to a decomposition group of the cocycles that obey
  given relations.
* `New.RelationSetting`: a finite Galois module with local conditions;
  `New.RelationSetting.relations` is the module of relations at split primes, in place of dual
  cocycles.

modules.title: Reciprocity at conjugate primes
modules.group: Anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups
modules.note:
Given a tied class `z` of full order whose Frobenius values at all new auxiliary primes are tame
values, one attaches to each member `y` of the dual group a `G`-map `η : T / a → (T / a)^{*c}` with
`η(z(h)) = y(h^c)` on `H`, which determines `y`. Here `G = Gal(Ω/E)`, `T / a` is the lattice modulo
`a`, `g^c = New.conjGal g` is the conjugate of `g` by complex conjugation, and `(T / a)^{*c}` is
the Cartier dual of `T / a` with `g` acting through `g^c`. The proof shows that the form
`Ψ(h, h') = ⟨z(h), y(h')⟩ - ⟨z(h'^c), y(h^c)⟩` vanishes on `H × H`.

* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.exists_isNewAuxiliaryPrime`: there are new auxiliary primes whose
  Frobenius element is near any element of `γ₀ H`, where `γ₀` is the tame generator at the first
  prime.
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.mirrorForm_self_eq_zero`: first step, `Ψ(h, h) = 0` by reciprocity.
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.mirrorForm_eq_zero`: second step, `Ψ = 0` by conjugation with `γ_*`.
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.exists_linearMap_apply_eq_dualSelmer_conj`: third step, the map `η`.
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.length_dualSelmer_le`: the dual group has length at most `globalTerm(T)`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum`: a lattice `T = O ^ n` with Galois action `T.ρ`, local conditions and an
  inertial element `γ_* = T.γ` that acts by a scalar; `T.tiedSelmer` is its tied Selmer group.
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.reductionKer`, `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.sahGroup`: the kernel `U` of the
  action on `T / ℓ ^ M` and `μ_{ℓ ^ N}`, and the group `H` generated by all `[g, γ_*]` and
  `[g, γ_*^c]`.
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.dualSelmer`: the dual of the tied Selmer group, formed for a finite set
  `R` of primes. Its members are equivariant homomorphisms from `U` to the characters
  `T / a → ℚ/ℤ`, extended by zero to `Gal(Ω/E)`, that are unramified outside `R \ {P₀, P̄₀}` and
  satisfy reciprocity at split primes outside that set.
* `New.Selmer.IsTiedPrimes`: says that `J` is a set of auxiliary primes with data `x` (place,
  Frobenius element, tame generator, character, slopes). It has a first prime `P₀`, whose Frobenius
  element lies in `W` and whose slopes are `0`, so that tied classes are unramified there.

modules.title: The universal twist and one system of equations for all twists
modules.group: Anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups
modules.note:
For homomorphisms `h_j : G → ℤ / q` let `ψ_X(g) = ∏ (1 + X_j) ^ (h_j g)`, and let `Sel(x)` be the
Selmer module of the twist of a representation by the value `ψ_x` at a point `x`. The members of all
`Sel(x)` are functions on one finite quotient of the Galois group, and the cocycle rule and the
other conditions are linear equations over `O[X]` for their values.

* `New.Selmer.universalChar`, `New.Selmer.IsTiedPrimes.universalChar_frob`,
  `New.Selmer.IsTiedPrimes.universalChar_tame_gen`: the polynomial `ψ_X` and its values at the
  auxiliary primes.
* `New.Selmer.finite_selmerModule`: for finite `S` and `ρ` locally constant modulo `ℓ ^ M`, the
  Selmer module with coefficients in a finite `O / a`, `a ∣ ℓ ^ M`, is finite.
* `New.Selmer.exists_matrix_selmerAtPoint_equiv`: there is one matrix `A` over `O[X]` such that each
  `Sel(x)` is isomorphic to the kernel of `A(x)` on a power of `O' / ℓ ^ M`.
* `New.Selmer.exists_isLeast_length_selmerAtPoint`, `New.Selmer.exists_sharp_polynomial`: the
  valuations of a set of polynomials (in the proof, maximal minors) bound the lengths of `Sel(x)` at
  all points over discrete valuation rings of characteristic zero, and one is sharp at a given
  point.

Notions from other files:
* `New.selmerModule ρ S L B`: the locally constant cocycles for `ρ` with values in `B ^ n` that are
  unramified outside `S` and obey the relations `L`.
* `New.obeying`, `New.mapRel`: a relation is a finitely supported `f : Γ →₀ Matrix n n O`; a
  function `c` obeys it if `∑ γ, f γ • c γ = 0`, and `mapRel e f` applies `e` to all entries of `f`.
* `New.Selmer.IsTiedPrimes ℓ S₀ V W N P₀ J d`: a finite set `J` of primes that, with their
  conjugates, avoid `S₀`, and a first prime `P₀ ∈ J`. At `v ∈ J`, `(d v).1` holds a place, a
  Frobenius element `φ`, a tame generator `γ` and a character to `ℤ / ℓ ^ N`, and `(d v).2 i ∈ O` is
  the slope for the index `i : ι`. The Frobenius element of `P₀` lies in `W`, and where the slope
  for `i` is not zero, the condition `V i` holds at `φ` and at `(c φ c)⁻¹` for the complex
  conjugation `c`.
* `New.QuotSpan a`, `New.Selmer.reduceModPow ℓ M ρ`: the ring `O / a`, and `ρ` modulo `ℓ ^ M`.

modules.title: The descent
modules.group: Anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups
modules.note:
Primes are added as long as this makes the tied Selmer groups modulo `ϖ ^ k`, `1 ≤ k ≤ e`, shorter.
When no prime does, reciprocity bounds the dual Selmer group at the level given by the exponent of
the tied group, and the comparison of the lengths of the two groups gives the bound for the tied
group. All data are treated at once: a prime that is added for one datum has slope `0` for the
others, which means that their classes stay unramified there. Lengths count composition factors, so
that each step lowers the sum of the lengths by at least `1`.

* `New.Selmer.tilting`: off few residues of `a`, the kernel of `a • evγ - evφ` is short.
* `New.Selmer.exists_slope_totalTiedLength_lt`: one step of the descent.
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.length_tiedSelmer_pow_le`: the bound when no step is possible.
* `New.Selmer.exists_isTiedPrimes_card_le_and_length_le`: boundedly many new primes with slopes make
  the tied Selmer groups of finitely many data short.

Throughout, `E` is a number field with a chosen embedding into the algebraic closure `Ω` of `ℚ`
(`New.EmbeddedNumberField`). From the first prime on, `E` is a CM field, `ℓ` is a prime
(`New.ThePrime`) and `S₀` is a finite set of finite places of `E`; for the Selmer data, `O` is the
integer ring of a finite extension of `ℚ_ℓ` (`New.PadicIntegerRing`).

Notions from other files:

* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum ℓ S₀ g₀ O n`: a Galois lattice `T = Oⁿ` with local conditions, unramified
