modules.literature:
Lowering Selmer groups mod ℓ^n by new local conditions at Chebotarev primes with trivial Frobenius
is known in the literature. Related work: Fakhruddin–Khare–Patrikis, Relative deformation theory,
relative Selmer groups, and lifting irreducible Galois representations, 2021; Mazur–Rubin,
Diophantine stability, 2018; Darmon–Diamond–Taylor, Fermat's Last Theorem, 1995.

modules.title: The failure to be tied
modules.group: Anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups
modules.note:
At a prime of norm `≡ 1` modulo `ℓ ^ N`, a Frobenius element `φ` and an inertial element `γ` commute
up to wild inertia and `ℓ ^ N`-th powers of inertia. If these act trivially and a cocycle `z`
vanishes on them, then `z(γ φ) = z(φ γ)`, which is the relation `(φ - 1) z(γ) = (γ - 1) z(φ)`.

Let `𝔮₀` be the first auxiliary prime and `s_𝔮` the slopes at the others. At a point of the line
`X_{𝔮₀} = Y`, `X_𝔮 = s_𝔮 Y` the relation puts `tie_w(z) = z(γ_w) - s_𝔮 z(φ_w)`, for `w = 𝔮, 𝔮̄`, in
the kernel of `φ_w - 1` for the twisted action. At `Y = 0` it does the same for `z(γ_w)`,
`w = 𝔮₀, 𝔮̄₀`. The valuation of a determinant bounds the length of the kernel.

* `New.Selmer.sub_one_smul_eq_of_tame`: the relation.
* `New.Selmer.selmerOnLine`: the Selmer module of the twist at a point of the line.
* `New.Selmer.IsTiedPrimes.relLength_tied_le`: the failure to be tied at the primes other than the
  first is at most `v(P¹(y))`, where `P¹ = New.Selmer.tiePolynomial`.
* `New.Selmer.IsTiedPrimes.relLength_tieRelations_le_sum_addVal_det`: the cost of dropping the ties
  at the first prime and its conjugate, at the point `0`.

Letters: `J` is the set of all auxiliary primes, `P₀ ∈ J` is the first prime `𝔮₀`, and `d` attaches
to `v ∈ J` the elements `φ_v = (d v).1.frob` and `γ_v = (d v).1.tameGenerator`, the homomorphism
`λ_v = (d v).1.character` to `ℤ / ℓ ^ N` and, for each index `i : ι`, the slope `(d v).2 i`.
Coefficients are taken modulo `ℓ ^ M`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Selmer.IsTiedPrimes`: an auxiliary set `J` of primes with places, Frobenius elements `φ`,
  tame generators `γ`, characters to `ℤ / ℓ ^ N` and slopes, and a first prime `P₀ ∈ J`.
* `New.Selmer.tieRelations`: the ties `z(γ) = s z(φ)` at the primes of a set and at their
  conjugates.
* `New.Selmer.universalChar`: the polynomial `ψ_X(g) = ∏ (1 + X_j) ^ (h_j g)`;
  `New.Selmer.selmerAtPoint` is the Selmer module `Sel(x)` of the twist by `ψ_x`.

modules.title: Stickelberger systems
modules.group: Anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups
modules.note:
A Stickelberger system consists of elements `Θ_Q` of the group rings over `ℤ̄_ℓ` of the class groups
`Cl_Q` of norm-one finite ideles, one for each finite set `Q` of places. Their values under
characters for `Q` change by Euler factors when `Q` grows to an auxiliary set. A character for
`Q` is a Galois character with `IsFromU1 (placesDividing E ℓ) Q`; it is read on `Cl_Q` through
`y / ȳ ↦ Art y`. Its order is not assumed to be a power of `ℓ`.

* `New.Selmer.U1ClassGroup`, `New.Selmer.groupRingEval`: the group `Cl_Q`, and the value of a
  function on the Galois group at an element of its group ring.
* `New.Selmer.StickelbergerSystem`, `New.Selmer.StickelbergerSystem.β`: the systems and their
  constant.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Ω`: the algebraic closure of `ℚ` into which every number field in this file is embedded;
  `Gal(Ω/E)` is the absolute Galois group of `E`, and `New.ClosurePlace` is the type of places
  (valuation subrings) of `Ω`.
* `New.IsFromU1 S I χ`, for sets `S` and `I` of finite places of a CM field `E`: the Galois
  character `χ` is locally constant and satisfies `χ(Art y) = η(y / ȳ)` for an idele class
  character `η` that is trivial on the local components at `S` and its conjugates and has
  modulus `I` away from these places.
* `New.IsAuxiliary S Q`: the places of `Q` have prime norm, neither they nor their conjugates lie in
  `S`, and their conjugates lie outside `Q`.
* `New.ellVal`: the valuation `v` on `ℚ̄_ℓ` with `v ℓ = 1`, cut off below at `0`; `New.intQpBar ℓ`
  is the ring `ℤ̄_ℓ` of integral elements.
* `New.artinMap`: the Artin map from the finite ideles to the abelianised Galois group.

modules.title: Stickelberger systems on a line
modules.group: Anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups
modules.note:
Let `P = ψ_X(Θ_J)` be the value of the polynomial character `ψ_X = ∏_j (1 + X_j) ^ h_j` at the
element `Θ_J` of a Stickelberger system, where `J` is a set of tied auxiliary primes, the first
prime `P₀` included. On the line on which all variables but the one of `P₀` vanish, `P` is a
polynomial `P(X, 0)` in one variable. Up to a power of `1 + X` it is congruent to `R₀ R₁` modulo
`(1 + X) ^ ℓ ^ N - 1`. Here `R₀` comes from the element for `{P₀}` and has `v(R₀(0)) ≤ β` if
`ϑ(φ_{P₀})` is close enough to `ϑ(g₀)` and `N` is large, and `R₁` comes from the Euler factors at
the other primes and has small Gauss valuation. If `ρ ≤ 1` and `v_ρ(R₀ R₁) < N ρ`, the congruence
bounds the valuation of `P` at a point where `R₀ R₁` attains its Gauss valuation.

* `New.Selmer.StickelbergerSystem.exists_congruence_lineChar_element`: the congruence.
* `New.Selmer.StickelbergerSystem.exists_point_ellVal_universalChar_le`: an upper bound for the
  valuation of `P` at some point whose coordinates have valuation at least `ρ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Selmer.StickelbergerSystem`: elements `Θ_Q` of the group rings of class groups `Cl_Q` with a
  norm relation, a character `ϑ`, a list of integers `e`, and the number `β`.
* `New.Selmer.IsTiedPrimes`: an auxiliary set `J` of primes with places, Frobenius elements `φ`,
  tame generators `γ`, characters `h` to `ℤ / ℓ ^ N` and slopes, and a first prime `P₀ ∈ J`; for
  primes `v, w ≠ P₀` of `J` one has `h_{P₀}(φ_v) = 1` and `h_w(φ_v) = 0`.
* `New.Selmer.groupRingEval`: the value of a function on `Gal(Ω/E)`, read on `Cl_Q` and extended
  linearly, at an element of the group ring of `Cl_Q`.
* `New.ellVal`: the valuation `v` of `ℚ̄_ℓ` with `v(ℓ) = 1`, cut off at `0` from below;
  `New.intQpBar` is its valuation ring.
* `New.Selmer.gaussVal`: the Gauss valuation `v_ρ(g) = min_i (v(y_i) + ρ i)` of `g = ∑ y_i Y ^ i`.

modules.title: Restriction to a line
modules.group: Anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups
modules.note:
For Selmer data and Stickelberger systems there is an integer `s₀` such that, for each radius `r`
with `0 < r` and `s₀ r < 1` and each large `N`, we find auxiliary primes `𝔮` and, for each datum and
each system, a polynomial `P` in variables `X_𝔮`. At a point `x = (ζ_𝔮 - 1)_𝔮` given by `ℓ ^ N`-th
roots of unity, `v(P(x))` bounds the length of the twisted Selmer group of a datum `T` if it is less
than `β_T + 1`, and `P(x)` is the twisted value of a system. At some point with coordinates of
valuation at least `r`, the valuation of `P` is at most `β + s₀ r`, where `β` is the number of the
datum or system. For a datum this point is taken on the line `X_{𝔮₀} = Y`, `X_𝔮 = s_𝔮 Y`, where `𝔮₀`
is the first prime and the `s_𝔮` are the slopes of the datum at the other primes.

For a datum, `v(P(x))` is bounded by `v(P⁰(y)) + v(P¹(y))` at the point `x` of the line with
`Y = y`. Here `P⁰` is the restriction to the line of a minor for the tied module that is sharp at
`0`, so that `v(P⁰(0)) ≤ β_T`, the polynomial `P¹` bounds the failure to be tied, and `y` is generic
for both.

* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.TwistedLengthLe`: a bound for the length of the twisted Selmer group.
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.exists_boundsSelmer_and_eval_dvd`,
  `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.exists_boundsSelmer_ellVal_eval_le`: the choice of `P⁰`, of `y` and of the
  polynomial `P` of a datum.
* `New.Selmer.IsTorsionLevel`: the power `ℓ ^ M` modulo which the Selmer modules are computed.
* `New.Selmer.TwistPolynomials`, `New.Selmer.exists_twistPolynomials`: the primes, polynomials and
  points.

Letters: for a set of tied primes (`New.Selmer.IsTiedPrimes`), `J` is the set `Q` of all auxiliary
primes, `P₀ ∈ J` is the first prime `𝔮₀`, and `d` attaches to `v ∈ J` a Frobenius element, a tame
generator, the homomorphism `λ_v = (d v).1.character` to `ℤ / ℓ ^ N` and the slopes `(d v).2 i`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.selmerModule ρ S L B`: the locally constant cocycles for `ρ` with values in `B ^ n` that are
  unramified outside `S` and obey the linear relations `L`. The coefficients `B` are
  `New.QuotSpan a = O / a` or `New.Selmer.DivisibleQuot O = Frac(O) / O`.
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum`: a lattice `T` with local conditions and the number `β_T`;
  `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.tiedSelmer` is its tied Selmer group.
* `New.Selmer.StickelbergerSystem`: elements `Θ_Q` of the group rings of class groups `Cl_Q` with a
  norm relation, and the number `β`.
* `New.CoeffRing`: rings of integers of finite Galois extensions of `ℚ_ℓ` inside `ℚ̄_ℓ`;
  `New.CoeffRing.normLength` scales lengths so that `O / ℓ` has length `1`.

modules.title: Roots of unity `ζ` with polynomials hardly more divisible at `ζ - 1` than at given points
modules.group: Anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups
modules.note:
For `ρ > 0`, `ε > 0`, finitely many integral polynomials `P_i` in at most `s₀` variables and points
`x_i` whose coordinates have valuation at least `ρ`, with a bound on `∑ v(P_i(x_i))`, we find roots
of unity `ζ_j` of `ℓ`-power order with `v(ζ_j - 1) ≤ ρ` such that `v(P_i((ζ_j - 1)_j))` exceeds
`v(P_i(x_i))` by at most `ε`. The orders of the `ζ_j` are bounded before the polynomials are given.

* `New.Selmer.exists_rootOfUnity_eval_le_gaussVal_add`: the step in one variable, by counting roots.
* `New.Selmer.exists_rootsOfUnity_ellVal_eval_le_add`: several variables, by moving one coordinate
  of all points at a time.

Notions from other files:
* `New.ThePrime ℓ`: the class saying that `ℓ` is prime and is the prime in scope.
* `New.ellVal`: the valuation `v(x) = max (-log_ℓ |x|) 0` on `ℚ̄_ℓ`, with `v ℓ = 1` and `v 0 = ∞`;
  `New.intQpBar ℓ` is the ring `ℤ̄_ℓ` of integral elements.
* `New.Selmer.gaussVal`: the Gauss valuation `v_ρ(g) = min_i (v(y_i) + ρ i)` of `g = ∑ y_i Y ^ i`.
modules.literature:
Finitely many integral polynomials of any degree that are little divisible at given points of
positive valuation remain so at a single tuple of `ζ - 1`, with `ζ` roots of unity of `ℓ`-power
order. A degree-free bound at some `ℓ`-power root of unity for one element is known in the
literature. Related work: Kriz–Nordentoft, Horizontal p-adic L-functions, 2023; Serban, An
infinitesimal p-adic multiplicative Manin–Mumford conjecture, 2018; Kurihara, The structure of
Selmer groups of elliptic curves and modular symbols, 2014.

modules.title: Twisting, general form
modules.group: Anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups
modules.note:
For finitely many Selmer data and Stickelberger systems (under the hypotheses of
`New.Selmer.exists_anticyclotomic_twist`) there is one anticyclotomic character whose first `m`
powers have short Selmer groups, values of small valuation at the elements of the systems, and
values far from `1` at the tame generators. The character is `∏ ζ_𝔮 ^ λ_𝔮`, with the `λ_𝔮` of
`New.Selmer.exists_twistPolynomials` and roots of unity `ζ_𝔮` from
`New.Selmer.exists_rootsOfUnity_ellVal_eval_le_add`.

* `New.Selmer.IsSmallTwist`: the bounds for one character.
* `New.Selmer.exists_rootsOfUnity_ellVal_eval_le`: roots of unity that serve all powers up to `m`.
* `New.Selmer.exists_anticyclotomic_twist`: one twist that works for all powers up to `m`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum ℓ S₀ g₀ O n`: a lattice `T = O ^ n` with an action of `Gal(Ω/E)`
  unramified outside `S₀`, local conditions above `ℓ`, and the number `β_T`, which includes the
  valuations of `det(ρ g - 1)` for `g = g₀` and its conjugate inverse. `TwistedLengthLe Q ψ b`
  says that its Selmer group `Sel_Q(T ψ)` has normalised length at most `b` over all large
  coefficient rings (`CoeffRing.normLength`: `len (O / ℓ) = 1`).
* `New.Selmer.StickelbergerSystem ℓ S₀ g₀`: a character `ϑ` with
  `ϑ g₀ ≠ 1`, elements `Θ_Q` of the group rings of class groups `Cl_Q` with a norm relation, and
  the number `β`.
* `New.Selmer.TwistPolynomials T Y s₀ r N`: an auxiliary set `Q` of at most `s₀ / 2` primes,
  homomorphisms `λ_𝔮` to `ℤ / ℓ ^ N` for `𝔮 ∈ Q`, and for each datum and system a polynomial in
  variables indexed by `Q` with a point whose coordinates have valuation at least `r`.
* `New.ellVal`: the valuation `v` on `PadicAlgCl ℓ` with `v(ℓ) = 1`, read in `[0, ∞]`.

modules.title: Main summands are Selmer data
modules.group: Anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups
modules.note:
A row is an `ℓ`-adic representation `R` that satisfies `IsMainSummandLike`. A main summand is a
lattice `u` in a row `R`, with the crystalline conditions above `ℓ`; the row is the main summand
with scalars extended to `ℚ̄_ℓ`.

* `New.Selmer.IsMainSummandLike.eventually_exists_selmerDatum`: over all large coefficient rings a
  row has a lattice that is a Selmer datum, with bounds for the global and the local terms.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Selmer.IsMainSummandLike`: the hypotheses on an `ℓ`-adic representation of the Galois group
  of `D.E` under which its Selmer groups are estimated.
* `New.Selmer.IsLatticeIn`: `u` over the coefficient ring `O` is conjugate to `R` over `ℚ̄_ℓ`.
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum`: a lattice `T` with local conditions and the number `β_T`.
* `New.Selmer.crysCocyclesAt`, `New.Selmer.crysRelations`: the crystalline cocycles at a place above
  `ℓ`, and the linear relations that hold on them.
* `New.CoeffRing.normLength`: a length over `O`, rescaled so that `O / ℓ` has length `1`.

modules.title: L-values of a pair as integral measures, and avatars of tame characters
modules.group: Anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups
modules.note:
For a pair `p` (`New.Data.CriticalPair`: a character `ν` of U(1) and a point `z`) ramified at the
chosen places, ratios of the values `L(z, (ν ϑ)⁻¹)`, as `ϑ` runs over tame characters
(`New.Data.TameChar`), are interpolated over `ℂ` by integral measures. The `ℓ`-adic form is in
`New.Congruences.Selmer.LValueSystems`.

* `New.Data.CriticalPair.exists_isTwistMeasure`: a function `F` of `ϑ` that is an integral measure
  at every modulus (`New.Data.TameChar.IsIntegralMeasure`) and gives a power of the ratio of
  `L`-values `New.Data.CriticalPair.ratio` on twists (`New.Data.CriticalPair.IsTwistMeasure`); the
  cases `z ≥ 2` and `z = 1` are `New.Data.CriticalPair.isTwistMeasure_integralAlgebraicPart` and
  `New.Data.CriticalPair.exists_isTwistMeasure_of_z_eq_one`.
* `New.Selmer.exists_tameChar_invAvatar_eq`: an anticyclotomic Galois character of auxiliary
  modulus that is trivial above `ℓ` is the `ℓ`-adic avatar of the inverse of a tame character
  (`New.Data.TameChar.invAvatar`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.IsAuxiliary S I`: The places of `I` have prime norm, neither they nor their conjugates lie in
  the set `S` of places, and their conjugates lie outside `I`.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair`: A character `p.character` of U(1) of weight `-p.negWeight` with tame part
  `p.tamePart`, and an integer `p.z` with `1 ≤ z ≤ c` at every infinite place.
* `New.Data.TameChar`: A character of U(1) of weight 0, with modulus a finite set `Q` of places and
  tame part `ψ` supported on `Q`; `New.Data.Twist` is the type of those that are twists of `D`.
* `New.Data.IsChosen`: The places dividing a fixed element `D.piM` of `E`; they carry the
  tame part of a pair.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.ratio`: The absolute value of `L(z, (ν ϑ)⁻¹) / L(z, ν⁻¹)`, without the
  Euler factors at the chosen places, in the numerator also at the modulus of `ϑ`, and their
  conjugates.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.IsRamified`: The tame part of the pair is nontrivial exactly at the chosen
  places.
modules.literature:
Known result: Integral group-ring elements interpolating twisted Hecke L-values, with norm
relations. The form proved here concerns tame anticyclotomic twists of a fixed modulus, and the
elements are integral at every prime away from it at once. At integers from 2 on, the element is the
squared norm of a theta lift from U(1); at 1 it is a theta period on U(2) times its conjugate and
gives the squared value. Adding a place multiplies the element by Euler factors. Source: N. Katz,
p-adic L-functions for CM fields, Invent. Math. 49 (1978); construction as theta elements:
Bertolini, Darmon, Invent. Math. 126 (1996), adelic form Chida, Hsieh, J. reine angew. Math. 741
(2018); Euler factor: Tamagawa, Ann. of Math. 77 (1963).

modules.title: The Stickelberger systems of the L-values
modules.group: Anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups
modules.note:
The integral measure of a ramified pair is mapped to the group rings of the class groups `Cl_Q`. Its
Euler factors give the norm relation, and its values at twists give the ratios of `L`-values. In
this file `ϑ` is the character of the system, `τ` a tame character and `ξ` a twist.

* `New.Data.CriticalPair.stickelbergerChar`: the character `ϑ` of the system.
* `New.Selmer.exists_stickelbergerSystem_β_le_and_norm_eq`: the system of a ramified pair and a
  sign.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Selmer.StickelbergerSystem`: elements `Θ_Q` of the group rings of the class groups `Cl_Q`
  with a norm relation. Its number `β` is `v(1(Θ_∅)) + ∑_e 2 v(ϑ(g) - 1)`, over the exponents `e`,
  where `g` is the Galois element of the system and `v` is `ellVal`, the `ℓ`-adic valuation
  truncated below at `0`.
* `badPlaces D ℓ`: for the data `D` (a number field `E` and primes `p₀`, `p₁`, `N`), the finite
  set of places of `E` dividing `ℓ p₀ p₁ N`. A modulus is auxiliary if its places have prime norm
  and it is disjoint from this set, from the conjugate of this set and from its own conjugate.

  a sign δ. Both L-functions omit the Euler factors at the chosen places and their conjugates; the
  numerator also omits those at the places of the modulus of τ and their conjugates.
* `New.IsFromU1`: a Galois character `ψ` is a character for `Q` if `ψ(Art x) = η(x / x̄)` for an

* `New.Data.CriticalPair.IsTwistMeasure`: values, one for each tame character, that are an integral
  measure, take Euler factors when a place is added and give powers of the ratio at twists.

modules.title: The twisting theorem
modules.group: Anticyclotomic twists with small Selmer groups
modules.note:
The general twisting theorem is applied to the Selmer data of finitely many representations of
main-summand type and to the Stickelberger systems of the ramified pairs, and the Galois character
it gives is read as the `ℓ`-adic avatar of a tame character.

* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum.TwistedLengthLe.hasDivisibleSelmerLengthLe`: a bound for the twisted
  Selmer group of a datum bounds the crystalline Selmer group of the twisted representation.
* `New.Selmer.exists_mFoldTwist_hasDivisibleSelmerLengthLe`: one tame character whose first `D.m`
  powers have small ramification, short Selmer groups on the main summands, and ratios of `L`-values
  of small valuation.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Selmer.HasDivisibleSelmerLengthLe`: a bound for the length of the Selmer group of a twisted
  representation with coefficients in `Frac(O) / O`.
* `New.Selmer.IsMainSummandLike`: the hypotheses on an `ℓ`-adic representation of the Galois group
  of `D.E` under which its Selmer groups are estimated.
* `New.Selmer.SelmerDatum`: a lattice `T` with Galois action, local conditions and an inertial
  element that acts by a scalar.
* `New.Selmer.twistError`: the number `e'_ℓ = (4 f + 3) r v(D.chosenGroupOrder) + 2 ^ (-ℓ)`.
* `New.Data.MFoldTwist`: a tame character whose tame part has non-trivial `n`-th power at every
  place of its modulus `Q`, for `1 ≤ n ≤ D.m`.
* `New.Data.CriticalPair.ratio`: the ratio `|L(z, (νϑ^s)⁻¹)| / |L(z, ν⁻¹)|` for a sign `s`, without
  the Euler factors at the chosen places, the modulus and their conjugates.
modules.literature:
For finitely many main summands of Galois representations of lifts, one finite-order anticyclotomic
twist ramified at new primes makes, for each of its first m powers, all Selmer groups short and the
ratios of twisted to untwisted Hecke values barely divisible by ℓ. This limits congruences. Twists
of ℓ-power order at new primes that kill a Selmer group or keep L-values barely divisible are known
in the literature. Related work: Mazur–Rubin, Diophantine stability, 2018; Kriz–Nordentoft,
Horizontal p-adic L-functions, 2023; Hida, Non-vanishing modulo p of Hecke L-values, 2004.

modules.title: Local loss above ℓ: main summand weights, b-places, crystalline relations and crystalline colength
modules.note:
This file provides the data for the bound on the loss of a lift at the places of `E` above `ℓ`
(`New.Selmer.eventually_exists_inClass_sum_dualDefect_le`). It defines the conditions on the weights
of a main summand and the unit of that bound, and studies the signs of the embeddings in a Galois
orbit that define b-places. Fix `ι : ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_ℓ` through `New.PadicIso`. For `e : E → ℚ̄_ℓ` and `g` in
`New.Gp ℓ`,
`New.Selmer.complexEmbeddingOf e g = ι⁻¹ ∘ g⁻¹ ∘ e`. `New.Selmer.cmSign σ` is `1` if `σ` belongs to
the CM type and `-1` if not.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Selmer.crystallineLoss`, `New.Selmer.defectBound`: the crystalline loss, and the unit of the
  bound on the total loss of a lift.
* `New.Selmer.ribetCocycles.exists_graph_subrepresentation`: for an element `a` of a noetherian ring
  `O` and finitely many matrix representations `u x` of a group, a cocycle with values in `(O/aO)^d`
  that obeys every linear relation among the families `(u x g - 1)_x` comes from an equivariant map
  on a subrepresentation, given by its graph. Its domain contains the families `(u x g - 1)_x` and
  all multiples of a power of `a` (Artin–Rees).
* `New.Selmer.SummandCoordIndex`, `New.Selmer.summandRep`: the summands of a lift, namely the main
  summand and `t` powers of the inverse cyclotomic character (`New.Selmer.tateTwist`).
* `New.Selmer.crysCocyclesAt`, `New.Selmer.crysRelations`: the crystalline cocycles at `v`, and the
  union over the places `v` above `ℓ` of the linear relations that hold on them, read as relations
  on functions on the global Galois group.
* `New.Selmer.crystallineColength`: the length by which cocycles in `New.Selmer.ribetCocycles`, with
  values in `(O/ℓ^M O)^n`, can miss these relations.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Parameters`: The fixed parameters: a multiple `q₀` of `18480 = 16 · 3 · 5 · 7 · 11` and a
  prime `d` with `d ≡ q₀/2 - 1 mod q₀`. For these, `P.E s = K(ζ)`, where `K = ℚ(√-d)` and `P.ζ s` is
  a root of unity of order `P.q₁ s = 3^c 2^s q₀`, `c = ⌊log₃ s⌋ + 5`. The group `P.Φ s` of infinite
  places of `P.E s` is identified with `(ℤ/q₁)ˣ`, and `P.placeClass` reduces it modulo a divisor of
  `q₁`.
* `New.Data`: The admissible data `D`. Among them are the ranks `m`, `r`, `k = r + 1 - m`, the
  length `t = 5r`, the weight `natB` and the set `D.bPlaces` of b-places of `D.E = P.E D.towerExp`,
  which lies in the cyclotomic field of order `D.cyclotomicConductor = q₁ d`.
* `New.Gp`: The absolute Galois group G_p = Gal(Q̄_p over Q_p).
* `New.Period.crysCocycles`: Z_f(T), the module of maps c: Γ → T such that some y in B⊗T, B = B_max,
  has 1⊗c(g) = gy − y for all g.
* `New.CoeffRing`: Rings of integers of finite Galois extensions of `ℚ_ℓ` inside `ℚ̄_ℓ`.

modules.title: Crystalline cocycles and the defect of a crystalline lattice at a place above ℓ
modules.note:
This file gives local estimates at a place above ℓ for the module `New.Period.crysCocycles` of
crystalline cocycles of a Galois lattice `L` over a coefficient ring `O`. Throughout, the instance
`OverGp Γ ℓ` gives a homomorphism j from `Γ` to G_ℓ = Gal(ℚ̄_ℓ / ℚ_ℓ) with open image.
`New.CoeffRing.normLength` normalises lengths so that `O / ℓ` has length `1`. For a crystalline
lattice, the defect `New.Lift.dualDefect` for a class of lattices is the length of the cocycles
modulo those in the annihilator `New.Lift.cupOrthogonal` of the lattices in the class. This file
computes the rank of the crystalline cocycles and bounds the normalised defect of a lattice whose
jumps lie in windows, under the size conditions `New.Selmer.CrystallineSizes`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Selmer.finrank_crysCocycles_eq_add_neg_jumps`: the rank is `rank L` plus the number of
  negative Hodge–Tate jumps at the embeddings that belong to the place.
* `New.Selmer.normLength_dualDefect_le_of_hasCupExponent`: if a power ℓ^k carries the cocycles into
  the annihilator of a class of lattices, as `New.Lift.HasCupExponent` says, then the defect is
  bounded in terms of k.
* `New.Selmer.normLength_dualDefect_le_of_crystallineSizes`: the defect is bounded in terms of the
  crystalline loss `New.Selmer.crystallineLoss`, uniformly in `ℓ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Lift.GalLattice`: A finite free O-module with a compatible ℤ_ℓ-module structure, together
  with an O-linear representation of the group Γ on it.
* `New.Period.IsPotentiallyCrystalline`: for a representation on T and the crystalline period ring
  B, the elements of B⊗T fixed by all g with j(g) near 1 span B⊗T over B.
* `New.Period.crysCocycles`: Z_f(T), the module, over the coefficient ring, of maps c: Γ → T such
  that some y in B⊗T has 1⊗c(g) = gy − y for all g.
* `New.Period.jump`: The multiplicity of the Hodge–Tate jump u at γ: the dimension over ℚ̄_ℓ (zero
  if infinite) of the space `New.Period.hodgeTateMaps`.

modules.title: The defect of the dual of a summand at a place above ℓ
modules.note:
This file bounds, at a place above ℓ, the normalised defect of the Tate dual of a summand whose
class is adapted to the summands of the data `D`. Here `New.Selmer.IsCompletionGroup` identifies Γ
with the Galois group of a completion of E, and `complexEmbeddingOf e g` is the complex embedding of
E read by g in G_ℓ. This file checks that the data satisfy the size conditions of the crystalline
bound, treats the tame case at the primes `D.levelPrime n`, and compares both bounds with the local
loss `New.Selmer.defectBound`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Selmer.IsSummandClass`: The lattices `L i` are the summands at a place above `ℓ`, and `F`,
  `K`, `U` are the data of a class `New.Lift.InClass F K U` adapted to them. The summand `L none` is
  the main summand, of rank `r` and with jumps `J g` at `coefficientEmbedding O g`; the summand
  `L (some c)` has the single jump `c < t`.
* `New.Selmer.summand_defect_le_at_place`: let `D` be the data, take the coefficient ring `O`
  sufficiently large, and consider summands consisting of one lattice of rank r, the main summand,
  and further lattices with a single jump each. If a summand lies in a tame or crystalline class
  adapted to the summands, then the defect of its dual is at most [G_ℓ :
  j(Γ)] · rank · `New.Selmer.defectBound` / x, where x = 1 for the main summand and x = D.t
  otherwise.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Lift.GalLattice`: A finite free O-module with a compatible ℤ_ℓ-module structure, together
  with an O-linear representation of the group Γ on it.
* `New.Period.IsPotentiallyCrystalline`: for a representation on T and the crystalline period ring
  B, the elements of B⊗T fixed by all g with j(g) near 1 span B⊗T over B.
* `New.Period.jump`: The multiplicity of the Hodge–Tate jump u at γ: the dimension over ℚ̄_ℓ (zero
  if infinite) of the space `New.Period.hodgeTateMaps`.
* `New.Data.t`: The natural number t = 5r, where r is the rank in the data.
* `New.Selmer.CrystallineSizes`: the size conditions of the crystalline bound on its eight
  parameters.
modules.literature:
See `New.Congruences.FirstOrder.RibetElement` for related work. See `Lib.PadicHodge.BlochKato` for
sources.

modules.title: A bound for non-crystalline cocycles modulo `ℓ ^ m` by the Tate dual lattice
modules.note:
This file proves a local estimate at a place above `ℓ`, by Tate duality. The group `Γ` maps to the
absolute Galois group of `ℚ_ℓ` (`OverGp Γ ℓ`), `R` is the integer ring of a finite extension of
`ℚ_ℓ` (`PadicIntegerRing R ℓ`), and `L = R ^ d` is the lattice of a matrix representation of `Γ`
(`matrixLattice`). `QuotSpan a` is the ring `R / a`.

* `New.Selmer.ComesFromClass`: a map with values modulo `ℓ ^ m` is the image of a crystalline
  cocycle of a lattice of a given class.
* `New.Selmer.relLength_le_of_comesFromClass`: if the map of `Γ` to the Galois group is an open
  embedding and `L` lies in the class, a module of maps that come from the class, modulo the
  reductions of the crystalline cocycles of `L`, is at most as long as the crystalline cocycles of
  the Tate dual of `L` modulo those orthogonal to the class.
* `New.Selmer.comesFromClass_of_mem_ribetCocycles`: let `η : Γ →* G`, and let the lattices of all
  `u x ∘ η` lie in the class. Then the restriction along `η` of a cocycle in `ribetCocycles u ρ`
  comes from the class.
* `New.Selmer.relLength_ribetCocycles_le`: if the map of `Γ` to the Galois group is an open
  embedding and the lattices of `ρ ∘ η` and of all `u x ∘ η` lie in the class, the same bound holds
  for `ribetCocycles u ρ` modulo the cocycles whose restriction along `η` obeys the linear
  relations that hold on the crystalline cocycles of the lattice `L` of `ρ ∘ η`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Lift.InClass F K U`: the class of `Γ`-lattices `Y` over `R` (`GalLattice R Γ`) with three
  properties: the periods of `Y` that are fixed by almost all elements of `Γ` near `1` and along the
  filter `F` on `Γ` span; at each algebra map `ι : R → ℂ_ℓ` the Hodge–Tate jumps of `Y` lie in the
  finite set `U ι`; and on the periods of `Y` the polynomial `Q` over `R`, evaluated at the action
  of an element `s` of `Γ`, is zero whenever `s` is in inertia and `K s Q` holds. Such lattices
  are potentially crystalline.
* `New.Period.crysCocycles`: the module `Z_f(T)` of maps `c : Γ → T` that become coboundaries in
  `Bmax ⊗ T`.
* `New.Lift.cupOrthogonal 𝒬 L`: the maps `c : Γ → L` whose cup product with every crystalline
  cocycle of every `Y` in `𝒬` is a coboundary, for every `k` and every pairing `Y × L → ℤ/ℓᵏ(1)`
  given by a `New.Lift.Pairing`.
* `New.Selmer.ribetCocycles u ρ a`: the cocycles for `ρ` with values modulo `a` that obey the
  linear relations among the families `(u x g - 1)_x`.

The estimate bounds the non-crystalline defect above `ℓ` of the cocycles used in
`New.Congruences.FirstOrder.RibetElement`.

modules.title: Tame classes from roots of unity and lattices read at a place above ℓ
modules.note:
This file passes local properties of an ℓ-adic representation R of the Galois group of E to lattices
over a coefficient ring O. Classes of polynomials defined by roots of unity are shown to be tame.
Conjugate self-dual representations of given level are shown to be trivial on inertia away from ℓ, M
and their level, where M = p₀p₁ is the product of the primes p₀, p₁ of the data.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Selmer.isTameType_of_roots`: a class of polynomials containing those that vanish on a given
  multiset of at most N roots of unity of orders dividing ℓ^a - 1, 1 ≤ a ≤ r, is
  `New.Lift.IsTameType`.
* `New.Selmer.localLattice`: a lattice restricted to the decomposition group at a place above ℓ.
* `New.Selmer.IsConjSelfDualOfLevel.hasJumps_localLattice`: a lattice in a conjugate self-dual
  representation of given level has the jumps of the representation at a place above ℓ.
* `New.Selmer.IsConjSelfDualOfLevel.inClass_localLattice`: a lattice in a conjugate self-dual
  representation of given level inherits admissibility at a place above ℓ and, if the place divides
  M, the polynomials that kill inertia.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Data.E`: The field E = K(ζ), ζ a primitive root of unity of order q₁ = 3^c 2^s q₀, for the
  exponent s of the data.
* `New.Selmer.AbsGal`: The absolute Galois group of the field E of the data D: automorphisms of an
  algebraic closure of E fixing E.
* `New.CoeffRing`: Rings of integers of finite Galois extensions of `ℚ_ℓ` inside `ℚ̄_ℓ`.
* `New.Selmer.IsConjSelfDualOfLevel`: R is conjugate self-dual, and at every place outside the level
  S or above ℓ M it is of finite type, has the prescribed jumps, and is good away from M.
* `New.Lift.InClass`: a lattice over O at a place above ℓ is admissible along the supremum of a
  given filter and the filter near 1, has its jumps in given sets, and inertia elements are killed
  on its periods by given polynomials.

modules.title: Lattices with prescribed orders, depth steps and the depth lemma
modules.group: Lifting crystalline extension classes in large weight
modules.note:
This file studies lattices with prescribed orders in W(C^♭) ⊗ L, for a lattice datum L over a
Kummer chart k with ring S = Λ⟦z⟧ ⊆ A_inf, coordinate z, p_a = φ^a(E), δ = zτ and Galois group Γ'.
Here τ = `tau` is the element [ε^{1/p}] − 1 of A_inf, `valueAt a μ` is μ ∘ φ^{−a} with values in
B_dR, and `hodgeFil n` is tⁿB_dR^+. `L.withOrders i c` consists of the x in the A_inf-span
`L.kisinLocAinf` at the letter i with `valueAt a μ x ∈ hodgeFil (c a u)` for all a, all u in
`L.jumpSet (i.stepBack a)` and all forms μ of type u at the letter `i.stepBack a`; such x are said
to have orders c at i. An element x of the Kisin module `L.kisinLoc` (all φ^a E inverted) has
depth n at p_a for a form μ if `valueAt a μ x` is a constant modulo `hodgeFil n`. Such an x at the
letter i has depth o a u at p_a for all a, all u in `L.jumpSet (i.stepBack a)` and all forms of
type u at `i.stepBack a` if and only if gx − x has orders o at i for every g in Γ'
(`New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.mem_invariantsMod_withOrders_iff`). The depth lemma gives an
operator p^c + υ ∑ (t_l − 1)/δ, with t_l in Γ', that sends elements of depth n to elements whose
value is a constant modulo `hodgeFil (n + 1)`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.withOrders`: the elements with orders at least c(a, u) at p_a
  on the jumps u.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.valueAt_mem_of_hodgeFil_le`: the gap rule, bounds for forms
  whose type need not be a jump.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.invariantsMod`: the x with gx − x in Q for all g in Γ'.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.mem_withOrders_improvedOrders`: an element with orders lo
  that is invariant modulo the elements with orders hi has the orders
  `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.improvedOrders lo hi`.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.exists_valueAt_sub_mem_hodgeFil_succ`: the depth lemma, with c =
  `k.cost a n`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.galMonoid`: the group Γ' as a submonoid of `FrobGroup Γ` = ℤ × Γ, whose
  first factor is generated by the Frobenius `φ`.
* `New.Lift.thetaPhiInv`: the ring map θ ∘ φ^{−a} from A_inf to O_C, with kernel generated by p_a.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.kisinLocAinf`, `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.kisinLoc`: the
  A_inf-module A_inf·𝒩 and the S-module 𝒩 in `L.Ambient` = W(C^♭) ⊗ L, where 𝒩 is the Kisin module
  with all p_a inverted (`New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.span_kisinLoc` shows that the first,
  defined as a saturation, is the span of the second).
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.formsOfType`: the A_inf-linear maps `L.Ambient → B_dR` that are
  Γ'-equivariant on 1 ⊗ L and send its projection to the letter i into t^{−u}B_dR^+.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.valueField`: the subfield `𝒦_a` of `B_dR` generated over
  `localFieldOf k.subgroup` by the images of `S_B = k.bicommutant ⊆ B⁺` and of `φ^{-a} S`.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.Letter`: the units of the field with p^f elements. The letter `i.stepBack a`
  is the one whose p^a-th power is i, `L.letterPart i` is the part of `L.Ambient` on which the root
  of unity ζ of the coefficient ring acts as the Teichmüller lift of i, and `L.jumpSet i` is a
  finite set of integers, called the jumps at i, that contains the Hodge–Tate jumps of L above i.
modules.literature:
See `New.Congruences.Lifting.SafeMoves` for related work. See
`Lib.PadicHodge.Kisin.PeriodMatrixFrame` for sources.

modules.title: Exponents of lattice elements in a Hodge basis and the length of one step on a line
modules.group: Lifting crystalline extension classes in large weight
modules.note:
Let `L` be a crystalline lattice over a Kummer chart `k` with prime `p` and residue degree
`f = k.f`. A letter is a unit of the field with `p ^ f` elements; it singles out some of the
embeddings of the coefficients into `ℂ_p`, and `i.stepBack a` is the letter `j` with `j^(p^a) = i`.
Take an element `x` of `L.kisinLocAinf` lying in the letter `i`. Then `x ∈ L.withOrders i c` says
the following: for every level `a : ℕ` and every form `μ` of a type `u ∈ L.jumpSet j` at the letter
`j = i.stepBack a`, the value `valueAt a μ x = μ (φ^(-a) x)` lies in `t^(c a u) B_dR⁺`. The file
shows how exponents behave under coordinates and Frobenius. It then shows that among sufficiently
many elements with given exponents some primitive `ℤ_[p]`-combination gains a step: it splits into
parts with raised exponents. The line `u` of a system `c` of exponents is the family `a ↦ c a u`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.mem_withOrders_stdOrders_iff`: the standard exponents
  `New.Lift.KummerChart.stdOrders l` cut out, at the letter, the span
  `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.frobKisinAinf l`, the image of `L.kisinAinf` under `φ^l`.
  On the line `u` these exponents are `0` below level `l` and `-u` from level `l` on.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.prod_frobEUnit_zpow_smul_mem_kisinLoc_and_withOrders_iff`:
  for a product `F` of integer powers of the `φ^a(E)`, the module `F` times the `S`-span of the
  image under `φ^l` of the Kisin module `L.kisinModule` is cut out in `L.kisinLoc`, at the letter,
  by the standard exponents raised by those of `F`.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.wittPairing_mem_withOrders`: exponents add under an
  equivariant bilinear map of lattices.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.raiseOrder`, `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.raiseOrdersAt`:
  the system of exponents `o` with the single value `o a u`, or all values at the level `a`, raised
  by one.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.exists_sum_smul_mem_locKisinPart_sup`: let the chart be
  unramified and the jump `u` of multiplicity at most `n` at the letter `b` steps before `l`. Let
  `o b u < o b v` on the lines `v < u` in `L.jumpSet (l.stepBack b)`. Then any `k.f * n + 1`
  elements of `L.kisinLoc` with exponents `o` at the letter `l` have a `ℤ_[p]`-combination with one
  coefficient `1` that is the sum of two elements of `L.kisinLoc`: one with all exponents at level
  `0` raised by one, and one with the exponent at level `b` on the line `u` raised by one.

Notions from other files:
* `JumpLattice O`: a finite free `O`-module `L` with a crystalline action and, for each letter `i`,
  a finite set `L.jumpSet i` that holds its jumps. `L.Ambient` is `W(C^♭) ⊗ L`, and `L.Functional`
  is the type of `A_inf`-linear maps `L.Ambient → B_dR`.
* `L.forms`, `L.formsOfType i u`: the functionals that are `Γ'`-equivariant on `1 ⊗ L`, and those
  among them that send the letter-`i` projection of `1 ⊗ L` into `t^(-u) B_dR⁺`.
* `L.ainfLattice` is the `A_inf`-span of `1 ⊗ L`. `L.kisinAinf` consists of the `x` in
  `A_inf[1/τ] ⊗ L` with `μ (φ^n x) ∈ B_dR⁺` for all forms `μ` and all `n ≥ 1`, and
  `L.kisinLocAinf` is its saturation by the elements `k.frobE a = φ^a(E)`.
* `saturateBy M P`: the elements that some member of the submonoid `M` multiplies into `P`.
modules.literature:
See `New.Congruences.Lifting.SafeMoves` and `New.Congruences.Lifting.CupOrthogonalityBounds` for
related work. For sources see `Lib.PadicHodge.Kisin.PeriodMatrixFrame`.

modules.title: Sides of a pairing, cokernel killers and the pairing lemma for cup products
modules.group: Lifting crystalline extension classes in large weight
modules.note:
A side `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide` consists of a lattice Y, a lattice C (`paramLattice`) and
an O-linear map α (`cocycleMap`) from C to the crystalline cocycles Z_f(Y)
(`New.Period.crysCocycles`). These cocycles define an extension of the trivial lattice on
`S.paramLattice` by Y. All lattices are tensored with W(C^♭), on which ℤ × Γ acts with φ the
Frobenius, and `P` is a pairing of the lattices of two sides modulo p^m. The pairing lemma shows
that, for cocycles that pair safely, safe moves from (φx, φx') to (x, x') make a multiple `p ^ e` of
their cup product, read in ℚ̄_p^×, a coboundary.

On a Kummer chart let z be the coordinate, E a generator of ker θ and N the Kisin module. The ideal
J_l(i) is generated by a modulus r and by the multipliers s ∈ A_inf for which s times each constant
(the letter-i part of 1 ⊗ c, c ∈ C) lifts to the extension inside A_inf·φ^{l*}N. Elements of the
form p^κ E^s and z^a are shown to lie in it.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Lift.Pairing.IsSafe`: a pair is safe if `p ^ e` times its pairing is small, that is, lies in
  the image `New.Lift.smallPart` of W(𝔪^♭).
* `New.Lift.Pairing.IsScaledCupCoboundary`: the cup product of the cocycles `S.cocycleMap c` and
  `p ^ e • S'.cocycleMap c'` is a coboundary.
* `New.Lift.Pairing.IsScaledCupCoboundary.of_isSafePath`: the pairing lemma, which derives this from
  a path of safe moves.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.liftIdeal`, `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.KillsCokernel`:
  the ideal J_l(i); p^κ E^s lies in J_0(i) with r = 0.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.exists_z_pow_mem_liftIdeal`: z^a ∈ J_0(i) with r = p^{κ+1} and
  (p − 1)a ≤ e(ω + κ), where the jumps are ≤ ω and e is the ramification index.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.killsCokernel_of_isUnramified`: on an unramified chart with p ≥
  5, p^s E^t ∈ J_0(i), r = 0, when the jumps are ≤ (p − 3)(s + t).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.Coeffs`: a ring of coefficients O, a finite free Z_p-algebra with an element
  ζ such that ζ^{p^f−1} = 1; ζ cuts out the letters.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice`: a finite free O-module with an action of Γ, crystalline over
  the subgroup Γ' of the chart, with a finite set `jumpSet i` of integers holding its jumps at each
  letter i. Its `Ambient` is its tensor product with W(C^♭).
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.Letter`: the letters of a Kummer chart: the multiplicative group of the
  field with p^f elements inside C^♭, where f is the number `k.f` of the chart.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.stdOrders`: the exponents (a, u) ↦ 0 for a < l and −u for a ≥ l, prescribed
  at φ^a E for the jump u.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.stdOrdersPart`: the elements of 𝒩, the Kisin module with all φ^a
  E inverted, that lie at the letter i and have the standard exponents of level l.

modules.title: Jump windows, the gap condition and points of the sides of a Kummer chart
modules.group: Lifting crystalline extension classes in large weight
modules.note:
This file defines windows of integers in which the jumps of lattices in a Kummer chart are required
to lie. It defines the gap condition that `p` divides no non-zero integer near 0, `b` or `-b`, and
it bounds sums of `p`-adic valuations over two windows. For one side it defines deep elements of

points by Frobenius. It also defines pairings of sides and the standard points, stops and rule
bound used by the walk.

  orders and a depth.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.pointsOver_nonempty_of_killsCokernel`,
  `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.pointsOver_nonempty_of_costs`: points exist, and their depth can
  be raised at a cost in powers of `p`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.Letter`: the letters of a Kummer chart, that is, the multiplicative group of
  the field with p^f elements in O^♭.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide`: lattices Y and C with an O-linear map `cocycleMap` from C to

* `New.Lift.Pairing`: a pairing of Y and L modulo p^m, that is, an O-linear ψ: Y ⊗ L → O(1) with

modules.title: Tame Kummer charts and the power of p that kills cokernels of Kisin modules
modules.group: Lifting crystalline extension classes in large weight
modules.note:
A tame chart `New.Lift.TameChart` is a Kummer chart `New.Lift.KummerChart`, with coordinate `z` and
exponent `e`, together with an element `s` of inertia. The power `s ^ k` multiplies `z` by `ξ ^ k`,
for some `ξ` in Λ = W(𝔽_{p^f}) that is a primitive e-th root of unity modulo `p`. The degree of a
polynomial that kills the operator induced by `s` bounds the power of `p` that kills the cokernel of
the map of Kisin modules attached to an extension of a trivial lattice `C` by a lattice `Y`. The
file also shows that, if Γ maps onto G_p, tame charts exist for each ramification index e dividing
p^f − 1, when p does not divide f.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Lift.TameChart.exists_z_smul_eq_sum_tameGen`: if a polynomial `q` over `ℤ_p` kills the
  operator β induced by `s`, then `q(s)` maps the Kisin module into `z` times
  `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.kisinAinf`.
* `New.Lift.TameChart.killsCokernel_of_isKilledBy`: if `Y` is potentially crystalline and a monic
  `q` kills β on `Y`, then `p ^ κ` kills the cokernel, that is, multiplies the constants of `C` into
  the image, as soon as `m (deg q + 1) ≤ κ`, `e ≤ p ^ m` and `p` is large against `κ` and the jumps.
* `New.Lift.exists_tameChart`: tame charts exist.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Lift.WittFq`: The ring Λ = W(𝔽_{p^f}) of constants, 𝔽_{p^f} taken inside the tilt O^♭.
* `New.Period.linearFrob`: For s in inertia, `linearFrob ρ s 0` is the B-linear operator β on B ⊗ T
  (B = `Bmax`) that acts as s on the vectors fixed by the elements of Γ near 1.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.Letter`: A letter is a unit i of 𝔽_{p^f}. The coefficient ring O carries an
  element ζ with ζ^{p^f−1} = 1, and the letter-i part of W(C^♭) ⊗ L is where ζ acts as [i].

modules.title: The long gap lemma for a side of a Kummer chart, by expansion in powers of E
modules.group: Lifting crystalline extension classes in large weight
modules.note:
This file concerns a side `S` over a Kummer chart, whose distinguished element is written `E`. It
defines the constants modulo `E ^ A` and expands vectors in powers of `E` with such constants as
coefficients. It then proves the long gap lemma. The proof multiplies a lift by `f(E)`, with `f`
monic of degree `N`, and takes the `N`-th Taylor coefficient of `p ^ (4 δ)` times the product.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.constantsModE`: the constants modulo E^A, with exponents
  `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.shiftedStdOrders`.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.pointsOver_nonempty_of_long_gap`: the long gap lemma. On an
  unramified Kummer chart, if `E ^ s` kills the cokernel at `i` and `p ^ κ` kills it at
  `i.stepBack l`, the jumps at `i` and the `l - 1` letters before it are at most `g`, `3 ≤ p ^ l`,
  `A ≤ p ^ l * δ`, and there is the long gap `s + g * ∑ a < l, p ^ a < A`, then a constant of the
  trivial lattice lifts, up to a power of p, to a point of the extension at `i` with a large order
  at E at the very negative jumps.

* `New.Lift.KummerChart`: a ring `k.S` = Λ⟦z⟧ in A_inf, where Λ = `WittFq k.f` = W(𝔽_{p^f}), and a
  subgroup Γ' of Γ of index prime to p that fixes Λ. It is unramified (`IsUnramified`) if E = z + p
  and the ramification index `k.e` is 1. The number `k.differentBound` is 0 if `k.e = 1` and
  v_p(e) + 1 otherwise.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.Coeffs`: a ring of coefficients O, a finite free Z_p-algebra with an element
  ζ such that ζ^{p^f−1} = 1; ζ cuts out the letters.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.Letter`: the letters of a Kummer chart, that is, the multiplicative group of
  the field with p^f elements in the tilt of the ring of integers of C_p; `i.stepBack a` is the
  letter `a` Frobenius steps back.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.withOrders`: for a lattice `L` with a finite set of jumps at
  each letter, the vectors of W(C^♭)⊗L at a letter whose value at φ^a E on the forms of jump u is
  divisible by t^{c(a,u)}; they are said to have the orders `c`.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide`, `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.KillsCokernel`: one side of
  a pairing: lattices Y and C (`paramLattice`), an O-linear map `cocycleMap` from C to the
  crystalline cocycles Z_f(Y), and for each letter a finite set of integers that contains 0, the
  jumps. The extension `extensionLattice` of C by Y maps by `projTrivial` to `trivialLattice`, the

modules.title: Safe moves and the walk for pairings of sides of a Kummer chart
modules.group: Lifting crystalline extension classes in large weight
modules.note:
This file concerns two sides of a Kummer chart with a pairing `P` modulo `p ^ m`. From numerical
conditions on orders it derives safe moves. It then walks along Frobenius orbits to derive the
condition `New.Lift.Pairing.IsScaledCupCoboundary`. It shows that at plain cuts deep enough standard
points are stops, and it sorts jumps in the windows into sides that are down or up.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.SidePairing.isSafe_of_orders`: for `w`, `y` over `0`, the
  pairs `(z τ w, y)` and `(w, z τ y)` are safe (`New.Lift.Pairing.IsSafe`) if the orders of `w`, `y`
  and a point of the Tate dual side `New.Lift.Pairing.tateDualSide` add up to a positive number.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.SidePairing.isSafeMoveFst_of_killsCokernel`,
  `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.SidePairing.isSafeMoveSnd_of_killsCokernel`: the rule. A move is
  safe if a power of `p` times a power of `E` kills the cokernel of the Tate dual side and the
  orders of the move and the depth of the point at rest add up to at least `ruleBound`.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.SidePairing.isScaledCupCoboundary_of_stops`: the walk. Standard
  points at the cuts are carried along by Frobenius; at each cut one side moves to a stop, rests
  there while the other side moves, and goes on to its own point.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.SidePairing.exists_mem_stopPoints_isSafeMoveSnd`,
  `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.SidePairing.exists_mem_stopPoints_isSafeMoveFst`: at a plain
  cut, where one side is down and the other is up, a deep enough standard point is a stop.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide`: lattices Y and C with an O-linear map `cocycleMap` from C to
  the crystalline cocycles of Y, and for each letter a finite set of jumps that contains 0.
* `New.Lift.Pairing`: a pairing of Y and L modulo p^m, that is, an O-linear ψ: Y ⊗ L → O(1) with
  gψ − ψ = p^m c(g) for a crystalline cocycle c, and a Z_p-linear f: O → Z_p.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.pointsOver`: points of the extension over `p ^ e c`, with
  exponents and a depth.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.stopPoints`: the points over `p ^ e c` with the exponents
  `stopOrders η l` of a stop, where one side rests while the other side moves.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.ruleBound`: the least sum of the orders of a move and the depth
  of the point at rest that the rule for `l` allows.
modules.literature:
Explicit powers of p and of the Eisenstein polynomial kill cokernels of Kisin modules on crystalline
extensions, and Galois operators buy divisibility at known cost. A walk along Frobenius orbits makes
cup products of crystalline classes vanish up to powers of p, and these tools bound the loss above p
in the Selmer bound. Zero cokernel for weights of one sign, cup products via Ext and torsion bounds
by Sen operators are known in the literature. Related work: Čoupek–Gazaki–Marmora, Exactness
property of Breuil–Kisin functors and Bloch–Kato Selmer groups, 2026; Gao–Liu, Integral Sen theory
and integral Hodge filtration, 2024; Chang–Diamond, Extensions of rank one (φ,Γ)-modules and
crystalline representations, 2011.

The file `New.Congruences.Lifting.CutExponentBounds` applies the walk to two choices of cuts.

modules.title: Exponent bounds by cuts for paired sides of a Kummer chart: sparse thick letters, two sizes
modules.group: Lifting crystalline extension classes in large weight
modules.note:
This file concerns two paired sides `S`, `S'` over a Kummer chart, whose distinguished element is
written `E`. Letters `i : k.Letter` are permuted by Frobenius `k.letterFrob`. The jumps

with opposite far windows, and `V + 4η ≤ W`. A cut a bounded number of letters back from each
letter then gives the bound for the exponent in `New.Lift.Pairing.IsScaledCupCoboundary`; two
choices of cuts treat the cases of two sizes of far windows: one where the thick letters, those
with the larger size, are sparse, and one where they form any pattern.

  plain cut and at a cut with a long gap.

  letter `a` Frobenius steps back.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide`, `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.KillsCokernel`: one side

  crystalline cocycles Z_f(Y), and for each letter a finite set of integers that contains 0, the

* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.pointsOver`: `S.pointsOver c i e o d` is the set of the vectors

modules.literature:
Take crystalline lattices with weights in short windows near 0 and near large weights, in the cases
of no small negative weight, two sizes, or sparse large weights. For these, an explicit power of p,
independent of the rank, makes crystalline classes cup to zero with those of congruent dual
lattices. This bounds the loss at the places above p in the Selmer bound. The case of small weights
and a rank-free factorial torsion bound by Sen operators are known in the literature. Related work:
Gao–Liu, Integral filtered Sen theory and applications, 2024; Iovita–Marmora, Continuity of the
finite Bloch–Kato cohomology, 2015; Y. Min, Congruences of first syntomic cohomology groups, 2026.

modules.title: Deep points and scaled cup coboundaries for a gap below zero or nonpositive jumps
modules.group: Lifting crystalline extension classes in large weight
modules.note:
A side `S` (`New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide`) has sets `S.jumpSet i` that hold the jumps at
each letter `i`. `S.pointsOver c i κ lo o` is the set of points over `p ^ κ c` at the letter `i`,
with orders `lo` and depth `o`. The steps from a depth `o` to a depth `o'` are the integers `y`
with `o l u ≤ y < o' l u`, each taken at its level `l`. The level `0` belongs to the prime `E` of
the chart `k`, and `d = k.differentBound`. This file raises the depth of points when all steps
occur at the level `0`, and bounds the cost of this with `New.Lift.KummerChart.cost`. It deduces
the cup conditions for paired sides in two cases: when no jump lies in `[-a, 0)`, and when the
chart is unramified and all jumps of the second side lie in `[-η, 0]`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.pointsOver_nonempty_of_noMultipleNear`: the depth can be raised
  at a cost of `p ^ ((8 n + 4) d)`. This needs every step to occur at `E` and within distance `n` of
  `0`, `b` or `-b`, and `p` to divide no nonzero integer within `n` of these.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.SidePairing.isScaledCupCoboundary_of_gap`,
  `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.SidePairing.isScaledCupCoboundary_of_jumps_nonpos`: the cup
  conditions when no jump lies in `[-a, 0)`, and when all jumps of `S'` lie in `[-η, 0]`.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.SidePairing.isScaledCupCoboundary_of_killsCokernel`: paired
  sides satisfy the cup conditions with exponent `H` when `3 (κ + (48 (a + η + W) + 4) d) ≤ H`. The
  hypotheses are these. The cokernels are killed. The jumps lie in opposite windows. At every `i`,
  `p` divides no nonzero integer within `6 (a + η + W)` of `0`, `b i` or `-b i`. Either no jump lies
  in `[-a, 0)`, or the chart is unramified and all jumps of `S'` lie in `[-η, 0]`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Lift.KummerChart`: a Kummer chart `k` of the group `Γ` over `G_p`: a ring `Λ⟦z⟧` inside
  `A_inf` with a distinguished element `E` (`E = z + p` if the chart is unramified) and a subgroup
  `Γ'` of `Γ` of index prime to `p`. Its letters are the units of the residue field
  `𝔽_{p ^ k.f}`; a letter singles out embeddings of the coefficients, and `i.stepBack l` is the
  letter `l` steps of Frobenius before `i`.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide`: one side of a pairing: lattices `Y` and `paramLattice`, an
  `O`-linear map `cocycleMap` from `paramLattice` to the crystalline cocycles `Z_f(Y)`, and for each
  letter a finite set of integers that contains `0`. `S.extensionLattice` is the extension of the
  trivial lattice `paramLattice` by `Y` given by the cocycles of `S`, with the jump sets of `S`.
* Orders `o l u` prescribe, for every level `l` and jump `u` at `i.stepBack l`, a power of the
  uniformiser of `B_dR⁺` that divides the value of an element on the line `u` at the level `l`. An
  element has depth `o` if its differences with its translates by `Γ'` have orders `o`.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.cost`: the cost `k.cost l n = v_p(n) + d + 3 l` of the step `n` at the level
  `l`, with `v_p(0) = 0`; here `d = 0` if the index `e` of the chart is `1`, and `d = v_p(e) + 1`
  otherwise.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide.KillsCokernel`: `p ^ κ * E ^ a` kills the cokernel at the letter
  `i`: it multiplies the letter-`i` part of `A_inf ⊗ C` into the image of the extension's module of
  standard exponents of level `0`.
* `New.Lift.FitsWindows`: `FitsWindows η ε b W U` says that `U` lies in the union of the low window
  `[-η, η]` and the far window `ε • [b, b + W]`.
* `New.Lift.Pairing.IsScaledCupCoboundary`: the cup conditions with exponent `H` for `c` and `c'`:
  the cup product of the cocycles `S.cocycleMap c` and `p ^ H • S'.cocycleMap c'` is a continuous
  coboundary.

modules.title: Few low jumps: length lost to depth and a submodule cupping to zero

modules.title: From sides to lattices: few low jumps, b-letters and tame types
modules.group: Lifting crystalline extension classes in large weight
modules.note:
Bounds for the power of p that makes the crystalline cocycles `New.Period.crysCocycles` of a lattice
L orthogonal (`New.Lift.cupOrthogonal`, under cup product) to a class of lattices
`New.Lift.InClass`. The class is given by admissibility, jump sets and polynomials that kill
inertia. The estimates themselves are proved for sides (`New.Lift.KummerChart.PairingSide`) over a
Kummer chart `New.Lift.KummerChart`. This file passes to lattices.

* `New.Lift.KummerChart.universalSide`,
  `New.Lift.KummerChart.pow_smul_mem_cupOrthogonal_of_isScaledCupCoboundary`: the side of all
  crystalline cocycles of L, and orthogonality from the relation
  `New.Lift.Pairing.IsScaledCupCoboundary` for all paired sides.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.dualDefect_eq_zero_and_dualDefect_le`: the defect `New.Lift.dualDefect` is 0
  if there is no small negative jump, and is bounded if there are few low jumps.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.hasCupExponent_any_pattern`,
  `New.Lift.KummerChart.hasCupExponent_sparse_thick`: explicit exponents (`New.Lift.HasCupExponent`)
  for any pattern of b-letters and for sparse b-letters.
* `New.Lift.hasCupExponent_of_isTameType`: an explicit exponent for tame inertial types
  (`New.Lift.IsTameType`).

Jumps lie in windows `New.Lift.FitsWindows` = [−η, η] ∪ ε[b, b + W]. An embedding g of O lies
over the letter i if g ζ = θ(ω(i)), where ζ is a root of unity in O and ω(i) is the Teichmüller lift
of i. The jump set `New.Lift.KummerChart.letterJumps` at i collects 0 and the sets U g for the g
over i.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.LetterRoot`: The elements ζ of O with ζ^q = 1, where q = p^f − 1 is the
  number of letters of the chart.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.Letter`: The letters of a Kummer chart: the multiplicative group of the
  field with p^f elements in the tilt of the ring of integers of C_p.
* `New.Period.theta`: Fontaine's ring homomorphism θ from A_inf to the ring of integers of C_p,
  sending the Teichmüller lift [x] to x^♯.
modules.literature:
Over Q_p, take potentially crystalline lattices of tame inertial type with weights in two windows
small against p. For these, a power of p makes Bloch–Kato classes cup to zero with those of
congruent dual lattices. The exponent, used in the Selmer bound, depends on the sizes of the types
and windows but not on the ramification index. Small ramification, the tame potentially
Barsotti–Tate case and Kisin modules with descent data for generic tame types are treated in the
literature. Related work: Iovita–Marmora, Continuity of the finite Bloch–Kato cohomology, 2015;
Nekovář, Compatibility of arithmetic and algebraic local constants II, 2018; Le–Le Hung–Levin–Morra,
Local models for Galois deformation rings, 2023.

Work over unramified p-adic fields with p ≥ 5, where p divides no non-zero integer near 0 or the
large weights. There, crystalline classes modulo those cupping to zero with congruent dual lattices
have length O(1 + large weight/p) per low weight plus O(rank × (window width + 1)), times the
residue degree and the length of O/p, and zero length absent small negative weights. This bounds the
loss above p in the Selmer bound. No loss for weights below p−1, exact Breuil–Kisin sequences for
weights of one sign, and torsion located by weights modulo p are known in the literature. Related
work: Iovita–Marmora, Continuity of the finite Bloch–Kato cohomology, 2015; Čoupek–Gazaki–Marmora,
Exactness of Breuil–Kisin functors, 2026; Gao–Liu, Integral filtered Sen theory and applications,
2024.

modules.title: Steep parameters and the setting of Laplace's method
modules.group: Discrete series with a large gap
modules.note:
This file begins the localization near the compact subgroups. It concerns a group `S` that maps to
`U(ε) × U(η)`, for two vectors of signs `ε` and `η`, together with the parameters of two discrete
series. Let `μ` and `μ'` be the diagonal matrices of the weights of their lowest `K`-types. Among
other properties, the function `φ s = tr (μ (g - 1)) - tr (μ' (g' - 1))` of the image `(g, g')` of
`s`, the difference of the two phases, is additive and purely imaginary.
The file defines the phase difference `New.HCParam.phase`, steep parameters, the properties
`New.DiscreteSeries.IsLaplaceDatum` and the integrand `New.HCParam.laplaceIntegrand`. It also
proves the polar decomposition of an invertible matrix.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.DiscreteSeries.IsLaplaceDatum`: the properties of `j : S →* U(ε) × U(η)` and `φ` that
  Laplace's method uses; `New.HCParam.laplaceIntegrand` is the function that is integrated.
* `New.DiscreteSeries.IsSteep`: the parameter `l` for the signs `ε` is steep with respect to `B`
  and the splitting `e : X ⊕ Fin M ≃ n` of the coordinates.

Notions from other files:
* `New.USign ε`: the unitary group `U(ε)` of the diagonal matrix `signMatrix ε` of the signs `ε`.
* `New.HCParam.lowestKType l`: the highest weight of the lowest `K`-type of the parameter `l`.
* `New.HCParam.dsCoeff l`: the matrix coefficient of that `K`-type, as a function of a matrix.

modules.title: Localizing products of discrete series coefficients near the compact subgroups
modules.group: Discrete series with a large gap
modules.note:
This file treats a group `S` with a map `j : S →* U(ε) × U(η)` that satisfies
`New.DiscreteSeries.IsLaplaceDatum`. It proves facts about `New.HCParam.laplaceIntegrand`, the
product of the first discrete series coefficient, the conjugate of the second and `exp (-φ)`. It
shows that a coefficient with a large gap decays away from the maximal compact subgroup. It also
shows that, if `1 ≤ B` and both noncompact parts at `s` are small, the integrand takes the same
value at some `t` for which both components of `j t` are near `1`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.DiscreteSeries.noncompactPart ε g`: the noncompact part `g - blockDiagPart ε g` of a
  matrix `g`.
* A coefficient with a large gap is small where the noncompact part of its argument is large
  (`New.DiscreteSeries.norm_dsCoeff_pow_four_le`).
* If `1 ≤ B` and both noncompact parts at `s` are small, then `laplaceIntegrand` takes the same
  value at some `t` for which both components of `j t` are near `1`
  (`New.DiscreteSeries.IsLaplaceDatum.exists_laplaceIntegrand_eq_and_norm_subOnePair_le`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.USign ε`: the unitary group `U(ε)` of the diagonal matrix `signMatrix ε` of the signs `ε`.
* `New.blockDiagPart ε g`: the compact part of `g`, which keeps the entries `g i j` with
  `ε i = ε j`.
* `New.HCParam.lowestKType l`, `New.HCParam.dsCoeff l`: the highest weight of the lowest `K`-type
  of the parameter `l`, and the matrix coefficient of that `K`-type.
* `New.DiscreteSeries.IsLaplaceDatum`: the properties of `j` and `φ` that Laplace's method uses.
* `New.HCParam.laplaceIntegrand`: the function to which Laplace's method applies.
modules.literature:
This file uses the discrete series coefficient that is known as Flensted-Jensen's function, the
coefficient of the lowest `K`-type of a discrete series
(defined in `Lib.DiscreteSeries.FlenstedJensen.Defs`).

modules.title: One minor of a product of three exponentials, to second order
modules.group: Discrete series with a large gap
modules.note:
For an orthogonal projection `Q` and small matrices `A₁`, `A₂`, `A₃` we expand
`log det (1 + Q (exp A₁ exp A₂ exp A₃ - 1))` to second order. The rest vanishes to order three in
the `Aᵢ` and to order two in their parts that cross `Q`; Schwarz's lemma turns this into the bound
`O(δ ζ²)`, where `δ` bounds the `Aᵢ` and `ζ` bounds the commutators `⁅Q, Aᵢ⁆`. All norms are
Hilbert–Schmidt (Frobenius) norms, and no constant depends on the dimension.

The main result is `exists_det_one_add_proj_mul_eq_exp`. The order three is obtained by direct
estimates of the exponential series and of the integral that defines the logarithm. The rest
`logMinorRemainder` is a principal logarithm, holomorphic in the factor `τ` that scales the crossing
parts, and Schwarz's lemma is applied in `τ`.

Notions from other files:
* `logOneAdd M = ∫ s in 0..1, (1 + s M)⁻¹ M` is the matrix logarithm `log (1 + M)`, used for
  `‖M‖ ≤ 1 / 2`.
* `IsStarProjection Q` says that `Q` is an orthogonal projection: self-adjoint and idempotent.

modules.title: Positions of a smaller unitary group, and the two traces
modules.group: Discrete series with a large gap
modules.note:
A position of `U(η)` in `U(ε)` consists of independent vectors `v₁, …, v_{j₀}` and an isometry `i₀`
into their orthogonal complement. It is stationary for two weights `μ`, `μ'` if `μ` moves `v_j` to
`v_{j + 1}` for `j < j₀` and compresses to `μ'` on the image of `i₀`, and `i₀` is the identity on
the common coordinates `X`. For a matrix `Y` that lowers the flag of the `v_j` together with its
adjoint, and induces `Y'` on the image of `i₀`, we compute `tr Y - tr Y'` and `tr μ Y - tr μ' Y'`.

Notions from other files:
* `signMatrix ε` is the diagonal matrix of the signs `ε i = ±1`, and `USign ε` its unitary group.
* `HCParam ε` consists of the integer vectors on `n`, used as doubled Harish-Chandra parameters
  `l = 2 λ`; `l.lowestKType` is the weight of the lowest `K`-type and `intDiagonal w` the diagonal
  matrix of a weight `w`.
* `l.phase k (Y, Y')` is `tr μ Y - tr μ' Y'` for the weights `μ`, `μ'` of the lowest `K`-types of
  `l` and `k`.

modules.title: The stationary position
modules.group: Discrete series with a large gap
modules.note:
For weights `μ` and `μ'` on opposite sides of `0`, with alternating signs on each side, there is a
position `(v, i₀)` in which `μ` moves each vector `v_j` to `v_{j + 1}` for `j < j₀`, where
`j₀ = d + 1` is the number of vectors, and `i₀` compresses `μ` to `μ'`
(`IsSteep.exists_isStationary`). The weight `μ` is realized as multiplication by `t` on
polynomials, and the form as a sum of residues.

Throughout, `p = nodal univ μ` and `q = nodal univ μ'` are the monic polynomials with the roots
`μ i` and `μ' j`, and `q_j = nodal (univ.erase j) μ'` is `q / (t - μ' j)`. The roots are indexed
from `0`, the vectors `v₁, …, v_{j₀}` from `1`. The vector `polyVec μ μ' F` is written `[F]`, and
`alternatingSignForm x y` is written `⟨x, y⟩`.

Notions from other files:

* `l.lowestKType`: the highest weight of the lowest `K`-type for the doubled Harish-Chandra
  parameter `l = 2 λ : HCParam ε`, a vector of integers; `intDiagonal` turns it into a diagonal
  matrix.
* `IsSteep l B e`: on `X` the signs `ε` are `+1` and that weight is `0`; on `Fin L` the signs
  are `+, -, …` and the weight decreases strictly in `[-3 B, -B]`.
* `IsPosition ε η d v i₀`: the ranks differ by `2 d + 1`, the columns of `v` are independent, their
  products vanish except that the last column has norm `±1`, and `i₀` is an isometry into their
  orthogonal complement.
* `signMatrix ε` is the diagonal matrix of the signs `ε`, and `formAdjoint ε η A` is the adjoint
  `A†` for the hermitian forms with the signs `ε` and `η`.

modules.title: One minor near the identity
modules.group: Discrete series with a large gap
modules.note:
Estimates for one principal minor `det_S`, in terms of the blocks that cross the set `S` of indices,
that is, the entries `(i, j)` with exactly one of `i`, `j` in `S`: its size on a unitary matrix
(`norm_principalMinor_sq_le_exp`), and its form on `kᴴ ĝ k` for `k` unitary and block diagonal and
`ĝ = reducedExp ε o Z` for a small `Z` in the Lie algebra of `U(J)`, with `o` injective and
`o i < o j` whenever `i ∈ S` and `j ∉ S` (`exists_principalMinor_conj_reducedExp_eq_cexp`): up to an
error, `exp (tr P Z + ‖[P, Z]‖² / 4)`, where `P` is the projection to `S` and `‖[P, Z]‖` is the norm
of the two blocks of `Z` that cross `S`. A third estimate for one minor is
`exists_det_one_add_proj_mul_eq_exp` in `New.Appendix.DiscreteSeries.MinorSecondOrder`.

The matrix `ĝ` differs from `exp Z` by unipotent factors. Block diagonal triangular factors multiply
Flensted-Jensen's coefficient by a character of their diagonal if the matrices involved are
accretive (`flenstedJensen_triangular_mul_mul_triangular`), so for small `Z` the coefficient is the
same at `ĝ` and at `exp Z` (`flenstedJensen_reducedExp`).

All norms of matrices are Frobenius norms, and `ε : n → ℤˣ` is a vector of signs. Notation:
* `principalMinor X p`, `coordProj p`: the principal minor `det_S X` and the diagonal projection for
  the set `S` of indices satisfying `p`.
* `blockDiagAlg ε`: the matrices that vanish at `(i, j)` whenever `ε i ≠ ε j`.
* `lowerMask ε o Z`: the matrix that keeps the entries `(i, j)` of `Z` with `o j < o i` and
  `ε i = ε j`.

modules.title: The Gaussian shape of the coefficient
modules.group: Discrete series with a large gap
modules.note:
Near `1` the coefficient `l.dsCoeff g` of a discrete series with a large gap is nearly the phase
`exp (tr μ log g)` times a number in `[0, 1]`, where `μ` is the weight `l.lowestKType`
(`exists_norm_dsCoeff_div_cexp_sub_le`). The coefficient is a mean over `K` of a quotient of
products of minors, and the estimates for one minor are multiplied over the sets `{i | t ≤ w i}` of
a weight `w`. In the comments, `λ^ρ` is `paramAddRho l`, `Q_w` is `gapWeightedNormSq w`, and `ĝ` is
`reducedExp ε l Z`. The Gaussian is `exp (-q)` with `q = Q_{-λ^ρ} (log g) / 4`; note `Q_{-w} = Q_w`.
Except in the first section, the norm of a matrix is the Frobenius norm.

* `USign ε` is the unitary group of the form `diag ε`; `K = maxCompactU ε` is its subgroup of
  unitary matrices, with the Haar measure `haarK ε` of mass one.
* `l : HCParam ε` is a doubled Harish-Chandra parameter `2λ`; `paramAddRho l` is `λ + ρ` and
  `l.lowestKType` is `λ + ρ - 2ρ_c`.
* `weightMinors w g` is the product over `t : ℤ` of the principal minors of `g` on the sets
  `{i | t ≤ w i}`, those with `t ≤ 0` divided by `det g`; `w.kTypeNormSq` is the mean of its
  squared modulus over `K`.
* `l.flenstedJensen g z` is the mean over `k ∈ K` of
  `weightMinors μ (g k) * conj (weightMinors μ k) / weightMinors (-paramAddRho l) (kᴴ z k)`,
  divided by `μ.kTypeNormSq` (Flensted-Jensen's integral); the matrix coefficient `l.dsCoeff` is
  defined through it.

modules.title: Lower bounds for periods by Laplace's method
modules.group: Discrete series with a large gap
modules.note:
This file proves lower bounds for periods of discrete series coefficients. Let
`j : S →* U(ε) × U(η)` be a homomorphism and write `θ` for the function `laplaceIntegrand` on `S`.
Laplace's method bounds the volume of a large ball by a power of `β` times `‖∫ θ‖`, where `β` bounds
the dimensions and the entries of the parameters.

## Main definitions and results

* The values of `θ` lie in a cone about the positive real axis, up to an exponentially small error
  (`IsLaplaceDatum.norm_laplaceIntegrand_le_mul_re_add`). With the decay of the coefficients, `θ` is
  integrable and the volume of a large ball is at most a power of `β` times `‖∫ θ‖`
  (`IsLaplaceDatum.laplace_method`). The file `PositionGroup` applies this to the group of a
  stationary position.

Notions from other files:
* `USign ε` is the unitary group `U(ε)` of the diagonal form with signs `ε`, and
  `U.sum (signMatrix_sum ε η)` is the block embedding `(g, g') ↦ g ⊕ g'` of `U(ε) × U(η)`.
* `l.dsCoeff g` is the discrete series coefficient with doubled Harish-Chandra parameter
  `l = 2λ : HCParam ε`, given by Flensted-Jensen's integral and normalised to take the value `1`
  at the identity; `l.lowestKType` is the highest weight of its lowest `K`-type. On the maximal
  compact subgroup it is the coefficient at the highest weight vector of this `K`-type
  (`New.dsCoeff_of_mem_maxCompactU`).
* A parameter `l = 2λ` indexed by `n` has gap `A` if its entries are distinct and congruent to
  `card n - 1` mod 2, and `|λ a - λ b| ≥ A` whenever `ε a ≠ ε b`; `l.HasLargeGap h` says that `l`
  has gap `500 (card n)³ + h`.
* `l.laplaceIntegrand k j φ s` is the coefficient of `l` at the first component of `j s`, times the
  conjugate of the coefficient of `k` at the second, times `exp (-φ s)`.
* `IsLaplaceDatum l k j τ B e φ` collects the hypotheses of Laplace's method. Let `μ`, `μ'` be the
  weights `l.lowestKType`, `k.lowestKType` and let `j s = (g, g')`.
  - The parameter `l` is steep (`IsSteep`) for the splitting `e : X ⊕ Fin M ≃ n`: on `X` the sign is
    `+1` and `μ` is `0`; on the other `M` indices the signs are `+, -, +, …` and `μ` decreases
    strictly in `[-3 B, -B]`.
  - The weight `μ'` is nonnegative, at most `3 B` if `η` takes both signs, and `0` on the image of
    `τ : X → m`, where the sign is `+1`.
  - The phase `φ s = tr (μ (g - 1)) - tr (μ' (g' - 1))` is additive and imaginary, and
    `tr (g - 1) = tr (g' - 1)`.
  - For each unitary `u` indexed by `X` there is an `s` such that `g - 1` and `g' - 1` are `u - 1`
    extended by zero along `e` and along `τ`.
modules.literature:
This file is the step of Laplace's method that makes restriction periods explicitly large. Near 1 a
discrete series coefficient of U(p,q) is an explicit phase times a number close to the interval
[0,1], up to a tenth of its size and an exponentially small error, so that the losses at the
archimedean places are at most powers of the weights. The integral formula for coefficients,
non-vanishing of periods and fixed-rank asymptotics for coherent states are known in the literature.
Related work: Nelson–Venkatesh, The orbit method and analysis of automorphic forms, 2021; H. He, On
the Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for U(p,q), 2017; B. Sun, Matrix coefficients of cohomologically
induced representations, 2007.

modules.title: The group of a position
modules.group: Discrete series with a large gap
modules.note:
The elements `g` of `U(ε)` for which `g - 1` lowers the flag of a position form a closed subgroup
`R`. It maps to `U(η)` by the action `g'` on the image of `i₀` modulo `A_{≤ j₀ - 1}`, and it
carries an additive sum `σ`.

* The period over `R` in a stationary position is bounded below by Laplace's method
  (`IsStationary.integrable_periodIntegrand_and_measure_le`). The bound passes to a group that maps
  properly onto `R` (`IsStationary.period_lower_bound_of_surjective`).
* The pairing over `U(ε)` of a coefficient of `U(ε)` with a conjugated coefficient of `U(ε ⊕ 1)` is
  bounded below (`IsSteep.exists_volume_le_mul_norm_integral_dsCoeff`). This is the period in a
  stationary position with one vector `v₁`, where `R` is the stabilizer of `v₁` in `U(ε ⊕ 1)`, a
  conjugate of `U(ε)`.

Notions from other files:
* `USign ε` is the unitary group `U(ε)` of the diagonal matrix `signMatrix ε` of signs, and
  `formAdjoint ε η A` is the adjoint `A†` of `A : (ℂ^m, η) → (ℂ^n, ε)` for these forms.
* `IsPosition ε η d v i₀`: the columns `v₁, …, v_{j₀}` of `v`, `j₀ = d + 1`, are independent, their
  products vanish except that `v_{j₀}` has norm `±1`, `i₀` is an isometry into their orthogonal
  complement, and `card n = card m + 2 d + 1`.
* `LowersFlag d v Y σ`: `Y` maps the span `A_{≤ j}` of `v₁, …, v_j` into `A_{≤ j - 1}` for `j ≤ j₀`,
  and `σ` is the sum of the coefficients of `v_j` in `Y v_{j + 1}`.
* `InducesOn d v i₀ Y Y'`: `Y i₀ = i₀ Y'` modulo `A_{≤ j₀ - 1}`.
* `IsSteep l B e`: for `e : X ⊕ Fin M ≃ n`, the weight of the lowest `K`-type of `l` is `0` on `X`
  and decreases in `[-3 B, -B]` on the other coordinates, with alternating signs there.
* `IsLaplaceDatum` collects the hypotheses of Laplace's method on a map into `U(ε) × U(η)`.
